The commentator says: (yaghib, "'anhu" means: from Allah, may He be mighty and majestic; "mithqal" means: weight; "dharrah" means: the smallest ant, "fi al-samawati wa la fi al-ard wa la asghara min dhalika wa la akbara illa fi kitabin mubin" [Saba' 3]).

This saying "la ya'zubu 'anhu" to the end is a negative attribute, and "'alimi al-ghayb" is an affirmative attribute.

Affirmative attributes, as established, are all attributes of perfection, and negative attributes are an emphasis of perfection, because they include the affirmation of the perfection that is the opposite of that defect, and for this reason there is no negation in the attributes of Allah except that it implies the affirmation of its opposite, indeed the affirmation of the perfection of its opposite. Note this carefully: the negative attributes, meaning the negation, are an affirmation of perfection, because they include the affirmation of perfect attributes free from this attribute which is a defect.

For example, if we say, "Nothing escapes the knowledge of Allah," this is for the perfection of His knowledge. If we say that He, may He be mighty and majestic, created the heavens in six days and no weariness touched Him, this is for the perfection of His power. And measure accordingly.

So every negative attribute attributed to Allah, may He be mighty and majestic, is intended to affirm the perfection of the opposite, as if He is described with perfection free of this defect.

His saying "mithqal dharrah": the author says that it is the smallest ants (the smallest ant). The author informs us that among ants there are small and large ones, while in our custom it is otherwise. In our custom, the ant is a specific kind of dharr. Do you agree? We have the small dharr, and there is something they call "naml," which is the one somewhat larger than dharr and smaller than the "qa'r." I do not know whether you call the qa'r by this name or not. Do you call it by this name?

* A student: I do not know it.

* The Shaykh: What, you do not know it? Perhaps one day it will bite you and you will know it, God willing.

They say that this qa'r is among the most stubborn of things, and it is proverbial for stubbornness: you push it away and it returns, and then if it grabs your garment or your skin, it cannot be released; it is cut off and does not separate. Glory be to Allah! From its stubbornness, if it grips a garment, meaning it clamps onto it with its pincers or the skin, it does not move at all; if you try to remove it, it is cut.

Also among us it is called "al-qi's," but these are varieties of one genus in reality. All are called naml, all are dharr, and for this reason the Messenger's prohibition of killing ants, peace and blessings be upon him, includes all of them.

His saying: ("illa fi kitabin mubin" [Saba' 3], which is the Preserved Tablet). Is there knowledge in this?

"Wa la asghara min dhalika wa la akbara illa fi kitabin mubin." We say: it indicates the affirmation of knowledge, because there is no writing except after knowledge; the writing of the unknown is inconceivable. So there is a benefit beyond the affirmation of knowledge, namely that what is known to Allah, may He be mighty and majestic, is written in the Preserved Tablet. The rest of the discussion on this will come, God willing (...).

* A student: (...)?

* The Shaykh: No, this does not indicate that.

* The student: (...).

* The Shaykh: Something may ascend and not reach the heavens nor enter them; the soul of the disbeliever, for example, has the gates of heaven closed to it so it does not enter, though it ascends.

* A student: (...).

* The Shaykh: The occurrence that happens, for example.

* The student: If someone said: Paradise, and nothing in it has occurred, this is not specific to the knowledge of Allah, glorified and exalted.

* The Shaykh: No, not at all. We know Paradise in one respect and are ignorant of it in another respect.

* The student: We do not know its manner (...), we know that it is (...).

* The Shaykh: Yes, we know the names, not the named realities.

* The student: This too is from the knowledge of (...).

* The Shaykh: Yes, there is no doubt about it. This is known occurrence: we know that there is now a Paradise, and a Fire, and in them what has been mentioned of bliss or punishment.

* The student: But we do not know their manner and how...

* The Shaykh: Correct, because we have not experienced them. Now, if someone informed you of an event occurring in your country, or even in your house where you are now, you know its meaning, but you do not know its reality as it is unless you witness it.

* * *

* A student: In the name of Allah, and praise be to Allah, and blessings and peace be upon the Messenger of Allah.

Third: clarifying the false consequences that follow from their negation, for the corruption of the consequence indicates the corruption of what entails it.

Fourth: that the texts concerning the attributes do not admit of interpretation, and if some of them admit of it, there is nothing that prevents the apparent meaning from being intended, so it is necessary to resort to it.

Fifth: that the claim of this (...).

* The Shaykh: "And those who disbelieve say, 'The Hour will not come upon us,'" where is the object of the saying in the saying (...).

Also, before taking the benefits, Allah commanded His Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, to swear here that the Hour will come upon them. Is there a parallel to it in the Quran?

* A student: Yes, "They ask you, 'Is it true?'" [Yunus 53].

* The Shaykh: No, the oath on this same meaning.

* A student: "Those who disbelieved claim that they will never be resurrected. Say, 'Yes, by my Lord, you will surely be resurrected.'"

* The Shaykh: "Then you will be informed of what you did, and that is easy for Allah" [al-Taghabun 7]. There is a third place too in which Allah commanded His Prophet to swear by it.

* A student: "I swear by the Day of Resurrection" [al-Qiyamah 1].

* The Shaykh: No, Allah commanded His Prophet to swear.

* A student: "They ask you, 'Is it true?' Say, 'Yes, by my Lord, it is indeed true.'" [Yunus 53].

* The Shaykh: "Say, 'Yes, by my Lord, it is indeed true.'"

* From the benefits of this noble verse: the denial of the disbelievers of the resurrection, by their saying, "The Hour will not come upon us."

* And from its benefits: that denying the resurrection is disbelief, by His saying, "And those who disbelieved said." If you say: what is the basis of this inference? The answer: the basis is that if this attribute had no effect, Allah would not have stated it with this attribute; He would have said, "And they said, 'The Hour will not come upon us.'" Since He said, "And those who disbelieved said," it is known that this saying is not uttered except by whom? By a disbeliever. "And those who disbelieved said."

* And from the benefits of the noble verse: the magnification of the matter of the Hour, by Allah commanding His Prophet Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, to swear that it will occur: "Say, 'Yes, by my Lord, it will surely come upon you.'"

* And from the benefits of the noble verse: the perfection of Allah's mercy toward His servants, in that He informed them of the resurrection and emphasized it with verbal, meaningful and even sensory emphatics; for faith in the resurrection is what moves a person to carry out the obedience of Allah, since if there were no resurrection, a person would never work for the Hereafter.

So we say: this is evidence of Allah's mercy toward the servants, that He affirms for them the resurrection in which recompense for deeds takes place, so that they may act for this day.

* And from the benefits of the noble verse: that the Hour is entrusted to the knowledge of Allah, by His saying, "The Knower of the Unseen"; so it is one of the unseen reports of Allah, glorified and exalted, which none knows except Allah.

The verses and hadiths on this meaning are also numerous. Whoever claims knowledge of the Hour is a disbeliever, because he contradicts the Quran, the Sunnah, and the consensus of the Muslims.

* And from the benefits of the noble verse: the comprehensiveness of Allah's knowledge over everything, by His saying, "Nothing escapes Him of the weight of an atom in the heavens or on the earth, nor anything smaller than that or greater."

* And from it: the affirmation of the heavens, and that they are plural. From where is this taken? (...). Yes, from His saying "fi al-samawat" and its plural form, so it contains the affirmation of the heavens and that they are plural.

Is the earth like the heavens?

The answer: Yes, as other texts besides this verse indicate.

* And from its benefits: that there is something smaller than the atom, by His saying, "wa la asghara min dhalika," which is what exists. Among the creatures of Allah, may He be mighty and majestic, are things you can hardly see with your eye, things you cannot see except with a microscope. And yet, when you see this thing, glory be to the Mighty, in a microscope that magnifies it a million times, you find that all its needs exist: hands, feet, eyes, everything, even the down on its back for its protection. This is evidence of the perfection of Allah's power, glorified and exalted, and that He is Subtle and All-Aware, glorified be He.

* And also among its benefits: the affirmation of the Preserved Tablet, by His saying, "kitab."

* Among its benefits: this Preserved Tablet (al-lawh al-mahfuz) has written in it the decrees of everything, small and great, because of His words: ﴿Nor is there anything smaller than that or greater, but it is in a clear Record.﴾

* Also among its benefits: this Book is clear (mubin), meaning it explains everything in detail, as Allah, Blessed and Exalted, said: ﴿We have not neglected anything in the Book, then unto their Lord they will be gathered.﴾ [al-An'am 38]. In this Preserved Tablet is everything that will occur until the Day of Resurrection, as the Sunnah has come to clarify this.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the permissibility of swearing an oath (qasam), and indeed its obligation when need calls for it. From where is this derived? From Allah's command to His Prophet to swear, to what? To the establishment of the Hour: ﴿Say: Yes, by my Lord, it will surely come upon you.﴾

Accordingly, we find that some of the Imams, may Allah have mercy on them, when they mention the ruling on some issue, sometimes swear to it. This is found in the speech of Imam Ahmad, and perhaps in the speech of others, though we have not come across it. He is sometimes asked: "Do you say such-and-such?" and he replies: "Yes, by Allah," swearing to the matter in order to affirm and confirm it, and to convey his certainty about it to the one addressing him.

On this basis, it is permissible for the mufti to swear to a ruling when need calls for that, and indeed it may be obligatory according to what the situation requires.

As for His words: ﴿Say: Yes, by my Lord, it will surely come upon you.﴾ Can it be derived from this noble verse that the address specific to the Messenger ﷺ also includes the Ummah? There is no clear indication of this in it. But we have previously mentioned that the address directed to the Messenger ﷺ is divided into:

* Student: (...).
* The Shaykh: No, into three categories. A category in which there is clear indication that what is meant is the Ummah along with the Messenger ﷺ.
The second category: clear indication that it is specific to the Messenger ﷺ.
The third category: that which has neither indication nor qarinah (contextual evidence). This is a matter of difference among the scholars: does this address directed to the Messenger, peace be upon him, include the Ummah by virtue of the wording (ṣīghah), or does it include the Ummah by virtue of emulation (uswah)?

An example of what has indication that it is specific to the Messenger, peace be upon him, is: ﴿Did We not expand for you your breast? And We removed from you your burden﴾ [al-Sharh 1, 2]. This is undoubtedly specific to the Messenger, peace be upon him.

An example of what evidence has established as general is His words, Exalted is He: ﴿O Prophet, when you divorce women...﴾ [al-Talaq 1]. In His words "when you divorce" there is clear indication that the address to the Messenger ﷺ also intends the Ummah. Other examples are numerous.

So does the ruling in the address include the Ummah by virtue of the wording or by virtue of emulation? Some of them say: it includes the Ummah by virtue of the wording, but it was directed to the Messenger, peace be upon him, because he is their leader (imam). The analogy is that you say to the commander of an army: "Go to such-and-such front," and what is meant is: go and those with you, those who follow you of the soldiers.

Others say: it is specific to the Messenger, peace be upon him, and does not include the Ummah, but the Ummah is commanded to emulate him: ﴿Indeed, in the Messenger of Allah you have an excellent example for whoever hopes in Allah and the Last Day and remembers Allah often.﴾ [al-Ahzab 21].

The disagreement on this is close to a matter of wording, since there is agreement that this ruling includes the Ummah.

So if we hear a person denying the Hour, are we permitted to swear? Or are we commanded to swear to its occurrence? Yes, we are commanded to swear to its occurrence.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the emphasis of a ruling according to what the situation requires, or, to put it more accurately, the emphasis of a statement (khabar) according to what the situation requires. The rhetoricians have mentioned that a statement is divided into three categories:
Either it is addressed to one whose mind is empty (khali al-dhihn), or to one who is hesitant (mutaraddid), or to one who denies (munkir). If it is addressed to one with an empty mind, there is no need to emphasize it, and it cannot be emphasized according to the rules of rhetoric except for a specific purpose. If it is addressed to a hesitant person, emphasis is good, to remove his hesitation and doubt. If it is addressed to a denier, emphasis is obligatory.

The first is ibtida'i (initial), the second is talabi (responsive), and the third is inkari (denial). This was covered for us in rhetoric (balaghah).

This matter: the emphasis of this statement, ﴿Say: Yes, by my Lord, it will surely come upon you.﴾ Which of the three categories is it: denial, responsive, or initial? It is denial, because it is addressed to a people who deny, so its emphasis is obligatory.

We mentioned during the explanation an objection: if these people are deniers, there is no benefit in swearing to them, because the one who denies a statement, whether you swear or not, does not believe you. We answered this.

* Student: With two answers. We said: the first is that it is a style of the Arabs: when they are denied, they swear, meaning it shows the sincerity of this person's belief, that he is certain of what is transmitted from the Shaykh, so he swears.

* The Shaykh: Just as he is certain of the existence of the one sworn by.

* Student: His words in the explanation: (good in Paradise).

* The Shaykh: Yes indeed, ﴿That He may reward those who believed﴾ [Saba' 4]. Shall we explain this now? We have not explained it.

* Student: Shaykh, Allah, glorified and exalted, says: ﴿And do not make Allah an obstacle for your oaths﴾ [al-Baqarah 224].

* The Shaykh: Yes, ﴿do not make Allah an obstacle for your oaths﴾, complete the verse.

* The student: ﴿That you be righteous and fear Allah and make peace among the people. And Allah is Hearing and Knowing.﴾

* The Shaykh: The most correct of what has been said about it: the meaning is, do not make the oath a barrier preventing you from doing righteousness, piety, and reconciliation between people. Do not make it an obstacle in such and such matters. This is the most correct of what has been said about it.

In addition, there is His saying: ﴿That He may reward those who believed and did righteous deeds. For those are forgiveness and a generous provision﴾ [Saba' 4]. Where does this verse fit in meaning with what comes before it? Or, the lam in His saying ﴿That He may reward﴾ is connected to what? Who? Did we not explain it?

* Students: No, teacher, the earlier part, which is (clarifies that it is the Preserved Tablet).

* The Shaykh: Allah the Exalted says: ﴿That He may reward those who believed and did righteous deeds﴾. He said: (﴿That He may reward﴾ in it), (in it) the pronoun refers to the Hour.

﴿That He may reward﴾: the lam here indicates purpose (ta'lil). We know from the rules of the Arabic language that prepositions must have something they relate to (muta'allaq). So where is the object of this lam? The object of this lam is His saying ﴿will surely come to you﴾. That is: it will surely come to you so that He may reward those who... So this lam is for purpose, and it is connected to His saying ﴿will surely come to you﴾.

And ﴿yajziya﴾ means: to recompense or to reward. The subject is Allah, glorified and exalted.

As for his saying (in it), the author, by his saying (in it), indicates that the prepositional phrase is connected to (will come to you), because the pronoun in his saying (in it) refers to the Hour: (﴿That He may reward﴾ in it).

﴿Those who believed and did righteous deeds﴾: they believed in the heart, and did righteous deeds with the limbs. When faith is mentioned alone, it includes outward actions, the actions of the limbs. Likewise, when action is mentioned alone, it includes faith in the heart, because faith in the heart is one of the deeds of the hearts. So when both are mentioned together, faith is in the heart and action is in the limbs. Faith is secret and action is open.

As for His saying ﴿believed﴾: faith (iman) linguistically means assent (tasdiq). In the sharia, it means assent that necessitates acceptance and submission (idhan). It is not mere assent; rather, it is assent that necessitates acceptance and submission. Acceptance applies to reports, and submission applies to commands. So, for example, a person accepts what Allah and His Messenger have informed, and accepts that this ruling is obligatory, or that it is voluntary, and similar things, and submits to that, meaning he worships Allah in accordance with what he believes and in accordance with what Allah has legislated, glorified and exalted is He.

In His saying ﴿those who believed and did righteous deeds﴾, ﴿did righteous deeds﴾ means: they did righteous actions. So ﴿righteous﴾ is an adjective for an omitted noun.

Omitting the described noun is permissible when there is an indication of it. Ibn Malik said:

"What is understood of the described noun and the adjective may be omitted, and in the adjective it is rare."

From the omission of the described noun is His saying: ﴿Do work, making coats of mail that are full length﴾ [Saba' 11], meaning: coats of mail that are full length.

So on this basis, ﴿righteous﴾ is an adjective for an omitted noun, meaning: the righteous deeds. And what are the righteous deeds? A righteous deed is one that combines two matters:

Sincerity to Allah, glorified and exalted, and following the Messenger ﷺ. If the first is missing, it is not righteous, and it is rejected from the doer. If the second is missing, it is also not righteous, and it is rejected from the doer.

The evidence: for the first, Allah said in a hadith qudsi: "I am the most self-sufficient of partners from association. Whoever does a deed in which he associates another with Me, I abandon him and his association." [Recorded by Muslim (2985/46) from the hadith of Abu Hurayra.]

For the second, the Prophet ﷺ said: "Whoever does a deed that is not in accordance with our affair, it is rejected," or "Whoever introduces into this affair of ours something that is not part of it, it is rejected." [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (2697) and Muslim (1718/18), from the hadith of Aisha.]

So it is not possible for a deed to be righteous except with these two conditions: sincerity, and following the Messenger ﷺ.

If a man introduces an innovation (bid'a) of the innovations, practicing it as a form of worship to Allah, glorified and exalted, and he finds in his heart tranquility in it, humility and weeping, yet it is an innovation in the religion of Allah, would it be a righteous deed? It would not be, even if the deed is made attractive to a person and he finds peace in it. It is not a righteous deed, so it is not accepted and not beneficial. Rather, the person sins by it, because it is drawing near to Allah by what He dislikes, and drawing near to Allah by what He dislikes is a kind of mockery of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

Consider: if you went to a person, a king among kings, and you presented to him a flask containing something you want to take to the analysis, would you be honoring him or not? Answer.

* Students: No.

* The Shaykh: No, because he dislikes this thing. How would you say: I present to him perfume, a jar of perfume? There is no harm in that. But if you present him with this thing and say: I draw near to him by it, this is the opposite of what you intend, and it is a kind of mockery of this honored or revered person.

So then, what are the righteous deeds? The righteous deeds are those that combine two conditions: sincerity to Allah, glorified and exalted, and following the Messenger ﷺ.

Some actions are disliked in the sharia, yet a person feels at ease and comfortable with them. So we say: do not be deceived by this comfort and this tranquility, for that is from the adornment of what? From the adornment of Satan. The worshippers of idols, who made them intercessors for them with Allah, feel comfortable with this, and see them as intermediaries between them and Allah, glorified and exalted. Yet these are still shirk.

An example of this: some people close their eyes during prayer and say that this is more conducive to humility. This is from the adornment of Satan, because closing the eyes in prayer without a reason is disliked and contrary to the guidance of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him. The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, did not close his eyes. Rather, he would look at the place of his prostration or straight ahead. As for closing the eyes, this is contrary to the Sunna, and therefore the jurists disliked it, may Allah have mercy on them. Yes, if there is a reason for closing the eyes, such as if something in front of you dazzles your eyes or designs distract you, then closing them here is for a reason, not to draw near to Allah through it, but to avert what confuses you and disturbs...

His saying: ﴿Knower of the unseen﴾ [Saba' 3] (...).

﴿That He may reward those who believed and did righteous deeds, for those are forgiveness﴾ [Saba' 4]. His saying: ﴿for those are forgiveness and a generous provision﴾: this sentence is a resumptive clause (isti'naf) to explain their reward, because His saying ﴿That He may reward those who believed and did righteous deeds﴾ is ambiguous, so He clarified this reward by His saying ﴿for those are forgiveness and a generous provision﴾.

The demonstrative in His saying ﴿those﴾ refers to ﴿those who believed and did righteous deeds﴾. It is the subject (mubtada'), ﴿for them﴾ is a fronted predicate (khabar muqaddam), ﴿forgiveness﴾ is a delayed subject (mubtada' mu'akhkhar), and ﴿and a generous provision﴾ is conjoined to it. The second clause, consisting of the subject and predicate, is the predicate of the first subject.

So we now have two subjects: ﴿those﴾ and ﴿forgiveness﴾, correct?

﴿Those﴾ is a subject. ﴿For them﴾ is a prepositional phrase serving as a fronted predicate for what? For ﴿forgiveness﴾. ﴿Forgiveness﴾ is a delayed subject, and ﴿a generous provision﴾ is conjoined to it. The clause made of the second subject and its predicate is in the place of a nominative predicate of the first subject. Is this understood by you?

Where is the connecting element? The connecting element is the pronoun in ﴿for them﴾, because it refers to the one indicated.

His saying: ﴿those for them are forgiveness﴾. ﴿Those﴾ is used with a demonstrative for the distant, to alert to the elevation of their rank, because this category of people is the highest class of people: ﴿those who believed and did righteous deeds﴾.

His saying: ﴿forgiveness﴾: with it, the disliked thing is removed. ﴿And a generous provision﴾: with it, the desired thing is attained. So for them is forgiveness for their sins and wrongdoings, so Allah forgives them their wrongdoings and sins by overlooking them and covering them over for them, because forgiveness is the covering of the sin and overlooking of it. Its derivation is from the mighfar, which is the helmet worn on the head in war, and it has two benefits: covering the head and protecting it from arrows. So forgiveness includes covering sins, overlooking them, and not punishing for them.

﴿And a generous provision﴾: provision means bounty. From it is His saying: ﴿And when the division takes place and the relatives, orphans and needy are present, provide for them from it﴾ [al-Nisa' 8], meaning: give them.

And generous means good in its quality and in its quantity. Allah, the Exalted, has indicated that the goodness of this provision cannot be reached by minds in His saying: ﴿No soul knows what is hidden for them of comfort for eyes as reward for what they used to do﴾ [al-Sajda 17]. So the reward of these believers who did righteous deeds is that their evil deeds are forgiven and that they are recompensed for their righteous deeds with a generous provision.

I say: ﴿generous﴾ means it is good in what? In its quantity and its quality. Its quantity cannot be counted, it does not perish or come to an end, and its quality is also beyond what the mind or heart can grasp: ﴿No soul knows what is hidden for them of comfort for eyes as reward for what they used to do﴾.

Then He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿And those who strive against Our verses, seeking to cause failure﴾, to the end [Saba' 5]. We discussed previously and said that the Qur'an is mathani, as Allah described it: ﴿Allah has sent down the best statement, a Book consistent and repeating﴾ [al-Zumar 23]. And this mathani is different from the mathani in His saying: ﴿And We have certainly given you seven of the mathani and the great Qur'an﴾ [al-Hijr 87], because what is meant by ﴿seven of the mathani﴾ is al-Fatiha, as was established from the Prophet ﷺ. So the mathani in ﴿a Book consistent and repeating﴾ means that meanings are repeated in it. Often, when the reward of the righteous is mentioned, the reward of the disbelievers is mentioned. When the description of Paradise is mentioned, the description of the Fire is mentioned. When the attributes beloved to Allah are mentioned, the attributes hated by Him are mentioned. Why? Because if only the desired attributes or rewards were mentioned, a person would be overtaken by hope until he feels safe from Allah's plan. And if the disliked matters were mentioned alone, despair and hopelessness would overtake him. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, mentions this and then mentions alongside it the other thing, so that the person travels to his Lord between what? Between fear and hope. For this is moderation: that you be fearful and hopeful as you journey to your Lord. For if you overwhelm hope, you become of those who feel secure from Allah's plan, because whoever overwhelms hope begins to commit sins and says: I hope Allah will forgive me, and neglects obligations and says: I hope Allah will forgive me. And whoever overwhelms fear enters into despair of Allah's mercy.

We mentioned that some scholars differed in this and said: when performing an act of obedience, you should give precedence to hope, because you have done what you were commanded, so hope for Allah's reward, since this is part of having good opinion of Allah. And when you are in a state of disobedience, give precedence to fear, so that you restrain yourself from what you want to do of disobedience.

And some scholars took another position and said: in the state of illness, give precedence to hope, because you are now in a state of weakness, so favor hope and good opinion of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, so that you do not die except while having good opinion of your Lord, glorified and exalted. And when you are in good health, give precedence to fear.

Imam Ahmad, may Allah have mercy on him, said: his fear and his hope should be equal. Whichever of them prevails, its companion is destroyed.

In reality, a person is the physician of his own soul. There is no doubt that if you see your soul inclining toward falsehood, you must instill fear of Allah in it, and not hope, because if you give it hope in this state, what does it do? It goes ahead with sins. Yes indeed.

He says: ﴿And those who strive against Our verses, seeking to cause failure, for them is a painful punishment of a grievous kind﴾.

﴿Strove against Our verses﴾: the author said: (in nullifying ﴿Our verses﴾, the Qur'an). So he posited in the verse an omitted element, its estimate being: in nullifying them.

The meaning of ﴿strove﴾ is: they walked vigorously. This is the original sense, and from it comes sa'y, meaning running. So what is meant is that these people race and hasten to nullify the verses of Allah, glorified and exalted. Nullifying them, as far as they are concerned, means they do not act upon them. Nullifying them, as far as others are concerned, means they turn people away from the religion of Allah. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve and avert [people] from the way of Allah and the Sacred Mosque﴾ [al-Hajj 25]. So these people strove with utmost effort against the verses of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, to nullify them and defeat them.

His saying: ﴿strove against Our verses﴾ does not specify with what they strove, because these people strive to nullify the verses of Allah at times through armed conflict, meaning they attack lands and fight them until they turn them back from their religion. At times through intellectual weapons, so they spread doubts among them about their religion, their Prophet, and their Lord, as much as they are able. And at times they strive through desires, so they spread among people love of amusement and lust. Among this is what the corrupt media spreads in disbelieving states and those who imitate them. You find them calling to the lowest of morals, calling by pen and by image. They photograph alluring women in a shameful state, may Allah protect us, and they also write calling to that. Do you think this matter affects belief, or only the body?

* Students: (...).

* The Shaykh: It affects belief in reality, because when a person becomes bestial, having no concern except filling his belly and satisfying his instincts, he remains without any connection to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and has no connection. The most important thing to him is what he has immersed himself in of desires and pleasures. So you find him turning away from the religion of Allah and not caring about it. For this reason, after the spreading of intellectual poison, among the most harmful things to Muslim lands is the spreading of lustful poison, because lust is something a person inclines toward by his nature, which the commanding soul to evil dictates to him, so he enters into it unwillingly. If he becomes immersed in it, may we ask Allah for well-being, it is unlikely that he will extricate himself from it.

So the point is that those who disbelieve strive with intense effort to nullify the signs of Allah, that they not be spread, or acted upon, or that people turn toward them with all the strength they have: either through armed conflict, or through spreading doubting and confusing ideas, or through spreading what? Desires, so that people turn away from their religion.

His saying: ﴿Our verses﴾: he said: (the Qur'an). The correct view is that ﴿Our verses﴾ here is more general than the Qur'an, because those who strive against the verses of Allah are not only from this nation. Even among previous nations there were those who strove against the verses of Allah. Is that not so?!

For example, Pharaoh threatened his people, saying: ﴿I know of no god for you other than me﴾ [al-Qasas 38], and urged them to disbelieve in Musa, peace be upon him, and other nations as well. All of them strove against the verses of Allah, meaning they sought to nullify them and turn people away from them.

On this basis, we say: the meaning of the verses of Allah here is more general than the Qur'an, including anyone who strives against any verse of the verses of Allah.

His saying: (﴿Mu'ajjizin﴾ [the shaykh read it ﴿mu'jizin﴾ from i'jaz, and the correct reading is from (ta'jiz), as we have established] and in one reading here and in what follows, ﴿mu'ajizin﴾, meaning: estimating our inability, or racing against us so that they escape us, due to their thinking that there is no resurrection and no punishment).

Yes, there are two reading-traditions that are canonical, or one of them is irregular?

* Students: Two canonical readings.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 34, verse 4–6 (part 2 of 4):

* The Shaykh: Two readings, is that right? Because it is the terminology of the author, may Allah have mercy on him, that when he says "wa-fi qira'a" (and in one reading), it is a canonical (sab'iyyah) reading, but when he says "wa-quri'a" (and it was read), it is an irregular (shadhdhah) reading. This is a specific terminology of the author. If you find in this book, this tafsir, "wa-fi qira'a," know that it is a canonical reading; and if you find "wa-quri'a," it is an irregular reading. The difference between them is that a canonical reading may be recited by a person in his prayer and worship Allah, the Exalted, with it, whereas an irregular reading remains irregular by its name. But is it used as evidence for rulings or not? On this there is a difference of opinion among the scholars.
So there are two readings: ﴿مُعَجِّزِينَ﴾ or ﴿مُعَاجِزِينَ﴾. The mu'ajjiz (one who causes to fail) is one who wants to make another incapable without there being any opposition from the other party. This is the mu'ajjiz, so the incapacitating is from one side only; that is, they want by this to make Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, incapable of seizing and punishing them, because they feel secure from the plotting of Allah, the Exalted.
﴿مُعَاجِزِينَ﴾ involves two parties, each of whom wants to incapacitate the other. It is as if, through their tyranny and transgression, they placed themselves in a position of conflict with Allah, the Mighty and Majestic; although Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, wants to incapacitate them, they too want to incapacitate Allah, the Exalted.
It has already been mentioned that each of the two readings may indicate a meaning that completes the other reading. Which of them is more eloquent: al-mu'ajjiz or al-mu'aajiz?
* Students: Al-mu'aajiz.
* The Shaykh: Al-mu'aajiz is more eloquent in expressing tyranny, because it means he wanted to make himself a combatant against Allah, the Exalted, opposing Him.
What is their recompense? He says: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ سَعَوْا فِي آيَاتِنَا مُعَاجِزِينَ أُولَئِكَ لَهُمْ عَذَابٌ مِنْ رِجْزٍ أَلِيمٌ﴾. He says: ﴿أُولَئِكَ لَهُمْ عَذَابٌ﴾. We say regarding its grammatical analysis what we said regarding His saying ﴿أُولَئِكَ لَهُمْ مَغْفِرَةٌ﴾: it is a mubtada' (subject) and its predicate is the clause following it.
﴿لَهُمْ عَذَابٌ مِنْ رِجْزٍ أَلِيمٌ﴾. "Adhab" means punishment, and the author says that "rijz" means "evil torment" (سيِّئ العَذَاب). Rijz is the evil of everything. So when it is said ﴿عَذَابٌ مِنْ رِجْزٍ﴾, its meaning is evil torment. Their torment is, we seek Allah's refuge, evil torment; indeed it is the worst torment, for the greatest torment with which mankind is punished is the torment of the Fire. We ask Allah for well-being. So it is the worst of torments.
As for His saying ﴿أَلِيمٌ﴾, meaning "painful," with the genitive and nominative (مؤلِم، بالجرِّ والرفْع): there are two readings, (an adjective of ﴿رِجْزٍ﴾ or of ﴿عَذَابٌ﴾). That is, the word ﴿أَلِيمٌ﴾ has two readings: ﴿أُولَئِكَ لَهُمْ عَذَابٌ مِنْ رِجْزٍ أَلِيمٌ﴾ or ﴿عَذَابٌ مِنْ رِجْزٍ أَلِيمٍ﴾. As for ﴿أَلِيمٌ﴾ being an adjective of ﴿عَذَابٌ﴾, this is frequent in the Qur'an: ﴿وَلَهُمْ عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌ﴾ [al-Baqarah 10]; Allah often describes the torment as painful. As for ﴿رِجْزٍ﴾, it was an adjective of it because it is closer than ﴿عَذَابٌ﴾.
Accordingly, if you say ﴿أُولَئِكَ لَهُمْ عَذَابٌ مِنْ رِجْزٍ أَلِيمٌ﴾, we say it is an adjective of ﴿عَذَابٌ﴾; and if you say ﴿أُولَئِكَ لَهُمْ عَذَابٌ مِنْ رِجْزٍ أَلِيمٍ﴾, we say it is an adjective of ﴿رِجْزٍ﴾. It is permissible to recite with this and with that; rather, it is recommended that you recite with both readings, and with all three if there are three readings, because the variation of readings is like the variation of attributes in acts of worship. We have already noted that what comes in acts of worship with multiple forms, it is better to practise this at one time and that at another, so that you obtain all the Sunnahs; likewise with readings. But beware of reciting while in doubt about the reading, because it is not permissible for us to recite except while certain that this is a correct reading.
Then He, the Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿وَيَرَى الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الْعِلْمَ الَّذِي أُنْزِلَ إِلَيْكَ مِنْ رَبِّكَ هُوَ الْحَقَّ﴾ [Saba' 6].
﴿يَرَى﴾ means "knows," because seeing may mean seeing with the eye, and seeing may be with the heart, and seeing with the heart is knowing. "Ra'a" in the sense of "knew" occurs frequently in the Qur'an, such as His saying: ﴿إِنَّهُمْ يَرَوْنَهُ بَعِيدًا (٦) وَنَرَاهُ قَرِيبًا﴾ [al-Ma'arij 6, 7]. ﴿نَرَاهُ﴾ means "we know it," because the meaning is not "we see it with our eyes," since it has not occurred, and the meaning is not "we suppose," because Allah is exalted above supposition. On this basis, ﴿نَرَاهُ﴾ means "we know it."
Here ﴿يَرَى الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الْعِلْمَ﴾ means "knows." But when "yara" comes in the sense of "knows," it indicates that the knowledge is at the highest level of knowledge, and that it has become like what is witnessed by the eye, seen with a complete seeing like that which is witnessed.
His saying ﴿الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الْعِلْمَ﴾ means "those who were given it." Do the words refer to the People of the Book, or are they general?
The author says: (﴿الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الْعِلْمَ﴾ are the believers among the People of the Book, such as 'Abdullah ibn Salam and his companions). The correct view is that it is more general than that, and that what is meant by ﴿الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الْعِلْمَ﴾ is everyone whom Allah, the Exalted, has given knowledge, including the People of the Book, Jews and Christians. The Negus, may Allah have mercy on him, was among the Christians, and saw that what was sent down to the Prophet ﷺ is true; and 'Abdullah ibn Salam, one of the rabbis of the Jews, saw that what was sent down to the Prophet ﷺ is the truth. Likewise, whoever Allah has given knowledge from this Ummah also sees that what was sent down to the Prophet ﷺ is the truth, unlike one who is ignorant, whose faith is faith by imitation; although that suffices for him, it is not like the faith of one whom Allah has given knowledge.
Evidence that what is meant by ﴿الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الْعِلْمَ﴾ is more general is the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿شَهِدَ اللَّهُ أَنَّهُ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا هُوَ وَالْمَلَائِكَةُ وَأُولُو الْعِلْمِ﴾ [Al 'Imran 18]. Those who were given knowledge are those who see that what was sent down to the Prophet ﷺ is the truth, by means of the firmly established knowledge that Allah has given them in their hearts. For this reason, you find that the worship of the layman who worships Allah, the Exalted, is closest to being a habit, even if he feels in his heart turning to Allah, humility and recollection; but he is not like one who worships Allah, the Exalted, with insight and knowledge, because in the heart of the latter there is certainty that is not in the heart of the former. So it is general.
﴿يَرَى الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الْعِلْمَ الَّذِي أُنْزِلَ إِلَيْكَ مِنْ رَبِّكَ هُوَ الْحَقَّ﴾. If "yara" is a verb of knowledge, it takes two objects. Where is the first object?
* Students: ﴿الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الْعِلْمَ﴾.
* The Shaykh: No.
* Students: ﴿الَّذِي﴾.
* The Shaykh: ﴿الَّذِي﴾. Where is the "alladhi"? ﴿الَّذِي أُنْزِلَ﴾ is a relative pronoun, and ﴿هُوَ الْحَقَّ﴾ — ﴿الْحَقَّ﴾ is the second object. Clear? As for the first ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾, it is the subject (fa'il).
Now, His saying ﴿الَّذِي أُنْزِلَ إِلَيْكَ مِنْ رَبِّكَ﴾ means the Qur'an; Allah sent it down to the Prophet ﷺ through Jibril.
His saying ﴿مِنْ رَبِّكَ﴾: here He attributed the lordship to the Prophet ﷺ, because revelation is a special lordship, for no one from this Ummah shares the Prophet ﷺ in it. Therefore He attributed the lordship to him alone, saying ﴿الَّذِي أُنْزِلَ إِلَيْكَ مِنْ رَبِّكَ﴾, for the sake of honouring both the one to whom it was sent down and what was sent down.
His saying ﴿مِنْ رَبِّكَ﴾: it has already been mentioned that the meaning of lordship (rubbubiyyah) is creation, dominion and management. Allah, the Exalted, is the Creator of the Prophet ﷺ, his Owner, and his Manager.
The author said: (i.e., the Qur'an, ﴿هُوَ﴾ is a separator (fasl), ﴿الْحَقَّ﴾). ﴿الْحَقَّ﴾ is the second object, and ﴿هُوَ﴾ is a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl). Its form is that of a pronoun but it is not a pronoun; therefore we do not say it is a noun, nor do we say it has a place in i'rab; that is, it has no place in i'rab and is not a noun, but it is brought for separation.
The evidence that it has no place in i'rab is the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿لَعَلَّنَا نَتَّبِعُ السَّحَرَةَ إِنْ كَانُوا هُمُ﴾ [al-Shu'ara' 40] ﴿الْغَالِبِينَ﴾, or "al-ghalibun"?
* Students: ﴿الْغَالِبِينَ﴾.
* The Shaykh: ﴿الْغَالِبِينَ﴾. Had it had a place in i'rab, it would have said "hum al-ghalibun." Since He said ﴿هُمُ الْغَالِبِينَ﴾ and ﴿الْغَالِبِينَ﴾ became the predicate of "kana," this shows that this pronoun has no place in i'rab. But what is its benefit?
The scholars mentioned that it has three benefits. The first benefit?
* A student: Separating the adjective from the predicate.
* The Shaykh: Separating the adjective from the predicate. The second benefit?
* The student: Restriction (ḥaṣr).
* The Shaykh: Restriction. The third benefit?
* The student: Emphasis (tawkid).
* The Shaykh: Emphasis. So it gives three benefits: restriction, emphasis, and separating the predicate from the adjective. Right? Give an example to explain this to us.
* The student: (...).
* The Shaykh: (Zaydun al-fadil). The word "al-fadil" here may also be an adjective of "Zayd" with the predicate not yet having come, so the listener is now awaiting the predicate, as if its estimate were: "Zayd the virtuous is present." Or not?
* The students: Yes indeed.
* The Shaykh: If you say, "Zaydun al-fadilu hadirun" (Zayd the virtuous is present), then "al-fadilu" is without doubt an adjective and "hadirun" is the predicate. But if you say, "Zaydun al-fadilu," only, it may be that you want to inform that Zayd is virtuous, and it may be that you want to describe Zayd as virtuous while the predicate has not come. Is that not so? If you say, "Zaydun huwa al-fadilu" (Zayd is the virtuous one), then "al-fadil" is now definitely the predicate, is it not? Good, this is the aspect of it separating the adjective from the predicate.
Good, is it also emphatic?
* Students: Yes.
* The Shaykh: It is emphatic, because when you say "Zaydun al-fadilu" and "Zaydun huwa al-fadilu," the second is without doubt more emphatic.
Likewise it is useful for restriction, because when you say "Zaydun huwa al-fadil," it means: not anyone else.
So the separating pronoun gives three benefits: restriction, emphasis, and separating the predicate from the adjective.
He, the Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿هُوَ الْحَقَّ﴾. ﴿الْحَقَّ﴾ means a established thing; this is the truth. Your saying "uhiqqu al-shay'" means "I establish the thing"; ﴿حَقَّتْ عَلَيْهِمْ كَلِمَتُ رَبِّكَ﴾ [Yunus 96] means they were established and became obligatory.
What is established in the Qur'an? Truthfulness in reports, and justice in rulings. So when al-haqq is attributed to a ruling, its meaning is justice: it is a just ruling. For this reason, if two litigants dispute before a judge and he rules for one of them in accordance with what the Sharia requires, we say: this is true, because he was just; and if he rules for the other contrary to it, we say: this is not true, this is false, because he ruled other than the truth. So truth in rulings is what? Justice; and in reports, truthfulness. Those whom Allah has given knowledge know that this Qur'an is true in its rulings and true in its reports. Its rulings are all justice, for they place things in their proper place and give the right to its rightful owners; and its reports too are what? Established and true; that is, they are firm and contain no lie. So the truth (...).
So when you say, "This report is true," meaning truthful; "this ruling is true," meaning just. For this reason Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿وَتَمَّتْ كَلِمَتُ رَبِّكَ صِدْقًا وَعَدْلًا﴾ [al-An'am 115]. The scholars said: ﴿صِدْقًا﴾ concerns reports, and ﴿عَدْلًا﴾ concerns rulings.
﴿هُوَ الْحَقَّ﴾. Together with that, (﴿وَيَهْدِي إِلَى صِرَاطِ﴾, the path of ﴿الْعَزِيزِ الْحَمِيدِ﴾, meaning Allah, the Mighty, the Praiseworthy), ﴿يَهْدِي﴾ means "guides/indicates," so guidance here is guidance of indication and instruction.
Guidance is of two kinds: guidance of success (tawfiq) and guidance of indication (dalalah). As for guidance of success, no one possesses it except Allah, the Mighty and Majestic; Allah said to His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ: ﴿إِنَّكَ لَا تَهْدِي مَنْ أَحْبَبْتَ﴾ [al-Qasas 56].
As for guidance of indication, it is established for everything through which instruction and indication occur; the Qur'an guides to a straight path, and the Prophet ﷺ guides to a straight path. Do you understand?
Good. Here: ﴿وَيَهْدِي إِلَى صِرَاطِ﴾ means what?
* A student: To the path.
* The Shaykh: No, what is the meaning of ﴿يَهْدِي﴾? It means "indicates."
His saying ﴿إِلَى صِرَاطِ الْعَزِيزِ الْحَمِيدِ﴾ means Allah. Here He said ﴿صِرَاطِ الْعَزِيزِ الْحَمِيدِ﴾, as He said in Surah Ibrahim: ﴿لِتُخْرِجَ النَّاسَ مِنَ الظُّلُمَاتِ إِلَى النُّورِ بِإِذْنِ رَبِّهِمْ إِلَى صِرَاطِ الْعَزِيزِ الْحَمِيدِ﴾ [Ibrahim 1]. He attributed it to this magnificent name, which indicates might, as a sign that whoever holds fast to this path will have might.
﴿الْحَمِيدِ﴾ is also a sign that whoever adheres to this path will be in a praiseworthy station.
As for ﴿الْعَزِيزِ﴾, which is a name of Allah: the Mighty is the one who possesses might, and Allah, the Exalted, possesses all might; ﴿فَلِلَّهِ الْعِزَّةُ جَمِيعًا﴾ [Fatir 10].
The might with which Allah is described includes three meanings: might of rank (qadr), might of dominance (qahr), and might of inaccessibility (imtina'). Pay attention! The might by which Allah is characterized includes three meanings: might of rank, dominance, and inaccessibility.
As for the might of rank, its meaning is that Allah, the Exalted, has great rank; as for the might of dominance, its meaning is that Allah has great dominance and overpowering that no one overcomes; and as for the might of inaccessibility, its meaning is that Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, is free from any deficiency in any respect; no defect can ever reach Him. This might is attributed to whom?
* Students: To Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.
* The Shaykh: To Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: might of rank, and what else? Dominance, and inaccessibility.
So it is said, for example: "This is 'aziz 'alayya" (dear to me); that is, of noble rank in my estimation. And Allah the Exalted said: ﴿وَعَزَّنِي فِي الْخِطَابِ﴾ [Sad 23], meaning: he overpowered me; this is the might of dominance and overpowering. It is said: "ardun 'azzaz," meaning a land that is firm and hard, on which the tread of feet has no effect; this is the might of inaccessibility. So Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, is described with might in all its three meanings.
As for ﴿الْحَمِيدِ﴾, the author says it means "praised" (al-mahmud). It is correct that fa'il may come in the sense of maf'ul, as in the saying "qatil" meaning "killed" and "jarih" meaning "wounded." But it also comes in the sense of fa'il, such as "'alim" meaning "knowing," "'aziz" meaning "mighty" (one who has might), "hakim" meaning "wise" (one who makes firm); in this way it comes in this sense too.
If it comes in both senses, that is, active and passive, is it better to restrict it to the passive or to make it inclusive?
* A student: Inclusive.
* The Shaykh: Inclusive. So He, the Glorified and Exalted, is "hamid" in the sense of one who praises and in the sense of one who is praised. As for His being one who praises, how often does Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, praise His believing servants! Or not? Does Allah praise the believers or not? So this is praising, and He is the Praiser, the Glorified and Exalted. As for His being praised, it is evident, for Allah, the Exalted, deserves praise in every situation.
The summary is that the author's explanation of ﴿الْحَمِيدِ﴾ as "praised" is deficient, and the correct view is that it means both praised and praising, and that to Him belongs praise, Glorified and Exalted, in this world and the Hereafter.
Good. Is there evidence in the addition of the path to the name of Allah, ﴿الْحَمِيدِ﴾? I said its benefit is that it indicates that whoever holds fast to this path is mighty and also praised; praised for his adherence to this path (...).
* * *
* A student: In His saying, ﴿لَهُمْ مَغْفِرَةٌ وَرِزْقٌ كَرِيمٌ﴾, the author said: (good provision in Paradise). Does this restrict the provision to Paradise?
* The Shaykh: No, his intention is: ﴿لَهُمْ مَغْفِرَةٌ وَرِزْقٌ﴾, meaning: in Paradise.
* The student: So it is general, meaning it is both in this world and the Hereafter?
* The Shaykh: No, when he mentioned forgiveness, forgiveness's effects only appear there. But as you said, the better view is generality; it is better to say that this is general.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 34, verse 4–6 (part 3 of 4):

If you say: We find among the believers who do righteous deeds someone who is poor, so where is the generosity in provision?

We say, as the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Wealth is not having many possessions; rather, wealth is the wealth of the soul" [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (6446) and Muslim (1051/120), from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah with the wording: "Wealth is not from having many possessions, but true wealth is the wealth of the soul."]. A person may have much wealth yet his condition be the condition of the poor.

* Student: Regarding His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And those who have been given knowledge see that what has been revealed to you from your Lord is the truth﴾, to the end. This raises a difficulty: some of those who have been given knowledge (...) do not see that what the Prophet was given is the truth, (...) they say: it is not true, it is falsehood, and there is nothing in it (...) and it does not fit the age (...). So what is the answer?

* Shaykh: Did you hear the brother's question? He says: among the people of knowledge, those who have been given knowledge, there are some who do not see that what was sent down to him from his Lord is the truth. We say: this is not possible. Everyone who has been given knowledge sees that what the Prophet (ﷺ) brought is the truth, but he may be stubborn and arrogant. The problem of this one, meaning obstinacy, has nothing for it except the sword, if he deserves to be killed. Otherwise, every person who is given knowledge must bear witness to the truth of what the Messenger (ﷺ) brought, because what the Messenger brought corresponds to reality, so he must know that it is the truth. Allah the Exalted said about the people of Pharaoh: ﴿And they denied them while their souls were convinced of them, out of wrongdoing and arrogance﴾ [an-Naml 14]. So they were certain of them and knew them to be the truth, but they denied. And He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿We know that what they say grieves you; but it is not you they deny, rather the wrongdoers deny the signs of Allah﴾ [al-An'am 33]. Yes indeed (...).
* * *
Among the benefits (...).
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: It includes everyone whom Allah has given knowledge, including Abdullah ibn Salam and others.
* Student: (...)?
* Shaykh: (...) this is not correct; it is permissible for the verse to be revealed before the event occurs.
* Among the benefits from His saying... I think... the benefits, brothers.
* Student: ﴿So that He may reward those who believed and did righteous deeds﴾.
* Shaykh: From whom is this?
* It is derived from the noble verse that the actions of Allah, glory be to Him, are motivated; meaning that they have a cause. From where is this derived?
* Students: ﴿So that He may reward﴾.
* Shaykh: From the lam in ﴿so that He may reward﴾; because the lam is for causation, and this supports the position of the People of the Sunnah and the Jama'ah, who say that the actions of Allah are accompanied by wisdom.
You know that the Jahmiyyah, and likewise some of the Ash'ariyyah, deny that the actions of Allah are for a wisdom, and they say: His actions are merely by will. They said: because wisdom is a purpose among the purposes that move one to act, and Allah, glory be to Him, is exalted above purposes.
We say to them: this contradicts the texts. If we reflect on the Qur'an we find thousands of verses that establish wisdom for Allah, Mighty and Majestic. Then, if the purpose is the benefit of another, it is what? Praise and commendation; and if it is for a need (...) in which there is no deficiency in any respect.
The corrupt principle has already been mentioned to you: those who say that Allah is exalted above accidents, purposes and parts.
When you hear this statement you think: this is a good statement, exalted above accidents, purposes and parts.
("Exalted above accidents") they mean by this the negation of His voluntary actions; meaning that He does not descend, does not come, does not speak, and so on, because these are accidents that arise and cease.
("Parts") they mean by this the negation of the Face, the two Hands, the two Eyes and what is similar to that, because these are parts with respect to us.
("Purposes") they mean by this the negation of wisdom. The Qur'an refutes their saying.
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the excellence of faith and righteous deeds, its aspect being from the reward that follows from it: ﴿For them is forgiveness and generous provision﴾; and whatever reward follows from it is virtuous, praiseworthy and desired.
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the distinction between faith and righteous deeds when they are mentioned together; for here He did not say ﴿those who believed﴾ alone, nor ﴿did righteous deeds﴾ alone, but combined them. We have already mentioned that when the two are combined, faith is in the heart and righteous deeds are in the limbs.
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: an indication that faith alone, meaning that which is in the heart only, does not suffice without righteous deeds; because He attached the reward to the presence of the two attributes in the doer, namely faith and righteous deeds. But I say: if faith is sincere, then righteous deeds must accompany it, due to the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "Verily, in the body there is a piece of flesh; if it is sound, the whole body is sound" [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (52), Muslim (1599/107), from the hadith of al-Nu'man ibn Bashir].
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: that deeds are not accepted, praised, or rewarded unless they are righteous; due to His saying: ﴿and did righteous deeds﴾.
When is it righteous? When it combines two conditions: sincerity to Allah, and second, following the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). If sincerity is lacking, it is not righteous and is rejected from its doer; Allah the Exalted said: "I am the most self-sufficient of partners in regard to partnership; whoever does a deed in which he associates another with Me, I abandon him and his partnership" [Muslim (2985/46), from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah]. And if following is lacking, it is also rejected and not accepted; due to the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "Whoever does a deed that is not in accordance with our command, it is rejected" [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (2697), Muslim (1718/18), the wording being his, from the hadith of Aisha]. Following is not realized except by six conditions:
That the worship or deed be in accordance with the Shari'ah in its cause, its kind, its amount, its manner, its time and its place. Following is not realized until the deed conforms to the Shari'ah in these six matters. What are they? In its cause, its kind, its amount, its manner, its time and its place. Complete.
So if a person introduces an act of worship for a non-legislated cause, it is rejected. If he says: "Whenever I hear the barking of dogs, I pray two rak'ahs." Is it valid or not?
Students: It is not valid.
* Shaykh: Is it accepted from him or not?
* Students: It is not accepted.
* Shaykh: Why? Because he attached it to a cause for which it was not legislated, so it is not accepted.
If someone sacrificed a mare, a female horse, saying: "I have a sheep worth two hundred riyals, and I have a mare worth twenty thousand riyals, and I want to sacrifice the mare." Is it accepted?
* Student: It is not accepted.
* Shaykh: Why?
* Student: The kind (...).
* Shaykh: Because it contradicts the Shari'ah in its kind; the sacrifice is only from the beast of livestock.
If someone worshipped Allah, Mighty and Majestic, with a specific act of worship in a defined amount, and increased its amount; as if he prayed six prayers, saying: "The period between 'Isha and Fajr is long and needs an additional prayer, and the period between Fajr and Dhuhr is long and needs an additional prayer; I want to pray seven times." What do you say?
* Students: It is rejected.
* Shaykh: Why?
* Student: For the manner.
* Another student: The amount.
* Shaykh: Its amount. Or if he prayed five in a four-rak'ah prayer or three in a two-rak'ah prayer, it is not accepted.
If someone says: "If a man glorifies Allah two hundred times after the prayer, do you reject all this glorification, or do you say: what conforms to the Shari'ah is accepted and what exceeds it is rejected?"
* Students: The latter.
* Shaykh: We say: if the act of worship in which the increase occurred is divisible, meaning that its first part is valid without its last part, we do not nullify its first part because of what occurred to it. But if it is not divisible, then if its last part is nullified, its first part is nullified; so if he prayed Dhuhr with five rak'ahs, his prayer is invalid, because its first part cannot be valid when its last part is corrupt. But in an increase in number, we do not nullify the first number; yet we say to this man: if you believe that two hundred is the legislated amount, then you are astray, because you are an innovator; and if you mean to say: I acknowledge that the legislated amount is one hundred, but I added to it as a voluntary act, then the reward of unrestricted glorification is written for you, not that of the restricted glorification.
As to its manner: if someone prayed and began to prostrate, then bow, then prostrate, what do you say?
* Students: It is not valid.
* Shaykh: Why?
* Students: The manner.
* Shaykh: Because the manner differs.
As to time: if someone said: "I will perform Hajj in Dhu al-Qa'dah; I will go out to Mina on the night of the ninth of Dhu al-Qa'dah and spend the night there, and on the ninth I will go to 'Arafah and stand there... to the end," and he completes the acts of Hajj in Dhu al-Qa'dah, why? He said: "Because no one bothers me here." What do you say about this?
* Students: It is not valid.
* Shaykh: Why?
* Student: Because the time differs.
* Shaykh: Because it did not conform to the Shari'ah in time. It is said that a Bedouin man used to sell livestock for sacrifices, bringing them to the market, and he had not performed the obligatory duty. He was asked: "Why have you not performed the obligation?" He said: "The obligation comes at the time of the season, and I do not like that; but I will go to the shaykh and ask him: may I perform Hajj on the Feast of Ramadan instead of the Feast of Sacrifice? For the Feast of Sacrifice is a season for us." So he went to the shaykh asking permission, saying: "I ask your permission, O shaykh, that you allow me to perform Hajj on the Feast of Ramadan instead of the Feast of Sacrifice, because the Feast of Sacrifice is a season for us." The shaykh said to him: "If I permit you to perform Hajj, then I permit you to sacrifice." Then the season becomes subordinate to what? To the Hajj, and there is no escaping it.
So I say: whoever performs Hajj in Dhu al-Qa'dah, even if it coincides with the ninth, tenth, eleventh, twelfth and thirteenth, it is not accepted, why? Because it contradicts the time.
A man in the last ten nights of Ramadan said: "I will remain in seclusion (i'tikaf) in my house; I will not go out to the mosque, I tire of obtaining food and drink, and perhaps someone will come and distract me from remembrance of Allah, so I will sit in the house." Is his i'tikaf accepted?
* Students: It is not accepted.
* Shaykh: Why?
* Students: The place.
* Shaykh: Yes, because it contradicts the Shari'ah in place.
So it has now become clear that the realization of following is only when the deed conforms to the Shari'ah in these six matters.
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the high rank of believers who do righteous deeds; due to His saying: ﴿those﴾, for the demonstrative here is for the distant, and that is because of their elevated rank, like His saying: ﴿Alif, Lam, Mim. That is the Book﴾ [al-Baqarah 1–2], although the Book is before us, yet He pointed to it with the demonstrative of distance because of its elevated rank.
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: that in faith and righteous deeds is the attainment of what is sought and the removal of what is disliked; due to His saying: ﴿For them is forgiveness﴾, this is the removal of what is disliked, and ﴿and generous provision﴾, this is the attainment of what is sought.
Know that when Allah forgives you, He opens for you the doors of knowledge and expands your chest with faith; for what causes constriction of the chest and scattering of thought is sins: ﴿When Our signs are recited to him, he says: "Tales of the ancients"﴾ [al-Mutaffifin 13]. Look: he does not recognize the worth of the Qur'an; when the Qur'an is recited to him he says "tales of the ancients," so he does not recognize its worth. Why? ﴿Nay, but what they used to earn has rusted over their hearts﴾ [al-Mutaffifin 14]. When his deeds have rusted over his heart, he becomes, may Allah protect us, unable to see this great Qur'an except as what? Except as tales of the ancients.
For this reason some scholars said: whoever is afflicted with a calamity and seeks its ruling, whether this calamity is specific to him or he is asked about it, he should seek Allah's forgiveness. They cited as evidence His saying: ﴿Indeed We have sent down to you the Book in truth, that you may judge between the people by what Allah has shown you; so do not be an advocate for the treacherous﴾ [an-Nisa 105]. What follows? ﴿And seek forgiveness from Allah; indeed Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful﴾ [an-Nisa 106]. And this is not far.
So among the benefits of faith and righteous deeds is the attainment of what is sought and deliverance from what is disliked.
* Also among the benefits of the noble verse: that the provision of Paradise is generous provision; i.e., vast, abundant, lasting and good. This is indicated by His saying: ﴿So no soul knows what has been hidden for them of comfort for eyes as reward for what they used to do﴾ [as-Sajdah 17], and His saying: ﴿And fruit in abundance, neither cut off nor forbidden﴾ [al-Waqi'ah 32–33].
Then He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿And those who strive against Our signs, seeking to frustrate them, for them is a painful punishment of a vile kind.﴾
* Derived from this verse: the realization of what Allah described the Qur'an with, that it is what?
* Student: True.
* Shaykh: No, that it is mathani (oft-repeated): when its meaning is mentioned, its opposite is mentioned, and when the doer is mentioned, the one who opposes him is mentioned.
* Also derived from it: the wisdom in address, and that address should combine causes of fear and causes of hope. Why?
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: It should combine them, because if fear alone is mentioned, despair of Allah's mercy may take hold of the heart; or hope alone, then a sense of security from Allah's plan may take hold of it, Glory be to Him.
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: that the disbelievers strive earnestly to nullify the signs of Allah, Mighty and Majestic; due to His saying: ﴿those who strive against Our signs﴾. Striving, as we know, is running with intensity; these ones strive earnestly to nullify the signs of Allah, Glory be to Him.
* Also among its benefits: that these disbelievers are as if they seek to outpace Allah and overcome Him; due to His saying: ﴿seeking to frustrate them﴾.
* Also among its benefits: that those who strive against the signs of Allah, seeking to frustrate them, are punished with this painful punishment; ﴿for them is a painful punishment﴾, and His saying: ﴿of a vile kind﴾ means: of an evil, painful punishment, as has passed for us.
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: warning against a person striving to nullify the signs of Allah. If we say, according to the rule that passed for us in the principles of tafsir the day before yesterday, that when something is forbidden, it is a command to its opposite, then this verse includes an exhortation to strive for the signs of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, to establish and confirm them. And so it is: we are commanded to strive, to the extent of our ability, in establishing and confirming the signs of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and spreading them among the Ummah until the religion is established.
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the affirmation of reward and of wisdom in it; for the believers who did righteous deeds, ﴿for them is forgiveness and generous provision﴾, and these, ﴿for them is a painful punishment of a vile kind﴾.
Then He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿And those who have been given knowledge see that what has been revealed to you from your Lord is the truth﴾, to the end.
* In this verse: the virtue of knowledge. From where is it derived?
* Students: ﴿those who have been given knowledge﴾.
* Shaykh: Yes, but the virtue of knowledge.
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: But what is the aspect by which this indicates the virtue of knowledge?
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: No.
* Student: That they see it as the truth, because Allah, Glory be to Him, has given them knowledge.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 34, verse 4–6 (part 4 of 4):

* The Shaykh: Correct. The scholar knows realities as they truly are, so he sees that what was sent down to the Messenger is the truth. There is no doubt that this is one of the virtues of knowledge, in contrast to one who wavers as to whether it is true or denies that it is true, and we seek refuge with Allah. Those whom Allah has favoured with knowledge see that it is the truth.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: an indication that a person should not be impressed by his own knowledge. From where is this taken?
* A student: (...).
* The Shaykh: ﴿And those who have been given knowledge see that what has been sent down to you from your Lord is the truth﴾.
* The student: (...).
* The Shaykh: No.
* A student: ﴿And those who see﴾; meaning: he knows...
* The Shaykh: No.
* A student: that this knowledge was sent down from Allah, the Exalted.
* The Shaykh: No.
* A student: ﴿That which was sent down to you﴾.
* The Shaykh: No, my brothers. In it is evidence that a person should not be impressed by his knowledge, due to His saying: ﴿those who have been given knowledge﴾; meaning, they did not attain it by themselves, but Allah, the Exalted, bestowed it upon them as a favour. Is it clear? Do not say: "This is from me." The same applies to wealth. Some people become impressed when they acquire wealth, yet the One who gave them the wealth is Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. And what did Allah do to the one who said: ﴿I was only given it on account of knowledge I have﴾ [al-Qasas 78]? He caused the earth to swallow him up. So ﴿those who have been given knowledge﴾ contains evidence that a person should not be impressed with himself and say: "I acquired this knowledge by my own understanding, my eagerness and my perseverance."
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that a person should turn to Allah, the Exalted, in acquiring knowledge. From where do we take this?
* A student: ﴿those who have been given knowledge﴾.
* The Shaykh: From His saying: ﴿those who have been given knowledge﴾. So if we are given knowledge, let us ask this knowledge from the One who gives it to us. Is that not so?
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that the Qur'an is the speech of Allah; ﴿sent down to you from your Lord﴾, ﴿from your Lord﴾. How is this evidence that it is the speech of Allah? Because not everything that is sent down is speech; Allah may mention the sending down of a thing that is not speech.
* A student: Because what descends from Allah is either subsisting in its own essence or subsisting in something else. That which subsists in its own essence is created, like rain and the like, whereas the Qur'an subsists in another (i.e., in the One who speaks).
* The Shaykh: Because it is speech, and speech cannot exist except from a speaker. Therefore the speech of Allah is uncreated. Is it clear, everyone? Otherwise, there are things that Allah sends down and says: "We sent them down," and they are created: ﴿He sends down water from the sky﴾ [al-An'am 99], ﴿And We sent down water from the sky﴾ [al-Mu'minun 18], ﴿And He sent down for you eight pairs of livestock﴾ [az-Zumar 6], ﴿And We sent down iron, wherein is great might﴾ [al-Hadid 25]. All of these things are created, are they not? Because they are entities subsisting in their own essence. This is unlike speech, for speech cannot exist except from a speaker. So when Allah says: ﴿He has sent down to you the Book﴾ [Al 'Imran 7], and it is speech, this speech becomes the speech of Allah.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the virtue of the Prophet ﷺ. From where is this taken?
* Students: ﴿from your Lord﴾.
* The Shaykh: From the attribution of lordship (rububiyyah) to him, and this lordship is a special one, as we also passed over in the principles of tafsir. So we say: in this is the virtue of the Prophet ﷺ.
* And among its benefits: the care of Allah for the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, by His saying: ﴿from your Lord﴾, and in it is a statement of the grace of Allah upon him, in that He sent down the truth to him.
* And among the benefits of this noble verse also: that this Qur'an is true in its reports and in its rulings. Truthfulness in reports is sincerity (sidq), and in rulings it is justice ('adl). Allah combined both in His saying: ﴿And the word of your Lord has been fulfilled in truth and justice﴾ [al-An'am 115].
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that the Qur'an is a beacon and guidance..
Among the benefits of this noble verse: that the Qur'an is a beacon and guidance by which people are guided and find light; due to His saying: ﴿and guides to the path of the Mighty, the Praiseworthy﴾ [Saba' 6].
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that whoever seeks guidance from other than it goes astray. For if it is the One who guides to the path of the Mighty, the Praiseworthy, then if you seek guidance from other than it, which opposes it, you will not be guided to the path of the Mighty, the Praiseworthy. For this reason, when the people of innovation sought to reach the Creator by a path other than the Qur'an, what befell them? They went astray, became lost, and remained bewildered and confused.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that whoever holds fast to this Qur'an attains might and praise, i.e., becomes mighty and praised; due to His saying: ﴿to the path of the Mighty, the Praiseworthy﴾. He did not say "to the path of Allah," but said: ﴿to the path of the Mighty, the Praiseworthy﴾, indicating that whoever holds fast to this Qur'an has might and has praise; he is praised for his actions, his words and his abstentions.
* And among its benefits: the affirmation of these two names of Allah, the Mighty and the Praiseworthy. We have said that the might with which Allah, the Exalted, is described has three types..
* A student: The might of subjugation (qahr), the might of decree (qadr), and the might of inaccessibility (imtina').
* The Shaykh: The might of inaccessibility, correct? The might of decree, the might of subjugation, and the might of inaccessibility, is that right? Good. Explain them.
* A student: The might of decree is that you are a person... this is a mighty person (...). As for the might of subjugation, Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿and he overpowered me in speech﴾ [Sad 23], meaning he overcame me. As for inaccessibility, you say: "This is a 'azaz land," meaning strong, hard, and unassailable.
* The Shaykh: Good, well done.
Al-Hamid is also one of the names of Allah, and it is derived from hamd (praise). Is it in the sense of the active participle or the passive participle?
(...) the might and the affirmation of praise for Allah. There is a phrase among people that says: "Praise be to Allah who is not praised for anything disliked except Him." What do you say about this phrase?
* Students: It is incorrect.
* The Shaykh: It is not appropriate, because you are making a complete declaration that you dislike what Allah has decreed. When the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, was struck by something he liked, he said: "Praise be to Allah through whose blessing good deeds are completed," and when something he disliked befell him, he said: "Praise be to Allah in every circumstance." [[Narrated by Ibn Majah (3803) from the hadith of 'A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her.]] He did not mention anything disliked. Therefore we should admonish whoever uses this phrase: say, "O brother, do not say it like this; this suggests you are not content with the decree of Allah. Say: 'Praise be to Allah in every circumstance.'"
Now, we know that Allah is the Lord of everything, and this includes dogs, pigs, insects and the like. But is it proper to say: "Allah is the Lord of dogs, the Lord of pigs, the Lord of insects"? This is not proper etiquette, to specify in this way, as Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah and others have stated. Here there is a difference between generalization and specification; for this reason the Messenger said: "Praise be to Allah in every circumstance."

In addition, there is His saying: ﴿That He may reward those who believed and did righteous deeds. For those are forgiveness and a generous provision﴾ [Saba' 4]. Where does this verse fit in meaning with what comes before it? Or, the lam in His saying ﴿That He may reward﴾ is connected to what? Who? Did we not explain it?

* Students: No, teacher, the earlier part, which is (clarifies that it is the Preserved Tablet).

* The Shaykh: Allah the Exalted says: ﴿That He may reward those who believed and did righteous deeds﴾. He said: (﴿That He may reward﴾ in it), (in it) the pronoun refers to the Hour.

﴿That He may reward﴾: the lam here indicates purpose (ta'lil). We know from the rules of the Arabic language that prepositions must have something they relate to (muta'allaq). So where is the object of this lam? The object of this lam is His saying ﴿will surely come to you﴾. That is: it will surely come to you so that He may reward those who... So this lam is for purpose, and it is connected to His saying ﴿will surely come to you﴾.

And ﴿yajziya﴾ means: to recompense or to reward. The subject is Allah, glorified and exalted.

As for his saying (in it), the author, by his saying (in it), indicates that the prepositional phrase is connected to (will come to you), because the pronoun in his saying (in it) refers to the Hour: (﴿That He may reward﴾ in it).

﴿Those who believed and did righteous deeds﴾: they believed in the heart, and did righteous deeds with the limbs. When faith is mentioned alone, it includes outward actions, the actions of the limbs. Likewise, when action is mentioned alone, it includes faith in the heart, because faith in the heart is one of the deeds of the hearts. So when both are mentioned together, faith is in the heart and action is in the limbs. Faith is secret and action is open.

As for His saying ﴿believed﴾: faith (iman) linguistically means assent (tasdiq). In the sharia, it means assent that necessitates acceptance and submission (idhan). It is not mere assent; rather, it is assent that necessitates acceptance and submission. Acceptance applies to reports, and submission applies to commands. So, for example, a person accepts what Allah and His Messenger have informed, and accepts that this ruling is obligatory, or that it is voluntary, and similar things, and submits to that, meaning he worships Allah in accordance with what he believes and in accordance with what Allah has legislated, glorified and exalted is He.

In His saying ﴿those who believed and did righteous deeds﴾, ﴿did righteous deeds﴾ means: they did righteous actions. So ﴿righteous﴾ is an adjective for an omitted noun.

Omitting the described noun is permissible when there is an indication of it. Ibn Malik said:

"What is understood of the described noun and the adjective may be omitted, and in the adjective it is rare."

From the omission of the described noun is His saying: ﴿Do work, making coats of mail that are full length﴾ [Saba' 11], meaning: coats of mail that are full length.

So on this basis, ﴿righteous﴾ is an adjective for an omitted noun, meaning: the righteous deeds. And what are the righteous deeds? A righteous deed is one that combines two matters:

Sincerity to Allah, glorified and exalted, and following the Messenger ﷺ. If the first is missing, it is not righteous, and it is rejected from the doer. If the second is missing, it is also not righteous, and it is rejected from the doer.

The evidence: for the first, Allah said in a hadith qudsi: "I am the most self-sufficient of partners from association. Whoever does a deed in which he associates another with Me, I abandon him and his association." [Recorded by Muslim (2985/46) from the hadith of Abu Hurayra.]

For the second, the Prophet ﷺ said: "Whoever does a deed that is not in accordance with our affair, it is rejected," or "Whoever introduces into this affair of ours something that is not part of it, it is rejected." [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (2697) and Muslim (1718/18), from the hadith of Aisha.]

So it is not possible for a deed to be righteous except with these two conditions: sincerity, and following the Messenger ﷺ.

If a man introduces an innovation (bid'a) of the innovations, practicing it as a form of worship to Allah, glorified and exalted, and he finds in his heart tranquility in it, humility and weeping, yet it is an innovation in the religion of Allah, would it be a righteous deed? It would not be, even if the deed is made attractive to a person and he finds peace in it. It is not a righteous deed, so it is not accepted and not beneficial.
