Therefore He attributed the lordship to him alone, saying ﴿الَّذِي أُنْزِلَ إِلَيْكَ مِنْ رَبِّكَ﴾, for the sake of honouring both the one to whom it was sent down and what was sent down.
His saying ﴿مِنْ رَبِّكَ﴾: it has already been mentioned that the meaning of lordship (rubbubiyyah) is creation, dominion and management. Allah, the Exalted, is the Creator of the Prophet ﷺ, his Owner, and his Manager.
The author said: (i.e., the Qur'an, ﴿هُوَ﴾ is a separator (fasl), ﴿الْحَقَّ﴾). ﴿الْحَقَّ﴾ is the second object, and ﴿هُوَ﴾ is a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl). Its form is that of a pronoun but it is not a pronoun; therefore we do not say it is a noun, nor do we say it has a place in i'rab; that is, it has no place in i'rab and is not a noun, but it is brought for separation.
The evidence that it has no place in i'rab is the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿لَعَلَّنَا نَتَّبِعُ السَّحَرَةَ إِنْ كَانُوا هُمُ﴾ [al-Shu'ara' 40] ﴿الْغَالِبِينَ﴾, or "al-ghalibun"?
* Students: ﴿الْغَالِبِينَ﴾.
* The Shaykh: ﴿الْغَالِبِينَ﴾. Had it had a place in i'rab, it would have said "hum al-ghalibun." Since He said ﴿هُمُ الْغَالِبِينَ﴾ and ﴿الْغَالِبِينَ﴾ became the predicate of "kana," this shows that this pronoun has no place in i'rab. But what is its benefit?
The scholars mentioned that it has three benefits. The first benefit?
* A student: Separating the adjective from the predicate.
* The Shaykh: Separating the adjective from the predicate. The second benefit?
* The student: Restriction (ḥaṣr).
* The Shaykh: Restriction. The third benefit?
* The student: Emphasis (tawkid).
* The Shaykh: Emphasis. So it gives three benefits: restriction, emphasis, and separating the predicate from the adjective. Right? Give an example to explain this to us.
* The student: (...).
* The Shaykh: (Zaydun al-fadil). The word "al-fadil" here may also be an adjective of "Zayd" with the predicate not yet having come, so the listener is now awaiting the predicate, as if its estimate were: "Zayd the virtuous is present." Or not?
* The students: Yes indeed.
* The Shaykh: If you say, "Zaydun al-fadilu hadirun" (Zayd the virtuous is present), then "al-fadilu" is without doubt an adjective and "hadirun" is the predicate. But if you say, "Zaydun al-fadilu," only, it may be that you want to inform that Zayd is virtuous, and it may be that you want to describe Zayd as virtuous while the predicate has not come. Is that not so? If you say, "Zaydun huwa al-fadilu" (Zayd is the virtuous one), then "al-fadil" is now definitely the predicate, is it not? Good, this is the aspect of it separating the adjective from the predicate.
Good, is it also emphatic?
* Students: Yes.
* The Shaykh: It is emphatic, because when you say "Zaydun al-fadilu" and "Zaydun huwa al-fadilu," the second is without doubt more emphatic.
Likewise it is useful for restriction, because when you say "Zaydun huwa al-fadil," it means: not anyone else.
So the separating pronoun gives three benefits: restriction, emphasis, and separating the predicate from the adjective.
He, the Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿هُوَ الْحَقَّ﴾. ﴿الْحَقَّ﴾ means a established thing; this is the truth. Your saying "uhiqqu al-shay'" means "I establish the thing"; ﴿حَقَّتْ عَلَيْهِمْ كَلِمَتُ رَبِّكَ﴾ [Yunus 96] means they were established and became obligatory.
What is established in the Qur'an? Truthfulness in reports, and justice in rulings. So when al-haqq is attributed to a ruling, its meaning is justice: it is a just ruling. For this reason, if two litigants dispute before a judge and he rules for one of them in accordance with what the Sharia requires, we say: this is true, because he was just; and if he rules for the other contrary to it, we say: this is not true, this is false, because he ruled other than the truth. So truth in rulings is what? Justice; and in reports, truthfulness. Those whom Allah has given knowledge know that this Qur'an is true in its rulings and true in its reports. Its rulings are all justice, for they place things in their proper place and give the right to its rightful owners; and its reports too are what? Established and true; that is, they are firm and contain no lie. So the truth (...).
So when you say, "This report is true," meaning truthful; "this ruling is true," meaning just. For this reason Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿وَتَمَّتْ كَلِمَتُ رَبِّكَ صِدْقًا وَعَدْلًا﴾ [al-An'am 115]. The scholars said: ﴿صِدْقًا﴾ concerns reports, and ﴿عَدْلًا﴾ concerns rulings.
﴿هُوَ الْحَقَّ﴾. Together with that, (﴿وَيَهْدِي إِلَى صِرَاطِ﴾, the path of ﴿الْعَزِيزِ الْحَمِيدِ﴾, meaning Allah, the Mighty, the Praiseworthy), ﴿يَهْدِي﴾ means "guides/indicates," so guidance here is guidance of indication and instruction.
Guidance is of two kinds: guidance of success (tawfiq) and guidance of indication (dalalah). As for guidance of success, no one possesses it except Allah, the Mighty and Majestic; Allah said to His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ: ﴿إِنَّكَ لَا تَهْدِي مَنْ أَحْبَبْتَ﴾ [al-Qasas 56].
As for guidance of indication, it is established for everything through which instruction and indication occur; the Qur'an guides to a straight path, and the Prophet ﷺ guides to a straight path. Do you understand?
Good. Here: ﴿وَيَهْدِي إِلَى صِرَاطِ﴾ means what?
* A student: To the path.
* The Shaykh: No, what is the meaning of ﴿يَهْدِي﴾? It means "indicates."
His saying ﴿إِلَى صِرَاطِ الْعَزِيزِ الْحَمِيدِ﴾ means Allah. Here He said ﴿صِرَاطِ الْعَزِيزِ الْحَمِيدِ﴾, as He said in Surah Ibrahim: ﴿لِتُخْرِجَ النَّاسَ مِنَ الظُّلُمَاتِ إِلَى النُّورِ بِإِذْنِ رَبِّهِمْ إِلَى صِرَاطِ الْعَزِيزِ الْحَمِيدِ﴾ [Ibrahim 1]. He attributed it to this magnificent name, which indicates might, as a sign that whoever holds fast to this path will have might.
﴿الْحَمِيدِ﴾ is also a sign that whoever adheres to this path will be in a praiseworthy station.
As for ﴿الْعَزِيزِ﴾, which is a name of Allah: the Mighty is the one who possesses might, and Allah, the Exalted, possesses all might; ﴿فَلِلَّهِ الْعِزَّةُ جَمِيعًا﴾ [Fatir 10].
The might with which Allah is described includes three meanings: might of rank (qadr), might of dominance (qahr), and might of inaccessibility (imtina'). Pay attention! The might by which Allah is characterized includes three meanings: might of rank, dominance, and inaccessibility.
As for the might of rank, its meaning is that Allah, the Exalted, has great rank; as for the might of dominance, its meaning is that Allah has great dominance and overpowering that no one overcomes; and as for the might of inaccessibility, its meaning is that Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, is free from any deficiency in any respect; no defect can ever reach Him. This might is attributed to whom?
* Students: To Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.
* The Shaykh: To Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: might of rank, and what else? Dominance, and inaccessibility.
So it is said, for example: "This is 'aziz 'alayya" (dear to me); that is, of noble rank in my estimation. And Allah the Exalted said: ﴿وَعَزَّنِي فِي الْخِطَابِ﴾ [Sad 23], meaning: he overpowered me; this is the might of dominance and overpowering. It is said: "ardun 'azzaz," meaning a land that is firm and hard, on which the tread of feet has no effect; this is the might of inaccessibility. So Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, is described with might in all its three meanings.
As for ﴿الْحَمِيدِ﴾, the author says it means "praised" (al-mahmud). It is correct that fa'il may come in the sense of maf'ul, as in the saying "qatil" meaning "killed" and "jarih" meaning "wounded." But it also comes in the sense of fa'il, such as "'alim" meaning "knowing," "'aziz" meaning "mighty" (one who has might), "hakim" meaning "wise" (one who makes firm); in this way it comes in this sense too.
If it comes in both senses, that is, active and passive, is it better to restrict it to the passive or to make it inclusive?
* A student: Inclusive.
* The Shaykh: Inclusive. So He, the Glorified and Exalted, is "hamid" in the sense of one who praises and in the sense of one who is praised. As for His being one who praises, how often does Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, praise His believing servants! Or not? Does Allah praise the believers or not? So this is praising, and He is the Praiser, the Glorified and Exalted. As for His being praised, it is evident, for Allah, the Exalted, deserves praise in every situation.
The summary is that the author's explanation of ﴿الْحَمِيدِ﴾ as "praised" is deficient, and the correct view is that it means both praised and praising, and that to Him belongs praise, Glorified and Exalted, in this world and the Hereafter.
Good. Is there evidence in the addition of the path to the name of Allah, ﴿الْحَمِيدِ﴾? I said its benefit is that it indicates that whoever holds fast to this path is mighty and also praised; praised for his adherence to this path (...).
* * *
* A student: In His saying, ﴿لَهُمْ مَغْفِرَةٌ وَرِزْقٌ كَرِيمٌ﴾, the author said: (good provision in Paradise). Does this restrict the provision to Paradise?
* The Shaykh: No, his intention is: ﴿لَهُمْ مَغْفِرَةٌ وَرِزْقٌ﴾, meaning: in Paradise.
* The student: So it is general, meaning it is both in this world and the Hereafter?
* The Shaykh: No, when he mentioned forgiveness, forgiveness's effects only appear there. But as you said, the better view is generality; it is better to say that this is general.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 34, verse 4–6 (part 3 of 4):

If you say: We find among the believers who do righteous deeds someone who is poor, so where is the generosity in provision?

We say, as the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Wealth is not having many possessions; rather, wealth is the wealth of the soul" [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (6446) and Muslim (1051/120), from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah with the wording: "Wealth is not from having many possessions, but true wealth is the wealth of the soul."]. A person may have much wealth yet his condition be the condition of the poor.

* Student: Regarding His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And those who have been given knowledge see that what has been revealed to you from your Lord is the truth﴾, to the end. This raises a difficulty: some of those who have been given knowledge (...) do not see that what the Prophet was given is the truth, (...) they say: it is not true, it is falsehood, and there is nothing in it (...) and it does not fit the age (...). So what is the answer?

* Shaykh: Did you hear the brother's question? He says: among the people of knowledge, those who have been given knowledge, there are some who do not see that what was sent down to him from his Lord is the truth. We say: this is not possible. Everyone who has been given knowledge sees that what the Prophet (ﷺ) brought is the truth, but he may be stubborn and arrogant. The problem of this one, meaning obstinacy, has nothing for it except the sword, if he deserves to be killed. Otherwise, every person who is given knowledge must bear witness to the truth of what the Messenger (ﷺ) brought, because what the Messenger brought corresponds to reality, so he must know that it is the truth. Allah the Exalted said about the people of Pharaoh: ﴿And they denied them while their souls were convinced of them, out of wrongdoing and arrogance﴾ [an-Naml 14]. So they were certain of them and knew them to be the truth, but they denied. And He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿We know that what they say grieves you; but it is not you they deny, rather the wrongdoers deny the signs of Allah﴾ [al-An'am 33]. Yes indeed (...).
* * *
Among the benefits (...).
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: It includes everyone whom Allah has given knowledge, including Abdullah ibn Salam and others.
* Student: (...)?
* Shaykh: (...) this is not correct; it is permissible for the verse to be revealed before the event occurs.
* Among the benefits from His saying... I think... the benefits, brothers.
* Student: ﴿So that He may reward those who believed and did righteous deeds﴾.
* Shaykh: From whom is this?
* It is derived from the noble verse that the actions of Allah, glory be to Him, are motivated; meaning that they have a cause. From where is this derived?
* Students: ﴿So that He may reward﴾.
* Shaykh: From the lam in ﴿so that He may reward﴾; because the lam is for causation, and this supports the position of the People of the Sunnah and the Jama'ah, who say that the actions of Allah are accompanied by wisdom.
You know that the Jahmiyyah, and likewise some of the Ash'ariyyah, deny that the actions of Allah are for a wisdom, and they say: His actions are merely by will. They said: because wisdom is a purpose among the purposes that move one to act, and Allah, glory be to Him, is exalted above purposes.
We say to them: this contradicts the texts. If we reflect on the Qur'an we find thousands of verses that establish wisdom for Allah, Mighty and Majestic. Then, if the purpose is the benefit of another, it is what? Praise and commendation; and if it is for a need (...) in which there is no deficiency in any respect.
The corrupt principle has already been mentioned to you: those who say that Allah is exalted above accidents, purposes and parts.
When you hear this statement you think: this is a good statement, exalted above accidents, purposes and parts.
("Exalted above accidents") they mean by this the negation of His voluntary actions; meaning that He does not descend, does not come, does not speak, and so on, because these are accidents that arise and cease.
("Parts") they mean by this the negation of the Face, the two Hands, the two Eyes and what is similar to that, because these are parts with respect to us.
("Purposes") they mean by this the negation of wisdom. The Qur'an refutes their saying.
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the excellence of faith and righteous deeds, its aspect being from the reward that follows from it: ﴿For them is forgiveness and generous provision﴾; and whatever reward follows from it is virtuous, praiseworthy and desired.
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the distinction between faith and righteous deeds when they are mentioned together; for here He did not say ﴿those who believed﴾ alone, nor ﴿did righteous deeds﴾ alone, but combined them. We have already mentioned that when the two are combined, faith is in the heart and righteous deeds are in the limbs.
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: an indication that faith alone, meaning that which is in the heart only, does not suffice without righteous deeds; because He attached the reward to the presence of the two attributes in the doer, namely faith and righteous deeds. But I say: if faith is sincere, then righteous deeds must accompany it, due to the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "Verily, in the body there is a piece of flesh; if it is sound, the whole body is sound" [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (52), Muslim (1599/107), from the hadith of al-Nu'man ibn Bashir].
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: that deeds are not accepted, praised, or rewarded unless they are righteous; due to His saying: ﴿and did righteous deeds﴾.
When is it righteous? When it combines two conditions: sincerity to Allah, and second, following the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). If sincerity is lacking, it is not righteous and is rejected from its doer; Allah the Exalted said: "I am the most self-sufficient of partners in regard to partnership; whoever does a deed in which he associates another with Me, I abandon him and his partnership" [Muslim (2985/46), from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah]. And if following is lacking, it is also rejected and not accepted; due to the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "Whoever does a deed that is not in accordance with our command, it is rejected" [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (2697), Muslim (1718/18), the wording being his, from the hadith of Aisha]. Following is not realized except by six conditions:
That the worship or deed be in accordance with the Shari'ah in its cause, its kind, its amount, its manner, its time and its place. Following is not realized until the deed conforms to the Shari'ah in these six matters. What are they? In its cause, its kind, its amount, its manner, its time and its place. Complete.
So if a person introduces an act of worship for a non-legislated cause, it is rejected. If he says: "Whenever I hear the barking of dogs, I pray two rak'ahs." Is it valid or not?
Students: It is not valid.
* Shaykh: Is it accepted from him or not?
* Students: It is not accepted.
* Shaykh: Why? Because he attached it to a cause for which it was not legislated, so it is not accepted.
If someone sacrificed a mare, a female horse, saying: "I have a sheep worth two hundred riyals, and I have a mare worth twenty thousand riyals, and I want to sacrifice the mare." Is it accepted?
* Student: It is not accepted.
* Shaykh: Why?
* Student: The kind (...).
* Shaykh: Because it contradicts the Shari'ah in its kind; the sacrifice is only from the beast of livestock.
If someone worshipped Allah, Mighty and Majestic, with a specific act of worship in a defined amount, and increased its amount; as if he prayed six prayers, saying: "The period between 'Isha and Fajr is long and needs an additional prayer, and the period between Fajr and Dhuhr is long and needs an additional prayer; I want to pray seven times." What do you say?
* Students: It is rejected.
* Shaykh: Why?
* Student: For the manner.
* Another student: The amount.
* Shaykh: Its amount. Or if he prayed five in a four-rak'ah prayer or three in a two-rak'ah prayer, it is not accepted.
If someone says: "If a man glorifies Allah two hundred times after the prayer, do you reject all this glorification, or do you say: what conforms to the Shari'ah is accepted and what exceeds it is rejected?"
* Students: The latter.
* Shaykh: We say: if the act of worship in which the increase occurred is divisible, meaning that its first part is valid without its last part, we do not nullify its first part because of what occurred to it. But if it is not divisible, then if its last part is nullified, its first part is nullified; so if he prayed Dhuhr with five rak'ahs, his prayer is invalid, because its first part cannot be valid when its last part is corrupt. But in an increase in number, we do not nullify the first number; yet we say to this man: if you believe that two hundred is the legislated amount, then you are astray, because you are an innovator; and if you mean to say: I acknowledge that the legislated amount is one hundred, but I added to it as a voluntary act, then the reward of unrestricted glorification is written for you, not that of the restricted glorification.
As to its manner: if someone prayed and began to prostrate, then bow, then prostrate, what do you say?
* Students: It is not valid.
* Shaykh: Why?
* Students: The manner.
* Shaykh: Because the manner differs.
As to time: if someone said: "I will perform Hajj in Dhu al-Qa'dah; I will go out to Mina on the night of the ninth of Dhu al-Qa'dah and spend the night there, and on the ninth I will go to 'Arafah and stand there... to the end," and he completes the acts of Hajj in Dhu al-Qa'dah, why? He said: "Because no one bothers me here." What do you say about this?
* Students: It is not valid.
* Shaykh: Why?
* Student: Because the time differs.
* Shaykh: Because it did not conform to the Shari'ah in time. It is said that a Bedouin man used to sell livestock for sacrifices, bringing them to the market, and he had not performed the obligatory duty. He was asked: "Why have you not performed the obligation?" He said: "The obligation comes at the time of the season, and I do not like that; but I will go to the shaykh and ask him: may I perform Hajj on the Feast of Ramadan instead of the Feast of Sacrifice? For the Feast of Sacrifice is a season for us." So he went to the shaykh asking permission, saying: "I ask your permission, O shaykh, that you allow me to perform Hajj on the Feast of Ramadan instead of the Feast of Sacrifice, because the Feast of Sacrifice is a season for us." The shaykh said to him: "If I permit you to perform Hajj, then I permit you to sacrifice." Then the season becomes subordinate to what? To the Hajj, and there is no escaping it.
So I say: whoever performs Hajj in Dhu al-Qa'dah, even if it coincides with the ninth, tenth, eleventh, twelfth and thirteenth, it is not accepted, why? Because it contradicts the time.
A man in the last ten nights of Ramadan said: "I will remain in seclusion (i'tikaf) in my house; I will not go out to the mosque, I tire of obtaining food and drink, and perhaps someone will come and distract me from remembrance of Allah, so I will sit in the house." Is his i'tikaf accepted?
* Students: It is not accepted.
* Shaykh: Why?
* Students: The place.
* Shaykh: Yes, because it contradicts the Shari'ah in place.
So it has now become clear that the realization of following is only when the deed conforms to the Shari'ah in these six matters.
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the high rank of believers who do righteous deeds; due to His saying: ﴿those﴾, for the demonstrative here is for the distant, and that is because of their elevated rank, like His saying: ﴿Alif, Lam, Mim. That is the Book﴾ [al-Baqarah 1–2], although the Book is before us, yet He pointed to it with the demonstrative of distance because of its elevated rank.
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: that in faith and righteous deeds is the attainment of what is sought and the removal of what is disliked; due to His saying: ﴿For them is forgiveness﴾, this is the removal of what is disliked, and ﴿and generous provision﴾, this is the attainment of what is sought.
Know that when Allah forgives you, He opens for you the doors of knowledge and expands your chest with faith; for what causes constriction of the chest and scattering of thought is sins: ﴿When Our signs are recited to him, he says: "Tales of the ancients"﴾ [al-Mutaffifin 13]. Look: he does not recognize the worth of the Qur'an; when the Qur'an is recited to him he says "tales of the ancients," so he does not recognize its worth. Why? ﴿Nay, but what they used to earn has rusted over their hearts﴾ [al-Mutaffifin 14]. When his deeds have rusted over his heart, he becomes, may Allah protect us, unable to see this great Qur'an except as what? Except as tales of the ancients.
For this reason some scholars said: whoever is afflicted with a calamity and seeks its ruling, whether this calamity is specific to him or he is asked about it, he should seek Allah's forgiveness. They cited as evidence His saying: ﴿Indeed We have sent down to you the Book in truth, that you may judge between the people by what Allah has shown you; so do not be an advocate for the treacherous﴾ [an-Nisa 105]. What follows? ﴿And seek forgiveness from Allah; indeed Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful﴾ [an-Nisa 106]. And this is not far.
So among the benefits of faith and righteous deeds is the attainment of what is sought and deliverance from what is disliked.
* Also among the benefits of the noble verse: that the provision of Paradise is generous provision; i.e., vast, abundant, lasting and good. This is indicated by His saying: ﴿So no soul knows what has been hidden for them of comfort for eyes as reward for what they used to do﴾ [as-Sajdah 17], and His saying: ﴿And fruit in abundance, neither cut off nor forbidden﴾ [al-Waqi'ah 32–33].
Then He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿And those who strive against Our signs, seeking to frustrate them, for them is a painful punishment of a vile kind.﴾
* Derived from this verse: the realization of what Allah described the Qur'an with, that it is what?
* Student: True.
* Shaykh: No, that it is mathani (oft-repeated): when its meaning is mentioned, its opposite is mentioned, and when the doer is mentioned, the one who opposes him is mentioned.
* Also derived from it: the wisdom in address, and that address should combine causes of fear and causes of hope. Why?
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: It should combine them, because if fear alone is mentioned, despair of Allah's mercy may take hold of the heart; or hope alone, then a sense of security from Allah's plan may take hold of it, Glory be to Him.
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: that the disbelievers strive earnestly to nullify the signs of Allah, Mighty and Majestic; due to His saying: ﴿those who strive against Our signs﴾. Striving, as we know, is running with intensity; these ones strive earnestly to nullify the signs of Allah, Glory be to Him.
* Also among its benefits: that these disbelievers are as if they seek to outpace Allah and overcome Him; due to His saying: ﴿seeking to frustrate them﴾.
* Also among its benefits: that those who strive against the signs of Allah, seeking to frustrate them, are punished with this painful punishment; ﴿for them is a painful punishment﴾, and His saying: ﴿of a vile kind﴾ means: of an evil, painful punishment, as has passed for us.
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: warning against a person striving to nullify the signs of Allah. If we say, according to the rule that passed for us in the principles of tafsir the day before yesterday, that when something is forbidden, it is a command to its opposite, then this verse includes an exhortation to strive for the signs of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, to establish and confirm them. And so it is: we are commanded to strive, to the extent of our ability, in establishing and confirming the signs of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and spreading them among the Ummah until the religion is established.
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the affirmation of reward and of wisdom in it; for the believers who did righteous deeds, ﴿for them is forgiveness and generous provision﴾, and these, ﴿for them is a painful punishment of a vile kind﴾.
Then He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿And those who have been given knowledge see that what has been revealed to you from your Lord is the truth﴾, to the end.
* In this verse: the virtue of knowledge. From where is it derived?
* Students: ﴿those who have been given knowledge﴾.
* Shaykh: Yes, but the virtue of knowledge.
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: But what is the aspect by which this indicates the virtue of knowledge?
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: No.
* Student: That they see it as the truth, because Allah, Glory be to Him, has given them knowledge.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 34, verse 4–6 (part 4 of 4):

* The Shaykh: Correct. The scholar knows realities as they truly are, so he sees that what was sent down to the Messenger is the truth. There is no doubt that this is one of the virtues of knowledge, in contrast to one who wavers as to whether it is true or denies that it is true, and we seek refuge with Allah. Those whom Allah has favoured with knowledge see that it is the truth.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: an indication that a person should not be impressed by his own knowledge. From where is this taken?
* A student: (...).
* The Shaykh: ﴿And those who have been given knowledge see that what has been sent down to you from your Lord is the truth﴾.
* The student: (...).
* The Shaykh: No.
* A student: ﴿And those who see﴾; meaning: he knows...
* The Shaykh: No.
* A student: that this knowledge was sent down from Allah, the Exalted.
* The Shaykh: No.
* A student: ﴿That which was sent down to you﴾.
* The Shaykh: No, my brothers. In it is evidence that a person should not be impressed by his knowledge, due to His saying: ﴿those who have been given knowledge﴾; meaning, they did not attain it by themselves, but Allah, the Exalted, bestowed it upon them as a favour. Is it clear? Do not say: "This is from me." The same applies to wealth. Some people become impressed when they acquire wealth, yet the One who gave them the wealth is Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. And what did Allah do to the one who said: ﴿I was only given it on account of knowledge I have﴾ [al-Qasas 78]? He caused the earth to swallow him up. So ﴿those who have been given knowledge﴾ contains evidence that a person should not be impressed with himself and say: "I acquired this knowledge by my own understanding, my eagerness and my perseverance."
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that a person should turn to Allah, the Exalted, in acquiring knowledge. From where do we take this?
* A student: ﴿those who have been given knowledge﴾.
* The Shaykh: From His saying: ﴿those who have been given knowledge﴾. So if we are given knowledge, let us ask this knowledge from the One who gives it to us. Is that not so?
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that the Qur'an is the speech of Allah; ﴿sent down to you from your Lord﴾, ﴿from your Lord﴾. How is this evidence that it is the speech of Allah? Because not everything that is sent down is speech; Allah may mention the sending down of a thing that is not speech.
* A student: Because what descends from Allah is either subsisting in its own essence or subsisting in something else. That which subsists in its own essence is created, like rain and the like, whereas the Qur'an subsists in another (i.e., in the One who speaks).
* The Shaykh: Because it is speech, and speech cannot exist except from a speaker. Therefore the speech of Allah is uncreated. Is it clear, everyone? Otherwise, there are things that Allah sends down and says: "We sent them down," and they are created: ﴿He sends down water from the sky﴾ [al-An'am 99], ﴿And We sent down water from the sky﴾ [al-Mu'minun 18], ﴿And He sent down for you eight pairs of livestock﴾ [az-Zumar 6], ﴿And We sent down iron, wherein is great might﴾ [al-Hadid 25]. All of these things are created, are they not? Because they are entities subsisting in their own essence. This is unlike speech, for speech cannot exist except from a speaker. So when Allah says: ﴿He has sent down to you the Book﴾ [Al 'Imran 7], and it is speech, this speech becomes the speech of Allah.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the virtue of the Prophet ﷺ. From where is this taken?
* Students: ﴿from your Lord﴾.
* The Shaykh: From the attribution of lordship (rububiyyah) to him, and this lordship is a special one, as we also passed over in the principles of tafsir. So we say: in this is the virtue of the Prophet ﷺ.
* And among its benefits: the care of Allah for the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, by His saying: ﴿from your Lord﴾, and in it is a statement of the grace of Allah upon him, in that He sent down the truth to him.
* And among the benefits of this noble verse also: that this Qur'an is true in its reports and in its rulings. Truthfulness in reports is sincerity (sidq), and in rulings it is justice ('adl). Allah combined both in His saying: ﴿And the word of your Lord has been fulfilled in truth and justice﴾ [al-An'am 115].
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that the Qur'an is a beacon and guidance..
Among the benefits of this noble verse: that the Qur'an is a beacon and guidance by which people are guided and find light; due to His saying: ﴿and guides to the path of the Mighty, the Praiseworthy﴾ [Saba' 6].
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that whoever seeks guidance from other than it goes astray. For if it is the One who guides to the path of the Mighty, the Praiseworthy, then if you seek guidance from other than it, which opposes it, you will not be guided to the path of the Mighty, the Praiseworthy. For this reason, when the people of innovation sought to reach the Creator by a path other than the Qur'an, what befell them? They went astray, became lost, and remained bewildered and confused.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that whoever holds fast to this Qur'an attains might and praise, i.e., becomes mighty and praised; due to His saying: ﴿to the path of the Mighty, the Praiseworthy﴾. He did not say "to the path of Allah," but said: ﴿to the path of the Mighty, the Praiseworthy﴾, indicating that whoever holds fast to this Qur'an has might and has praise; he is praised for his actions, his words and his abstentions.
* And among its benefits: the affirmation of these two names of Allah, the Mighty and the Praiseworthy. We have said that the might with which Allah, the Exalted, is described has three types..
* A student: The might of subjugation (qahr), the might of decree (qadr), and the might of inaccessibility (imtina').
* The Shaykh: The might of inaccessibility, correct? The might of decree, the might of subjugation, and the might of inaccessibility, is that right? Good. Explain them.
* A student: The might of decree is that you are a person... this is a mighty person (...). As for the might of subjugation, Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿and he overpowered me in speech﴾ [Sad 23], meaning he overcame me. As for inaccessibility, you say: "This is a 'azaz land," meaning strong, hard, and unassailable.
* The Shaykh: Good, well done.
Al-Hamid is also one of the names of Allah, and it is derived from hamd (praise). Is it in the sense of the active participle or the passive participle?
(...) the might and the affirmation of praise for Allah. There is a phrase among people that says: "Praise be to Allah who is not praised for anything disliked except Him." What do you say about this phrase?
* Students: It is incorrect.
* The Shaykh: It is not appropriate, because you are making a complete declaration that you dislike what Allah has decreed. When the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, was struck by something he liked, he said: "Praise be to Allah through whose blessing good deeds are completed," and when something he disliked befell him, he said: "Praise be to Allah in every circumstance." [[Narrated by Ibn Majah (3803) from the hadith of 'A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her.]] He did not mention anything disliked. Therefore we should admonish whoever uses this phrase: say, "O brother, do not say it like this; this suggests you are not content with the decree of Allah. Say: 'Praise be to Allah in every circumstance.'"
Now, we know that Allah is the Lord of everything, and this includes dogs, pigs, insects and the like. But is it proper to say: "Allah is the Lord of dogs, the Lord of pigs, the Lord of insects"? This is not proper etiquette, to specify in this way, as Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah and others have stated. Here there is a difference between generalization and specification; for this reason the Messenger said: "Praise be to Allah in every circumstance."

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 34, verses 7–9 (part 1 of 2):

﴿And those who disbelieved said, "Shall we direct you to a man who will inform you that when you have been completely torn apart, you will be [restored] in a new creation?"﴾ [Saba': 7] and so on to the end.

First, on the grammar (i'rab) and the rhetorical meanings (balagha): ﴿هَلْ نَدُلُّكُمْ﴾ ("Shall we direct you…"): the interrogative here is intended as mockery. ﴿رَجُلٍ﴾ ("a man"): it is indefinite (nukkira) ﴿عَلَى رَجُلٍ﴾ ("to a man") in order to belittle him, meaning that he is a contemptible man. This is like the Almighty's saying about those who denied the messengers in general: ﴿أَهَذَا الَّذِي يَذْكُرُ آلِهَتَكُمْ﴾ ("Is this the one who mentions your gods?"), and His saying: ﴿أَهَذَا الَّذِي بَعَثَ اللَّهُ رَسُولًا﴾ ("Is this the one whom Allah has sent as a messenger?") [al-Furqan: 41]. This is for belittling him.

And His saying: ﴿يُنَبِّئُكُمْ﴾ ("will inform you") takes three objects: the first object is the kaf (the "you"), and the second and third objects are governed by His saying: ﴿إِنَّكُمْ لَفِي خَلْقٍ جَدِيدٍ﴾ ("that you will be in a new creation").

The Almighty says about the disbelievers that some of them say to others, in a manner of wonder, as the author said, but rather in a manner of belittling: ﴿قَالَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا﴾ ("And those who disbelieved said"), i.e., (some of them said to others, in a manner of wonder, ﴿هَلْ نَدُلُّكُمْ عَلَى رَجُلٍ﴾ ("Shall we direct you to a man"), he is Muhammad). I said the interrogative here is for mockery, but the author added another meaning, which is (wonder), meaning: Do you not wonder at what we are going to direct you to?

As for His saying: ﴿عَلَى رَجُلٍ﴾ ("to a man"), the author says: (he is Muhammad). But they said it with indefiniteness, in the manner of belittling. They did not mention him by name, because mentioning a person by name may imply exalting his status. Rather, they used this indefinite expression to belittle him.

(﴿يُنَبِّئُكُمْ﴾ "will inform you" — he informs you that you, ﴿إِذَا مُزِّقْتُمْ﴾ "when you are torn apart," are cut up, ﴿كُلَّ مُمَزَّقٍ﴾ "into utter pieces," meaning a tearing apart, ﴿إِنَّكُمْ لَفِي خَلْقٍ جَدِيدٍ﴾ "that you will be in a new creation" — this is the thing being reported.) He says: ﴿يُنَبِّئُكُمْ﴾ means "informs you" (yukhbirukum). So naba' means khabar (news/information). The naba' may be used for important matters, while khabar is more general. You may report (akhbara) about an important thing or about a trivial thing, but you do not use naba' except for something great, as in His saying: ﴿عَمَّ يَتَسَاءَلُونَ (1) عَنِ النَّبَإِ الْعَظِيمِ﴾ ("About what are they asking one another? About the great news") [al-Naba': 1–2], and He said: ﴿قُلْ هُوَ نَبَأٌ عَظِيمٌ (67) أَنْتُمْ عَنْهُ مُعْرِضُونَ﴾ ("Say: It is great news, from which you turn away") [Sad: 67–68]. So naba' may be used for great things, unlike khabar, which is more general.

As for His saying: ﴿إِذَا مُزِّقْتُمْ كُلَّ مُمَزَّقٍ﴾ ("when you have been completely torn apart"), he says: (when you are cut up). This tearing means the earth tearing apart human flesh. When a person is buried, the earth tears him apart, and his solid bones become crumbled dust (ramim). So they say: ﴿يُنَبِّئُكُمْ إِذَا مُزِّقْتُمْ كُلَّ مُمَزَّقٍ﴾. The author said: (meaning a tearing), and on this basis the word (mumazzaq) is a masdar (verbal noun) of the form mimmi (مميميٌ, a mīmī verbal noun).

As for His saying: ﴿إِنَّكُمْ لَفِي خَلْقٍ جَدِيدٍ﴾, this is the locus of the news, and it is in the accusative position, filling the role of the second and third objects of ﴿يُنَبِّئُكُمْ﴾.

As for His saying: ﴿إِذَا مُزِّقْتُمْ﴾, the word ﴿إِذَا﴾ here is temporal (zarfiyyah). Is it connected to ﴿يُنَبِّئُكُمْ﴾, or to something omitted that is indicated by the context? The latter, because the Prophet's (ﷺ) informing them was not at the time of their being torn apart. Rather, he informed them during the life of this world. Their being torn apart is when they are buried. The meaning is: when you are buried and torn apart, you will be in a new creation. This new creation is the resurrection (al-ba'th). Is the resurrection a restoration of what has passed, or the beginning of a creation different from the first? The correct view is that it is a restoration of what has passed, as Allah the Almighty said: ﴿وَهُوَ الَّذِي يَبْدَأُ الْخَلْقَ ثُمَّ يُعِيدُهُ﴾ ("It is He who originates creation and then repeats it") [al-Rum: 27]. But it is called a "new creation" because when a person is resurrected, he is not raised in his state of the world. Rather, he is raised in a state that is stronger and more powerful, because when he is resurrected he will be in a stronger state, since he will be raised as one who is everlasting and does not die. For this reason, on the Day of Resurrection people will endure distress, anxiety and grief that they do not endure in this world. For example, if the sun were to come close to people in this world by the distance of a mile, it would burn them. But in the Hereafter, it will draw near to them and yet not burn them.

He says: ﴿إِنَّكُمْ لَفِي خَلْقٍ جَدِيدٍ﴾. So new in what respect? New in its essence and its parts, or in its attributes?

In its attributes, because the correct view is that creation is a restoration of what has passed (...).

﴿أَفْتَرَى﴾ ("Has he invented…") with a fatha on the hamza, for the interrogative, and it is used in place of the hamzat al-wasl (the connecting hamza). The original form is (a-iftara), but the hamzat al-wasl drops when it is combined with the hamzat al-istifham (interrogative hamza). An example is also His saying: ﴿أَصْطَفَى الْبَنَاتِ عَلَى الْبَنِينَ﴾ ("Has He chosen daughters over sons?") [al-Saffat: 153]. ﴿أَصْطَفَى﴾ means a-istafa, so the hamza drops, because it came after the interrogative hamza. I think its dropping is well known, because the hamzat al-wasl drops in connected speech, and when the interrogative hamza comes, the speech becomes connected, and when it is connected, the hamzat al-wasl drops.

﴿أَوْحَيْنَا إِلَيْهِ أَنِ اصْنَعِ الْفُلْكَ﴾ ("We revealed to him: construct the ship") [al-Mu'minun: 27]. Where did the hamzat al-wasl go in ﴿اصْنَعِ﴾? It dropped because the speech is connected. So ﴿أَفْتَرَى﴾ dropped its hamzat al-wasl because the speech is connected.

(﴿أَفْتَرَى عَلَى اللَّهِ كَذِبًا﴾ "Has he invented a lie against Allah," in that) meaning: in his saying that you will be resurrected and brought forth in a new creation. Is this a fabrication against Allah? Allah will make that clear. But they say that his condition is confined to one of two matters: either he is a man who fabricates against Allah (﴿أَفْتَرَى عَلَى اللَّهِ كَذِبًا﴾ "Has he invented a lie against Allah"), ﴿أَمْ بِهِ جِنَّةٌ﴾ ("or is there madness in him?"), i.e., madness through which he imagined that. So they—may Allah protect us—divided the state of the Prophet (ﷺ) into two states with no third, which are fabrication against Allah and madness.

(﴿أَمْ بِهِ جِنَّةٌ﴾ "or is there madness in him," i.e., madness that imagined that to him.) Is there a third state? Yes, there is a third state, but they do not acknowledge it, which is that he is truthful and sane. He is truthful and did not fabricate, and he is sane and has no madness. This is the reality. But they, may Allah protect us, dropped this third category because they do not acknowledge it. It is strange that these people who describe the Messenger (ﷺ) with this attribute, that he is either a fabricator, a madman, a poet, a soothsayer or something similar, used to call him before prophethood "the trustworthy" (al-Amin), and they considered him one of the most truthful of people and the greatest in trustworthiness. But—may Allah protect us—when he came with what did not agree with their desires, they began to give him these epithets. These bad epithets with which the polytheists titled the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) were inherited by whom? They were inherited by the enemies of the believers and the allies of the criminals, as Allah the Almighty said: ﴿إِنَّ الَّذِينَ أَجْرَمُوا كَانُوا مِنَ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا يَضْحَكُونَ (29) وَإِذَا مَرُّوا بِهِمْ يَتَغَامَزُونَ﴾ ("Indeed, those who committed crimes used to laugh at those who believed. And when they passed by them, they would wink at one another") [al-Mutaffifin: 29–30]. So these bad epithets exist now. All enemies of the messengers title the allies of the messengers with the same epithets with which the messengers were titled.

You know that it has passed us in 'Aqidah (creed) that some people title the people of the Sunnah and the Jama'ah (the followers of the Sunnah and the community) with what? With al-Hashwiyyah, al-Nawabit, al-Ghuthha' (scum), al-Mujassimah (anthropomorphists) and similar terms. All of this is to repel people from following their school.

He says: ﴿أَمْ بِهِ جِنَّةٌ﴾. Allah the Almighty said, nullifying that: (﴿بَلِ الَّذِينَ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ بِالْآخِرَةِ﴾ "Rather, those who do not believe in the Hereafter," which includes the resurrection and the punishment).

﴿فِي الْعَذَابِ وَالضَّلَالِ الْبَعِيدِ﴾ ("are in punishment and far error") (﴿فِي الْعَذَابِ﴾ "in the punishment" in it, ﴿وَالضَّلَالِ الْبَعِيدِ﴾ "and far error," from the truth in this world).

His saying: ﴿بَلِ﴾ ("Rather") is for idrab (a turn or change in the discourse). Is it the idrab ibṭālī (nullifying idrab) or the idrab intiqālī (transitional idrab)? It is the nullifying idrab. The nullifying idrab means that what came before "bal" is false. The transitional idrab means that what came before "bal" is a stage from which one moves to another stage without nullifying it. Here, ﴿بَلِ﴾ is nullifying idrab. That is, Allah nullified these two categories between which these disbelievers vacillated regarding the Prophet's (ﷺ) condition. The meaning is: rather, he is not a fabricator and there is no madness in him. But those who do not believe are in punishment and far error, and we cannot acknowledge them (in that). An example of transitional idrab is His saying: ﴿بَلِ ادَّارَكَ عِلْمُهُمْ فِي الْآخِرَةِ بَلْ هُمْ فِي شَكٍّ مِنْهَا بَلْ هُمْ مِنْهَا عَمُونَ﴾ ("Rather, their knowledge has failed concerning the Hereafter. Rather, they are in doubt about it. Rather, they are blind to it") [al-Naml: 66]. This is transitional: their knowledge of the Hereafter first fell short, then they doubted it, then after that they became blind to it, may Allah protect us. These are their transitional states.

Allah said: ﴿بَلِ الَّذِينَ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ بِالْآخِرَةِ﴾, i.e., they do not affirm it or acknowledge it.

* A student: O Shaykh, did we not say (bal) means (aw)?
* The Shaykh: It sometimes comes like ﴿أَوْ يَزِيدُونَ﴾ ("or they increase") [al-Saffat: 147].

He said: ﴿بَلِ الَّذِينَ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ بِالْآخِرَةِ﴾, i.e., they do not believe in its existence and do not believe in what takes place in it. It has already passed us that the Last Day includes everything the Prophet (ﷺ) informed about that occurs after death. So everything the Messenger informed about that occurs after death, such as the trial of the grave, its bliss and its punishment, is included in the Hereafter.

He said: (which includes the resurrection and the punishment, ﴿فِي الْعَذَابِ﴾ "in the punishment" in it, ﴿وَالضَّلَالِ الْبَعِيدِ﴾ "and far error" from the truth in this world). The author, may Allah have mercy on him, restricted the absolute in the two places here. Allah said: ﴿فِي الْعَذَابِ﴾ and the author said: (in the Hereafter), and He said: ﴿وَالضَّلَالِ الْبَعِيدِ﴾ and the author said: (in this world). The more correct view is that the verse is absolute: they are in punishment in this world and in the Hereafter. As for the punishment of the Hereafter, it is obvious. As for the punishment of this world, it is the distress and constriction in their hearts, and the punishment they receive from Allah the Almighty, as He said: ﴿فَكُلًّا أَخَذْنَا بِذَنْبِهِ فَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ أَرْسَلْنَا عَلَيْهِ حَاصِبًا وَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ أَخَذَتْهُ الصَّيْحَةُ وَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ خَسَفْنَا بِهِ الْأَرْضَ وَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ أَغْرَقْنَا﴾ ("So We seized each one for his sin. Among them were those upon whom We sent a storm of pebbles, and among them were those who were seized by the blast, and among them were those whom We caused the earth to swallow, and among them were those whom We drowned") [al-'Ankabut: 40]. Likewise, the punishment that takes place at the hands of the messengers, such as the punishment that befalls them through defeats, is from the punishment of this world. As for the Hereafter, it is obvious.

So ﴿فِي الْعَذَابِ﴾ includes this world and the Hereafter. Restricting it to the Hereafter is questionable. Indeed, it is befitting for us, and it is obligatory upon us, not to restrict anything that Allah has left absolute except by evidence from the Book of Allah, the Sunnah of His Messenger (ﷺ), or consensus (ijma').

As for His saying: ﴿الضَّلَالِ الْبَعِيدِ﴾, he says: (in this world). So they are in far error from the truth. They are also in error in the Hereafter, for they are not guided to the path by which whoever crosses it is saved from the Fire. Rather, they are guided to the path of Hellfire, and so they go astray from the path by which salvation comes. Allah the Almighty said: ﴿احْشُرُوا الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا وَأَزْوَاجَهُمْ وَمَا كَانُوا يَعْبُدُونَ (22) مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ فَاهْدُوهُمْ إِلَى صِرَاطِ الْجَحِيمِ﴾ ("Gather those who did wrong and their companions and what they used to worship besides Allah, and lead them to the path of Hellfire") [al-Saffat: 22–23]. And He, glorified and exalted, said about the believers: ﴿نُورُهُمْ يَسْعَى بَيْنَ أَيْدِيهِمْ وَبِأَيْمَانِهِمْ﴾ ("Their light running before them and on their right") [al-Tahrim: 8]. This indicates that error exists in the Hereafter just as it exists in this world. Therefore, it is better to leave the text on its generality, both in this world and in the Hereafter.

Then Allah the Almighty said: (﴿أَفَلَمْ يَرَوْا﴾ "Have they not looked" means: they have not looked ﴿إِلَى مَا بَيْنَ أَيْدِيهِمْ وَمَا خَلْفَهُمْ﴾ "at what is before them and what is behind them," what is above them and what is below them, ﴿مِنَ السَّمَاءِ وَالْأَرْضِ إِنْ نَشَأْ نَخْسِفْ بِهِمُ الْأَرْضَ أَوْ نُسْقِطْ عَلَيْهِمْ كِسَفًا مِنَ السَّمَاءِ﴾ "from the heaven and the earth. If We will, We cause the earth to swallow them, or We drop upon them fragments from the sky") and so on to the end.

The interrogative here is for threat. The meaning is that Allah threatened those who denied the Prophet (ﷺ) in his saying that they would be resurrected. He threatened them with one of two matters: being swallowed by the earth, or having fragments (kisaf), i.e., pieces of punishment, dropped on them from above. He mentioned above and below only because they cannot escape from them. As for right, left, behind and in front, escape is possible. If an enemy comes at you from behind, you can flee forward, and if he comes from the front, you can flee backward. But if he comes from below, where will you go? You will jump, and you cannot. And if he comes from above, where will you go? You cannot. For this reason Allah threatened them with two matters from which they cannot escape.

As for the author's saying: (Have they not looked), he explained ﴿يَرَوْا﴾ as meaning (look). It is better that it include both sight, meaning looking, and the inner sight, meaning knowledge and reflection. That is, Almighty Allah urges them to reflect with an urging intended as a threat. So the seeing here includes seeing with the eye and seeing with the heart through reflection.

As for His saying: ﴿إِلَى مَا بَيْنَ أَيْدِيهِمْ وَمَا خَلْفَهُمْ﴾, the author also explained it: (what is above them and what is below them). Well, what is "between the hands"? According to the author's statement, if it is a rhetorical arrangement (laff wa nashr murattab, where the order of the items matches), then what is above them is what is "between their hands," and what is behind them is what is below them.

But someone may say: this is diverting the speech from its apparent meaning without evidence. Rather, we say: ﴿إِلَى مَا بَيْنَ أَيْدِيهِمْ﴾ means what is in front of them, and ﴿وَمَا خَلْفَهُمْ﴾ means what is behind their backs. So it is possible that what is meant by ﴿مَا بَيْنَ أَيْدِيهِمْ﴾ is what is in front of them in time, and it is possible that what is meant by ﴿مَا بَيْنَ أَيْدِيهِمْ﴾ is in place. And we say the same about what is behind them.

What is "between the hands" may be what is in front of you in time, and what is behind you is what you have left behind in time, as in His saying: ﴿يَعْلَمُ مَا بَيْنَ أَيْدِيهِمْ وَمَا خَلْفَهُمْ﴾ ("He knows what is before them and what is behind them") [al-Baqarah: 255], i.e., ﴿مَا بَيْنَ أَيْدِيهِمْ﴾ is what is to come, and ﴿وَمَا خَلْفَهُمْ﴾ is what has passed. It may also be about place, as when you say: "I passed between the hands of the one praying," meaning in front of him. And you say: "The follower stands behind the imam," meaning behind him. Is that in place or in time? In place.

Here, ﴿أَفَلَمْ يَرَوْا إِلَى مَا بَيْنَ أَيْدِيهِمْ وَمَا خَلْفَهُمْ﴾: we say it is possible that place is meant, and it is possible that time is meant. The purpose is that they should reflect on the matter: has anyone escaped the punishment of Allah? Look at what is before you in place or in time, and what is behind you in place or in time: has anyone escaped the punishment of Allah?

The answer: No, no one has escaped. So they too do not escape the punishment of Allah.

﴿إِنْ نَشَأْ نَخْسِفْ بِهِمُ الْأَرْضَ﴾: the sentence here is conditional. The protasis (fi'l al-shart) and its apodosis are in the present tense, in the jussive mood: ﴿إِنْ نَشَأْ نَخْسِفْ﴾ ("If We will, We cause to swallow").

His saying: ﴿أَوْ نُسْقِطْ﴾ ("or We drop") is conjoined to ﴿نَخْسِفْ﴾, meaning: or if We will, We drop upon them fragments (kisaf).

The author said in a reading: (with the sīn sakin and fatha: a piece). This means there are two canonical readings: ﴿كِسْفًا﴾ with a sukun on the sīn, and ﴿كِسَفًا﴾ with a fatha on the sīn. It is permissible to recite both. We have previously said that when readings are multiple, it is better to recite this one at times and that one at other times, because all of them are true. Committing to one reading alone is a deficiency, except that readings whose authenticity you are not certain of are not permissible for you to recite, because you must recite what has been established for you.

He said: ﴿كِسَفًا مِنَ السَّمَاءِ﴾. In one reading, the three verbs are with the yā' (third-person). Where are the three verbs? ﴿نَشَأْ﴾, ﴿نَخْسِفْ﴾, ﴿نُسْقِطْ﴾ with yā', so it is said: ﴿إِنْ يَشَأْ يَخْسِفْ بِهِمُ الْأَرْضَ أَوْ يُسْقِطْ عَلَيْهِمْ كِسَفًا مِنَ السَّمَاءِ﴾ ("If He wills, He causes the earth to swallow them, or He drops upon them fragments from the sky"). The subject of the pronouns here refers back to Allah the Almighty. As for the reading with nūn, ﴿إِنْ نَشَأْ﴾, the matter is clear, because the pronoun in it is a first-person pronoun. But on the reading with yā', the pronoun is a third-person pronoun, and a third-person pronoun must have a referent, either preceding or following. So where is the referent of the pronoun in ﴿إِنْ يَشَأْ﴾? It is said that it is known from the context, as in His saying: ﴿وَخُلِقَ الْإِنْسَانُ ضَعِيفًا﴾ ("and man was created weak") [al-Nisa': 28]. Who created him? Allah. Here everyone knows that no one among humans or non-humans can cause the earth to swallow people or drop upon them pieces of punishment. So the referent of the pronoun is known from the context.

As for His saying: (﴿إِنَّ فِي ذَلِكَ﴾ "Indeed, in that" which is seen ﴿لَآيَةً لِكُلِّ عَبْدٍ مُنِيبٍ﴾ "is a sign for every servant who turns back [to his Lord]," indicating Allah's power over resurrection) and so on to the end. That is: the verse indicates the resurrection.

﴿Indeed, in that﴾, meaning in what lies before them of the heavens and the earth, ﴿is a sign for every servant who turns back (to Allah)﴾. We have mentioned that "what is before them and behind them" of the heavens and the earth includes everything that came before and everything that has passed, and everything in front of them of place and everything behind them. Among that, we see the sign in the sky: rain descends from the sky onto the dry, barren earth, and it returns green and alive. Is there not in this a proof of the possibility of the re-creation of creation? The answer is: yes. For this reason He said: ﴿Indeed, in that﴾, meaning in what is seen of what is before us and behind us of the heavens and the earth, ﴿is a sign﴾, meaning an indication of the power of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and of His knowledge and wisdom. But this sign is not a sign for everyone; rather, it is ﴿for every servant who turns back﴾.

﴿Servant (ʿabd)﴾ is derived from servitude (ʿubudiyyah), which is humility (tadhallul). We have already mentioned that humility is of two kinds: humility before the legislative command (al-amr al-shar'i), and humility before the universal command (al-amr al-kawni). Which of them is praiseworthy and rewarded? Humility before the legislative command. As for humility before the universal command, a person has no power over it and it is not praised: a person's submission to Allah's universal command, such as sickness, poverty, the death of a family member or the like, is not praised, because it is not his own action. But his submission to Allah's legislative command, so that he performs the laws of Allah, this is what is praised.

Here, is the intended meaning of "servant" the one who is humbled before the universal or the legislative command? The legislative. Evidence for this is His saying: ﴿who turns back﴾, meaning returns to Allah, the Glorified and Exalted, returns to Allah from disobedience to obedience. It includes one who stands in worship even without having committed a sin, and it includes one who repents from sin. When a man stands to pray, worshipping Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, it is said that he has turned back to Allah; and if he commits a sin, then seeks forgiveness and returns, it is also said that he has turned back to Allah. So turning back here includes turning back from a sin one committed, in which case it means repentance, and it includes turning back to Allah by standing in obedience to Him, in which case it is more comprehensive and general.

In His saying: ﴿Have they not looked at what is before them﴾ (and this is a point I forgot to mention) there is an issue of i'rab (grammatical analysis) on which the grammarians differ. The grammarians differed over the analysis of a sentence that begins with the interrogative hamza followed by a conjunction particle. It was said: the hamza, meaning the interrogative hamza, enters upon something implied according to the context. And it was said: the hamza enters upon the sentence that is present, without any implied element, and the conjunction particle should have preceded the hamza, but it was placed after it because the hamza has priority of position.

According to the first view, the implied element in His saying ﴿Have they not looked at what is before them and what is behind them﴾ would be: "Were they heedless?" or "Did they turn away?" or the like.

As for the second view, there is no need for this implied element. Rather, we say: the hamza is interrogative, the fa' is a conjunction particle, and it has been placed after the hamza because the hamza has priority. Which is better?

The second is better. That is, our saying that the hamza enters upon this sentence itself is preferable, because the first view may cause you difficulty in estimating the omitted element, meaning it is hard for you to estimate what is omitted. But this view, based on the premise that this sentence is conjoined to what came before, does not need an implied element, so you do not toil over it.

Then Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿And We had certainly given Dawud a bounty from Us﴾ [Saba' 10]. The waw is a conjunction particle, and it may be for beginning a new statement (istinaf). The lam is an introductory lam for an oath.

* A student: (...).
* The Shaykh: How?
* The student: (...).
* The Shaykh: No, (...). The lam is an introductory lam for an oath, and (qad) is for emphasis confirmation. This construction comes often in the Qur'an, and it is said that the sentence is emphasized with three emphases: the implied oath, the lam, and (qad). So the implied form of this sentence is "By Allah, indeed We had given Dawud a bounty from Us." Is it permissible to omit the lam? Yes, it is permissible. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿By the sun and its brightness, and by the moon when it follows it, and by the day when it displays it, and by the night when it covers it, and by the sky and He who constructed it﴾ [al-Shams 1–5], up to His saying: ﴿He has certainly succeeded who purified it﴾. This is the answer to the oath. And in ﴿He has certainly succeeded who purified it﴾, outside the Qur'an, we may say: "laqad aflaha" (indeed he has succeeded). Fine. And is it permissible to omit the lam and (qad)? Yes, as in His saying: ﴿By the sky containing great stars, and by the promised day, and by the witness and the witnessed, "Killed were the companions of the trench"﴾ [al-Buruj 1–4]. So ﴿Killed﴾ is the answer to the oath, and it contains neither (qad) nor the lam. So when the answer to the oath is a past-tense verb, three possibilities are permitted: it may be joined with the lam and (qad); it may be joined with (qad); or the lam and (qad) may be omitted. But generally neither the lam nor (qad) is omitted unless the oath is long; if it is not long, they are not omitted.

If you say: "Wallahi, laqad qama Zayd" (By Allah, indeed Zayd stood up), is that correct? Correct, and this is the original form. "Wallahi qad qama Zayd" is also correct; we omitted the lam. "Wallahi qama Zayd" is also correct; we omitted from it the lam and qad. And Allah knows best.

(...)

* Among the benefits of this noble verse, ﴿And those who disbelieved said: "Shall we direct you to a man who will inform you"﴾ [Saba' 7] to the end: that the Prophet (ﷺ) called to belief in the Last Day. From where is this taken? From His saying: ﴿"He will inform you that when you are completely torn apart, you will be in a new creation."﴾

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the demonstration of the arrogance of the disbelievers, their haughtiness and their pride, in that they expressed themselves in this manner, mocking what the Prophet (ﷺ) reported. Their arrogance and pride appear in three aspects:
First, mockery of this news.
Second, belittling the Prophet (ﷺ).
Third, describing him as being in one of two states: either a liar or a madman. These are three aspects, all of which indicate the haughtiness and stubbornness of these disbelievers.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the demonstration of the harm the Prophet (ﷺ) suffered, and that he was patient. For a matter that reaches this degree of belittling him and disregarding his report undoubtedly affects his soul profoundly. I believe that when the caller to the message is harmed in this manner, it is more severe for him than being beaten or imprisoned.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the demonstration of the power of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, who will recreate this creation after it has been torn into every kind of tearing apart, because this is evident from His saying: ﴿He will inform you that when you are completely torn apart﴾.

* Among its benefits: that the disbelievers who disbelieved in the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to acknowledge Allah. From where is this taken? ﴿Has he invented a lie against Allah?﴾

* Among its benefits: the demonstration of the ugliness of fabricating lies against Allah, to the extent that the disbelievers consider it ugly, as shown by His saying: ﴿Has he invented a lie against Allah?﴾

* Among the benefits of this noble verse also: that the enemies of the messengers, indeed the enemies of the message of the messengers, pour out insults, slander and defamation against what the messengers brought, or against the messengers and what they brought. This is shown by their saying: ﴿Has he invented a lie against Allah, or is there madness in him?﴾. It is well known that the speech of a liar and the speech of a madman are not accepted. So they resort to expressions of distortion and disparagement so that the truth will not be accepted. And does this continue to our time? Yes, it continues to our time, because the enemies of the message of the messengers will continue until the Day of Resurrection. But the followers of the messengers must be patient, and such words must not weaken their resolve, because they are upon the truth, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, you are upon the clear truth﴾ [al-Naml 79].

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the demonstration that Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, has undertaken to make the truth manifest and to nullify falsehood and cause it to be routed; this is shown by His saying: ﴿Rather, those who do not believe in the Hereafter are in punishment and far error﴾.

* Among its benefits also: that disbelief necessitates the non-acceptance of the truth and not being guided by it. This is derived from His saying: ﴿in punishment and far error﴾. The "fi" (in) here denotes enclosure, and its meaning is that error surrounds them from every side. For this reason Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And We turn their hearts and their sight, as they did not believe in it the first time, and We leave them in their transgression, wandering blindly﴾ [al-An'am 110]. So when a person does not believe in the truth, he remains in error. The evidences for this are numerous. Listen to this verse and to His saying the Exalted: ﴿Rather, they denied the truth when it came to them, so they are in a confused matter﴾ [Qaf 5], meaning: disordered and confused. So everyone who denies the truth increases only in error, even if clear and manifest signs come to him, for he does not benefit from them, ﴿And as for those in whose hearts is a disease, it adds to their filth, upon their filth, and they die while they are disbelievers﴾ [al-Tawbah 125], even though they are clear and evident signs.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: ﴿Have they not looked at what is before them and what is behind them﴾: the obligation of reflection and taking lessons from the signs that exist in the heavens and the earth. This is shown by His saying: ﴿Have they not looked at what is before them and what is behind them of the heavens and the earth?﴾, because this interrogation is for rebuke, and one is only rebuked for abandoning an obligation.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that there are signs in the heavens and the earth, but for whom? For the servant who turns back to Allah. As for one who does not want to turn back to his Lord, he does not benefit from these signs, even if he sees them, contemplates them and reflects upon them; he does not benefit.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the affirmation of Allah's will; this is shown by His saying: ﴿If We will, We shall cause the earth to swallow them﴾.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse also: that what occurs of earth-swallowing, earthquakes and calamities happens by the permission of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, as a punishment for the servants and as a lesson. This is unlike those who say that these are natural matters that do not indicate the anger of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, nor His warning, as is the view of one who does not believe in Allah. So earth-swallowing is a punishment, and what comes of thunderbolts and horizon-wide disasters is also a punishment. For this reason He said: ﴿If We will, We shall cause the earth to swallow them, or cause pieces of the sky to fall upon them﴾.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that Allah the Exalted encompasses the servants, and they cannot escape His decree and His destiny; Allah the Exalted encompasses everything, and there is no escape for the servants from Him. This is shown by His saying: ﴿We shall cause the earth to swallow them, or cause pieces of the sky to fall upon them﴾.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, bestows favor upon the servant by making the signs manifest to him so that the truth becomes clear to him; this is shown by His saying: ﴿Indeed in that is a sign for every servant who turns back﴾. When Allah bestows upon the servant the favor of contemplating His signs and reflecting upon them, his faith in Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, increases, and his faith in what these signs require of His attributes increases too, for each sign indicates a specific attribute of Allah. The sending down of rain indicates power, knowledge and mercy; its occurring at a suitable time indicates wisdom. Everything that happens in the heavens and the earth indicates an attribute of Allah, the Exalted, that fits it.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that there are great signs in the heavens and the earth for whoever looks and reflects. Allah, the Glorified and Exalted, affirmed this in the Qur'an in many places: ﴿And in the earth are signs for those who are certain﴾ [al-Dhariyat 20]; ﴿And in the earth are neighboring tracts, and gardens of grapes, crops, and palm trees, some with multiple trunks and some with single trunks, watered with one water, yet We make some of them exceed others in fruit. Indeed in that are signs for a people who reason﴾ [al-Ra'd 4]. Verses with this meaning are numerous. Whoever reflects on what is in the heavens, what is in the earth, and what is between them, Allah's signs will become clear to him, which strengthen his faith and increase his hope in Allah's bounty and his fear of His punishment.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 34, verses 7–9 (part 1 of 2):

﴿And those who disbelieved said, "Shall we direct you to a man who will inform you that when you have been completely torn apart, you will be [restored] in a new creation?"﴾ [Saba': 7] and so on to the end.

First, on the grammar (i'rab) and the rhetorical meanings (balagha): ﴿هَلْ نَدُلُّكُمْ﴾ ("Shall we direct you…"): the interrogative here is intended as mockery. ﴿رَجُلٍ﴾ ("a man"): it is indefinite (nukkira) ﴿عَلَى رَجُلٍ﴾ ("to a man") in order to belittle him, meaning that he is a contemptible man. This is like the Almighty's saying about those who denied the messengers in general: ﴿أَهَذَا الَّذِي يَذْكُرُ آلِهَتَكُمْ﴾ ("Is this the one who mentions your gods?"), and His saying: ﴿أَهَذَا الَّذِي بَعَثَ اللَّهُ رَسُولًا﴾ ("Is this the one whom Allah has sent as a messenger?") [al-Furqan: 41]. This is for belittling him.

And His saying: ﴿يُنَبِّئُكُمْ﴾ ("will inform you") takes three objects: the first object is the kaf (the "you"), and the second and third objects are governed by His saying: ﴿إِنَّكُمْ لَفِي خَلْقٍ جَدِيدٍ﴾ ("that you will be in a new creation").

The Almighty says about the disbelievers that some of them say to others, in a manner of wonder, as the author said, but rather in a manner of belittling: ﴿قَالَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا﴾ ("And those who disbelieved said"), i.e., (some of them said to others, in a manner of wonder, ﴿هَلْ نَدُلُّكُمْ عَلَى رَجُلٍ﴾ ("Shall we direct you to a man"), he is Muhammad). I said the interrogative here is for mockery, but the author added another meaning, which is (wonder), meaning: Do you not wonder at what we are going to direct you to?

As for His saying: ﴿عَلَى رَجُلٍ﴾ ("to a man"), the author says: (he is Muhammad). But they said it with indefiniteness, in the manner of belittling. They did not mention him by name, because mentioning a person by name may imply exalting his status. Rather, they used this indefinite expression to belittle him.

(﴿يُنَبِّئُكُمْ﴾ "will inform you" — he informs you that you, ﴿إِذَا مُزِّقْتُمْ﴾ "when you are torn apart," are cut up, ﴿كُلَّ مُمَزَّقٍ﴾ "into utter pieces," meaning a tearing apart, ﴿إِنَّكُمْ لَفِي خَلْقٍ جَدِيدٍ﴾ "that you will be in a new creation" — this is the thing being reported.) He says: ﴿يُنَبِّئُكُمْ﴾ means "informs you" (yukhbirukum). So naba' means khabar (news/information). The naba' may be used for important matters, while khabar is more general. You may report (akhbara) about an important thing or about a trivial thing, but you do not use naba' except for something great, as in His saying: ﴿عَمَّ يَتَسَاءَلُونَ (1) عَنِ النَّبَإِ الْعَظِيمِ﴾ ("About what are they asking one another? About the great news") [al-Naba': 1–2], and He said: ﴿قُلْ هُوَ نَبَأٌ عَظِيمٌ (67) أَنْتُمْ عَنْهُ مُعْرِضُونَ﴾ ("Say: It is great news, from which you turn away") [Sad: 67–68]. So naba' may be used for great things, unlike khabar, which is more general.

As for His saying: ﴿إِذَا مُزِّقْتُمْ كُلَّ مُمَزَّقٍ﴾ ("when you have been completely torn apart"), he says: (when you are cut up). This tearing means the earth tearing apart human flesh. When a person is buried, the earth tears him apart, and his solid bones become crumbled dust (ramim). So they say: ﴿يُنَبِّئُكُمْ إِذَا مُزِّقْتُمْ كُلَّ مُمَزَّقٍ﴾. The author said: (meaning a tearing), and on this basis the word (mumazzaq) is a masdar (verbal noun) of the form mimmi (مميميٌ, a mīmī verbal noun).

As for His saying: ﴿إِنَّكُمْ لَفِي خَلْقٍ جَدِيدٍ﴾, this is the locus of the news, and it is in the accusative position, filling the role of the second and third objects of ﴿يُنَبِّئُكُمْ﴾.

As for His saying: ﴿إِذَا مُزِّقْتُمْ﴾, the word ﴿إِذَا﴾ here is temporal (zarfiyyah). Is it connected to ﴿يُنَبِّئُكُمْ﴾, or to something omitted that is indicated by the context? The latter, because the Prophet's (ﷺ) informing them was not at the time of their being torn apart. Rather, he informed them during the life of this world. Their being torn apart is when they are buried. The meaning is: when you are buried and torn apart, you will be in a new creation. This new creation is the resurrection (al-ba'th). Is the resurrection a restoration of what has passed, or the beginning of a creation different from the first? The correct view is that it is a restoration of what has passed, as Allah the Almighty said: ﴿وَهُوَ الَّذِي يَبْدَأُ الْخَلْقَ ثُمَّ يُعِيدُهُ﴾ ("It is He who originates creation and then repeats it") [al-Rum: 27]. But it is called a "new creation" because when a person is resurrected, he is not raised in his state of the world. Rather, he is raised in a state that is stronger and more powerful, because when he is resurrected he will be in a stronger state, since he will be raised as one who is everlasting and does not die. For this reason, on the Day of Resurrection people will endure distress, anxiety and grief that they do not endure in this world. For example, if the sun were to come close to people in this world by the distance of a mile, it would burn them. But in the Hereafter, it will draw near to them and yet not burn them.

He says: ﴿إِنَّكُمْ لَفِي خَلْقٍ جَدِيدٍ﴾. So new in what respect? New in its essence and its parts, or in its attributes?

In its attributes, because the correct view is that creation is a restoration of what has passed (...).

﴿أَفْتَرَى﴾ ("Has he invented…") with a fatha on the hamza, for the interrogative, and it is used in place of the hamzat al-wasl (the connecting hamza). The original form is (a-iftara), but the hamzat al-wasl drops when it is combined with the hamzat al-istifham (interrogative hamza). An example is also His saying: ﴿أَصْطَفَى الْبَنَاتِ عَلَى الْبَنِينَ﴾ ("Has He chosen daughters over sons?") [al-Saffat: 153]. ﴿أَصْطَفَى﴾ means a-istafa, so the hamza drops, because it came after the interrogative hamza. I think its dropping is well known, because the hamzat al-wasl drops in connected speech, and when the interrogative hamza comes, the speech becomes connected, and when it is connected, the hamzat al-wasl drops.

﴿أَوْحَيْنَا إِلَيْهِ أَنِ اصْنَعِ الْفُلْكَ﴾ ("We revealed to him: construct the ship") [al-Mu'minun: 27]. Where did the hamzat al-wasl go in ﴿اصْنَعِ﴾? It dropped because the speech is connected. So ﴿أَفْتَرَى﴾ dropped its hamzat al-wasl because the speech is connected.

(﴿أَفْتَرَى عَلَى اللَّهِ كَذِبًا﴾ "Has he invented a lie against Allah," in that) meaning: in his saying that you will be resurrected and brought forth in a new creation. Is this a fabrication against Allah? Allah will make that clear. But they say that his condition is confined to one of two matters: either he is a man who fabricates against Allah (﴿أَفْتَرَى عَلَى اللَّهِ كَذِبًا﴾ "Has he invented a lie against Allah"), ﴿أَمْ بِهِ جِنَّةٌ﴾ ("or is there madness in him?"), i.e., madness through which he imagined that. So they—may Allah protect us—divided the state of the Prophet (ﷺ) into two states with no third, which are fabrication against Allah and madness.

(﴿أَمْ بِهِ جِنَّةٌ﴾ "or is there madness in him," i.e., madness that imagined that to him.) Is there a third state? Yes, there is a third state, but they do not acknowledge it, which is that he is truthful and sane. He is truthful and did not fabricate, and he is sane and has no madness. This is the reality. But they, may Allah protect us, dropped this third category because they do not acknowledge it. It is strange that these people who describe the Messenger (ﷺ) with this attribute, that he is either a fabricator, a madman, a poet, a soothsayer or something similar, used to call him before prophethood "the trustworthy" (al-Amin), and they considered him one of the most truthful of people and the greatest in trustworthiness. But—may Allah protect us—when he came with what did not agree with their desires, they began to give him these epithets. These bad epithets with which the polytheists titled the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) were inherited by whom? They were inherited by the enemies of the believers and the allies of the criminals, as Allah the Almighty said: ﴿إِنَّ الَّذِينَ أَجْرَمُوا كَانُوا مِنَ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا يَضْحَكُونَ (29) وَإِذَا مَرُّوا بِهِمْ يَتَغَامَزُونَ﴾ ("Indeed, those who committed crimes used to laugh at those who believed. And when they passed by them, they would wink at one another") [al-Mutaffifin: 29–30]. So these bad epithets exist now. All enemies of the messengers title the allies of the messengers with the same epithets with which the messengers were titled.

You know that it has passed us in 'Aqidah (creed) that some people title the people of the Sunnah and the Jama'ah (the followers of the Sunnah and the community) with what? With al-Hashwiyyah, al-Nawabit, al-Ghuthha' (scum), al-Mujassimah (anthropomorphists) and similar terms. All of this is to repel people from following their school.

He says: ﴿أَمْ بِهِ جِنَّةٌ﴾. Allah the Almighty said, nullifying that: (﴿بَلِ الَّذِينَ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ بِالْآخِرَةِ﴾ "Rather, those who do not believe in the Hereafter," which includes the resurrection and the punishment).

﴿فِي الْعَذَابِ وَالضَّلَالِ الْبَعِيدِ﴾ ("are in punishment and far error") (﴿فِي الْعَذَابِ﴾ "in the punishment" in it, ﴿وَالضَّلَالِ الْبَعِيدِ﴾ "and far error," from the truth in this world).

His saying: ﴿بَلِ﴾ ("Rather") is for idrab (a turn or change in the discourse). Is it the idrab ibṭālī (nullifying idrab) or the idrab intiqālī (transitional idrab)? It is the nullifying idrab. The nullifying idrab means that what came before "bal" is false. The transitional idrab means that what came before "bal" is a stage from which one moves to another stage without nullifying it. Here, ﴿بَلِ﴾ is nullifying idrab. That is, Allah nullified these two categories between which these disbelievers vacillated regarding the Prophet's (ﷺ) condition. The meaning is: rather, he is not a fabricator and there is no madness in him. But those who do not believe are in punishment and far error, and we cannot acknowledge them (in that). An example of transitional idrab is His saying: ﴿بَلِ ادَّارَكَ عِلْمُهُمْ فِي الْآخِرَةِ بَلْ هُمْ فِي شَكٍّ مِنْهَا بَلْ هُمْ مِنْهَا عَمُونَ﴾ ("Rather, their knowledge has failed concerning the Hereafter. Rather, they are in doubt about it. Rather, they are blind to it") [al-Naml: 66]. This is transitional: their knowledge of the Hereafter first fell short, then they doubted it, then after that they became blind to it, may Allah protect us. These are their transitional states.

Allah said: ﴿بَلِ الَّذِينَ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ بِالْآخِرَةِ﴾, i.e., they do not affirm it or acknowledge it.

* A student: O Shaykh, did we not say (bal) means (aw)?
* The Shaykh: It sometimes comes like ﴿أَوْ يَزِيدُونَ﴾ ("or they increase") [al-Saffat: 147].

He said: ﴿بَلِ الَّذِينَ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ بِالْآخِرَةِ﴾, i.e., they do not believe in its existence and do not believe in what takes place in it. It has already passed us that the Last Day includes everything the Prophet (ﷺ) informed about that occurs after death. So everything the Messenger informed about that occurs after death, such as the trial of the grave, its bliss and its punishment, is included in the Hereafter.

He said: (which includes the resurrection and the punishment, ﴿فِي الْعَذَابِ﴾ "in the punishment" in it, ﴿وَالضَّلَالِ الْبَعِيدِ﴾ "and far error" from the truth in this world). The author, may Allah have mercy on him, restricted the absolute in the two places here.
