David, peace be upon him, was among the best of people in voice and in chanting the remembrance, to the extent that God, Mighty and Majestic, commanded the mountains with a command, either a cosmic one or a legislative one. He said to them: ﴿O mountains, echo along with him﴾. (Awwaba) means "to return the sound," and from it comes "al-awwab," meaning one who returns repeatedly to God. From it also comes "āba yauūbu awban," meaning "to return." So ﴿awwibī maʿahu﴾ means "return with him." Echoing (tarjī') means that you repeat the sound that he makes. For example, when he recited, you would hear as if all the mountains around him were reciting with his recitation. This is different from the ordinary echo that happens to every person, because that echo, which happens to everyone when mountains surround them, is a natural matter. But what David was given was beyond that, for the mountains would echo with him, because of the beauty of his voice and his melodies, to the extent that the mountains would echo with him by the command of God, Glorified and Exalted.

﴿And the birds﴾: ﴿the birds﴾ is in the accusative, and he says it is in the accusative as a conjunction with the grammatical position of "the mountains." How? ﴿O mountains﴾ is a vocative. Is it or not? It is indeclinable, built on the ḍamma in the position of the accusative. It is built on the ḍamma although it is indefinite because it is intended, and an intended indefinite noun is like a proper noun, so for this reason it was built on the ḍamma. ﴿The birds﴾: if it were conjoined to the wording ﴿O mountains﴾, it would be nominative built on the ḍamma, but it is conjoined to the grammatical position of "the mountains," which is the accusative. That is, God likewise commanded the birds to echo with him. So the birds in the air of the sky would stop when they heard David, peace be upon him, reciting, and would echo with him. If you imagine this matter, and that a man recites the Psalms with that recitation and those beautiful melodies, and then the birds from above glorify, and the mountains, there is no doubt that it is a magnificent and awe-inspiring sight. Everything recites with the recitation of this man by the command of whom? By the command of God, Mighty and Majestic.

And His words: ﴿And We made iron soft for him﴾ (﴿We made iron soft for him﴾, so it became in his hand like dough). ﴿We made iron soft for him﴾ means: We made it pliable in his hand, so that it was like dough in the hand of any one of us. Is the intended meaning that He made it soft for him through the means that soften iron, which were made subservient and prepared for him, or that God softened the iron for him without a known cause?

Some people hold the first view, that the intended meaning of ﴿And We made iron soft for him﴾ is that We facilitated for him the means by which iron became soft for him, because the facilitating of means is without doubt a blessing of God. Do you see, if you want to bend a piece of iron and you have a weak fire, does it tire you or not? But if you had a very strong fire, within a few minutes this iron would soften as you wish. So some scholars hold that the intended meaning of softening iron for David is the facilitation of the means by which its softening became easy. But some people of knowledge say: God softened the iron for him without a cause, rather by the power of God, Mighty and Majestic, and God made that a sign for him, just as God made the staff of Moses, when it fell to the ground, become a serpent, and when he picked it up it became a staff in an instant, in one moment. God is over all things capable. The One who made iron hard is able to make it soft. And in my view this is closer to the meaning. First: God said ﴿And We made it soft for him﴾, attributing the softening to Himself, indicating that the softening of this iron was by mere power. Saying that this was by ordinary causes that were merely facilitated for him is contrary to the apparent meaning of the verse. Then, if we say this view, would this be a sign for him? No, because everyone for whom the means of softening iron are facilitated, God makes iron soft for him. Fine. God softened iron for him until it was in his hand like dough, able to shape it as thin, or as thick, as he wished. For this reason He said: ﴿That make full coats of mail﴾. This is the wisdom of God's softening iron for him: that he make from it coats of armor for the fighters in the way of God.

He said ﴿That make full coats of mail﴾. The author, may God have mercy on him, informed us by his words: (And We said ﴿That make﴾) that "an" is a verbal particle whose governed verb has been deleted, and the estimate is: (And We said: that make), i.e., "that you make," meaning "by making." It is possible that "an" is explanatory, and we estimate the deleted element as "We revealed" ("And We revealed to him that make"), because the explanatory "an" is one preceded by a meaning of speech but not its letters. This is closer than the author's estimate. And ﴿That make﴾ means: "And We revealed to him: that make full coats of mail."

﴿Make﴾ means "fashion." From what? He said: (from it), i.e., from iron. ﴿Full coats of mail﴾: what follows it in your copies? "Dir'an" in the accusative? For me it is not accusative (...). ("Complete ones that its wearer drags on the ground.")

﴿Full coats of mail﴾: the author explained it by saying: (complete ones that its owner drags on the ground). And by saying "dir'an" (coats of mail), he informed us that ﴿sābighāt﴾ is an adjective of an omitted noun, and the omitted noun is "dir'an." Omitting the modified noun is permissible. Ibn Malik said:

*"What is understood of the modified and the modifier may be omitted, and in the modifier it is rare."*

"Sābigh" of anything is the complete, perfect, full one. From it is God's words: ﴿And He has completed upon you His favors, apparent and hidden﴾ [Luqman 20], meaning He perfected and completed them. From it also comes "isbāgh al-wuḍū'," meaning its perfecting and completing. So these "sābighāt" coats of mail are the full, complete ones that prevent their wearer from being harmed.

As for the author's statement, (that its wearer drags on the ground), this requires consideration, because there is no need for it to be dragged on the ground, and because if it reached that level it might hinder the charge and retreat. What is known is that coats of mail reach only to the knee; that is their limit, because they are iron, and if a person wears iron that reaches the ground, he would be shackled with chains. So the proper thing is to say: ﴿sābighāt﴾ means complete, without deficiency, and the completeness of each thing is according to its kind.

﴿That make full coats of mail and calculate well the links﴾ ("al-sard" means weaving the coat of mail, just as cloth is woven from cotton or wool; the coat of mail is woven from iron. It was said to its maker: "sarrād," meaning make it such that its rings are proportionate.) ﴿Calculate well the links﴾: ("al-sard") means weaving the coat of mail, as cloth is woven from cotton and from wool. The coat of mail is woven from iron. The meaning of "calculating in the weaving" is: make this weaving measured and proportionate. Calculation means that you make the rings proportionate: you do not bring a large ring and a small ring, and among that is that you do not make the rings too tight, because if they are tight the coat of mail becomes stiff and not easy to move in. And do not make them too wide, because if you make them very wide they do not protect; and then they become larger, and if you make them very wide they grow and harm the wearer. Rather, make them measured and proportionate. And I do not know whether you imagine coats of mail or not.

* Student: (...) round.
* The Shaykh: On the hand?
* The student: Yes.
* The Shaykh: No, coats of mail are shirts, a shirt like this garment of ours.
* The student: And what is this called?
* The Shaykh: I do not know about this. Apparently they are the armor of the athletes.
* The student: The shield?
* The Shaykh: The one held in the hand?
* The student: (...).
* The Shaykh: No, coats of mail are shirts made of iron, a shirt you wear as you wear this garment, except that its sleeve does not reach the palm, only to the upper arm. And this coat of mail is woven from iron rings, small rings interlocked with one another, interlaced one with another until the weaving is complete.
* Student: (...).
* The Shaykh: They exist. Perhaps God, Glorified and Exalted, will facilitate that we see someone who has a museum here in town, and we have him bring us something.
* Student: It exists?
* The Shaykh: It exists. As for what you mentioned, the one held in the hand to protect against the spear, this is called a "turs" (shield).
* The student: (...).
* The Shaykh: "Dir"? 
* The student: (...).
* The Shaykh: This shield? I did not know it by this word.
* Student: (...).
* The Shaykh: In any case, now the "dir'" is the iron shirt.

Fine. ﴿And calculate well the links﴾: the meaning of calculating in the weaving now is that the rings should be proportionate, neither tight nor wide, because if they are not proportionate they cause harm: one small and one large. If they are wide they harm and may not protect against arrows; if they are tight they do not move as they should and are heavy on the wearer.

He said: ﴿That make full coats of mail and calculate well the links, and do righteousness﴾ (﴿and do﴾, i.e., the family of David together, ﴿righteousness. Indeed I am Seeing of what you do﴾, so I will reward you for it).

When God, Mighty and Majestic, explained what He bestowed upon David: teaching him the craft of coats of mail, softening iron for him, and directing him how to make these coats, He said: ﴿And do righteousness﴾. Why did the address shift from the singular in ﴿calculate well﴾ to the plural in ﴿and do righteousness﴾? Because calculating the weaving was specific to David, while righteous deeds are general to him and to others, so the address was directed to all the family of David: ﴿and do righteousness﴾.

His words ﴿righteousness﴾ are an adjective of an omitted noun; the estimate is "a righteous deed." Righteous deed is that which combines two qualities: sincerity to God and conformity to His law. So a righteous deed must include these two conditions: sincerity to God and conformity to the Law. If sincerity is absent, it is not righteous, because of the presence of shirk. God Most High said in the sacred hadith: "I am the most self-sufficient of partners in need of partners. Whoever does a deed in which he associates others with Me, I leave him and his association" [Muslim (2985/46) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him]. The second is conformity to God's law. If it does not conform to God's law, it is not righteous and is not accepted. The evidence is the words of the Prophet ﷺ: "Whoever does a deed that is not in accordance with our command, it is rejected" [Muslim (1718/18) from the hadith of 'A'ishah, may God be pleased with her], and God's words: ﴿Or do they have partners who have legislated for them from religion that which God has not permitted?﴾ [ash-Shura 21]. So for a deed to be righteous, these two conditions are necessary.

﴿Indeed I am Seeing of what you do﴾: this verse contains a fronting and a delay. What is the fronting?

* Student: (...).
* The Shaykh: The fronting is "Seeing"?
* Students: No, (...).
* The Shaykh: ﴿Seeing﴾ is the delayed element, and the fronted element is the object. If you say: it is a established rule that fronting an object indicates restriction, is that not so? Fine. Here, if we say it indicates restriction, then God becomes Seeing of what they do exclusively, not of other things, although He, Mighty and Majestic, is Seeing of everything. So what is the reason? The reason for that fronting, since it came in the form of restriction, is to deter from disobedience. As if, were God not Seeing of anything, He would be Seeing of what? Of your deeds. Since a person may say that God does not see my deed, God made the wording by its outward form indicate restriction, so that no claimant may say that God does not know his deed, from one aspect. From another aspect, it suits the rhyme of the verses, and God knows best.

* Student: We said that every prophet in the Qur'an is a messenger. And Adam, what about him?
* The Shaykh: Adam came before the messengers.
* Student: (...)?
* The Shaykh: No, an exception is made from this; Adam is excepted, because He did not mention him as a messenger.
* Student: (...)?
* The Shaykh: This will come, God willing, in the lessons.
* Student: When it is intended for comparison (...), or in everything we recite?
* The Shaykh: No, it is general to everything: everything that recites and everything that glorifies.
* Student: God's words: ﴿Have they not considered what is before them and behind them of the heaven and the earth?﴾ [Saba' 9]. Is it permissible to go to those places (...)?

* Shaykh: No, it is not permissible to enter the place of punishment except on the condition that a person is weeping. The Prophet (ﷺ) said, "If you are not weeping, then do not enter them"[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (433) and Muslim (2980/38) from the hadith of Ibn 'Umar (may Allah be pleased with them both), and its wording: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to the companions at al-Hijr: "Do not enter upon these punished people unless you are weeping; and if you are not weeping, then do not enter upon them, lest there befall you what befell them."]].
* Student: I said: Is the command, whether legislative or universal, valid (...)?
* Shaykh: Yes, indeed, it is valid; because when Allah the Exalted commands them, since they glorify Allah in worship and humility toward Him, it is valid. Its discussion will come, Allah willing, in the benefits.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the demonstration of Allah the Exalted's favour upon Dawud; for His saying: ﴿And We had certainly given Dawud bounty from Us﴾.
* Second: Among its benefits also: Allah's care in clarifying this bounty; for He emphasized it with the oath, the lam, and qad.
* Among its benefits also: that this bounty is a great bounty; because Allah the Exalted attributed it to Himself in His saying: ﴿bounty from Us﴾, and what is attributed to the Great is great. A parallel to this is the supplication that the Prophet (ﷺ) taught Abu Bakr: "So forgive me with a forgiveness from You"[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (834) and Muslim (2705/48) from the hadith of Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (may Allah be pleased with him).]].
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the address of Allah the Exalted directed to inanimate things; for His saying: ﴿O mountains, echo with him [the praises of Allah]﴾.
* Among its benefits also: that inanimate things perceive the address of Allah the Exalted. The reasoning for this: were it not that they perceive, addressing them would be pointless, and Allah the Exalted is free of futility in His words and deeds. What indicates that they perceive this is that they echoed with him and responded.
* Among its benefits also: that among the virtues of Dawud is that Allah commanded the mountains to echo the glorification with him and to recite the Zabur, along with the birds. Is the command in His saying: ﴿O mountains, echo with him﴾ a universal command or a legislative command? It may bear both meanings. If you consider that they are commanded to worship, you would say it is a legislative command; and if you consider that, were it supposed that these mountains disobeyed, would they be punished? Allah knows best: perhaps they would be punished and perhaps not, since they have no intellect by which they comprehend as the children of Adam do, you would say it is a universal command. To escape these two possibilities we say: Allah commanded the mountains to echo with him, and we do not say it is a universal command nor a legislative command.
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the manifestation of the sign of Allah the Mighty in complete power, in that He softened iron for Dawud; for His saying: ﴿And We made iron soft for him﴾. This softening has no known perceptible cause; for had it been by known means, there would be no difference between Dawud and others. This is the correct view, although some scholars say: ﴿We made it soft for him﴾ means: We prepared for him the means by which iron becomes soft, but We prepared for him great, strong means that are not available to others.
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: is iron by its nature hard or not? It is indeed, were it not that Allah softens it by what He has placed of means by which people benefit; but Allah softens it by what He has placed for it of means that soften it so that people may benefit from it. And which is harder, iron or stones? Stones; that is why stones do not soften by fire, whereas iron softens by fire. The scholars said: this indicates that stones are harder. When Allah compared hard hearts, He said: ﴿Then they are like stones or even harder in hardness﴾ [al-Baqarah 74].
Then the Exalted said: ﴿That make full coats of mail and measure well the links﴾ [Saba' 11], to the end.
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: that Allah the Exalted bestowed favour upon Dawud and upon others by teaching him this craft, the craft of making coats of mail, as Allah said: ﴿And We taught him the making of coats of mail for you to protect you from your violence; so are you grateful?﴾ [al-Anbiya' 80]. This teaching which Allah taught Dawud has remained to this day. This is like how Allah taught Nuh the building of the ship, and Allah indicated the materials of its construction in His saying: ﴿And We carried him on a [vessel of] planks and nails﴾ [al-Qamar 13], i.e., nails.
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: that whoever makes something should complete it, for His saying: ﴿make full coats of mail﴾, complete, and not diminish anything from them. Also, whoever makes something should perfect it; and this is a new benefit: that he should perfect it, for His saying: ﴿and measure well the links﴾, completion and perfection.
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: that one should, indeed one must, when Allah bestows a blessing upon him, perform its thanks by righteous action, for His saying: ﴿And work righteousness﴾.
* Among its benefits also: that when Allah bestows a blessing upon a person of a tribe, it is a bestowal upon the whole tribe. How so? By His saying: ﴿And work righteousness﴾, He addressed all the family of Dawud, although the bounty was specific to Dawud. That is why when someone of distinction arises in a tribe, he raises the status of the whole tribe; isn't that so? Just as the reverse holds: when someone of the tribe becomes base, the whole tribe is reproached through him. This is a known matter.
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the warning against opposition, for His saying: ﴿Indeed, I am Seeing of what you do﴾.
* Among its benefits: that Allah the Exalted is Seeing of all that we do, of good and evil, little and much, apparent and hidden, even the deeds of the hearts He knows? Yes; Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And We have certainly created man, and We know what his soul whispers to him﴾ [Qaf 16]. Be mindful: do not harbour in your heart anything that angers Allah; for when you do, Allah the Exalted will certainly know it, and nothing is hidden from Him: ﴿Indeed, I am Seeing of what you do﴾.

The commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on Surah 34, verses 10–11 (part 1 of 3):

The words of Allah: ﴿And We had certainly given David bounty from Us. "O mountains, repeat [praises] with him, and the birds"﴾ [Saba' 10].

﴿Ātaynā﴾ means "We gave." It takes two objects that are not originally subject and predicate. Every verb that takes two objects that are not originally subject and predicate is called one of the "give and clothe" type (min bāb "a'ṭā wa-kasā," lit. "the category of gave and clothed"). Here, ﴿ātaynā Dāwūda minnā faḍlan﴾: ﴿Dāwūda﴾ is the first object (mafʿūl awwal), and ﴿faḍlan﴾ is the second object (mafʿūl thānī). These cannot be a subject and predicate. If you say "Dāwūd faḍl," is it acceptable? It is not acceptable, all right.

It is also said "ajaynā," but its meaning differs from ﴿ātaynā﴾; rather, the meaning of "ajaynā" is "we came." Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And We had certainly brought them a Book which We detailed with knowledge﴾ [al-A'raf 52], and He the Exalted says: ﴿The command of Allah has come﴾ [al-Nahl 1], meaning the command of Allah has come.

He says: ﴿And We had certainly given David bounty from Us.﴾ David was one of the prophets of the Children of Israel. Was he after Moses or before him?
* Students: Before him.
* Other students: After him.
* The Shaykh: ﴿Have you not considered the chiefs of the Children of Israel after Moses, when they said to a prophet of theirs, "Appoint for us a king so we may fight in the way of Allah"﴾ [al-Baqarah 246]. In the story, David was among them. So he came after Moses, and he was a prophet from among the prophets. The Jews—may the curse of Allah be upon them—denied that he was a prophet and described him as a king, and in that they lied. He was a prophet of Allah's prophets, whom we must believe in, and our faith is not complete except by believing in them, because the pillars of faith, as we know, are belief in Allah, His angels, His books, and His messengers. He was also a messenger, because every prophet mentioned in the Qur'an is a messenger.

He says: ﴿And We had certainly given David bounty from Us.﴾ ﴿From Us﴾: he began with the source before the bounty, to make clear the greatness of that bounty, because when a thing is attributed to a great source, it becomes great. This is like his saying in the authentic hadith: "And forgive me a forgiveness from You and have mercy upon me,"[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (834) and Muslim (2705/48), from the hadith of Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may Allah be pleased with him.]] "from You," so he attributed it to Allah in order to make its greatness clear.

(﴿We gave David bounty from Us﴾: prophethood and a book.) This is what the author (al-Mu'allif, i.e., al-Baghawi or the commentator he is quoting) explained the verse by, and it is by way of example, for Allah gave him prophethood and messengership as well, and He gave him the Book. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And We gave David the Zabur﴾ [al-Nisa' 163]. Did He give him anything other than this? Yes. That is why he made the word "bounty" indefinite, so that it would encompass all the bounty given to him, whether religious or worldly. David, peace be upon him, was among the most beautiful of people in voice and in chanting the remembrance, to the extent that Allah the Mighty and Majestic commanded the mountains with a command, either cosmic or legislative, saying to them: ﴿O mountains, repeat [praises] with him.﴾ (﴿Awwibī﴾) means "to echo back," and from it comes al-awwāb, i.e., one who returns to Allah repeatedly. From it also comes "āba yaūbu awban," meaning "returned." So ﴿awwibī maʿahu﴾ means "return with him" (echo with him). Tarjī' (echoing back) means that you repeat the voice that he utters. For example, if he recited, you would hear as if all the mountains around him were reciting along with his recitation. This is different from the echo that happens to every person, because the echo that happens to everyone when the mountains surround him is a natural matter. But what David was given was beyond that, so the mountains would echo back with him, because of the beauty of his voice and his melodies, to the extent that the mountains echoed with him by the command of Allah, glorified and exalted be He.

﴿And the birds﴾: ﴿al-ṭayr﴾. He says: (in the accusative, in coordination with the position of the mountains [ʿaṭfan ʿalā maḥall al-jibāl]). How? ﴿Yā jibālu﴾: this is a vocative (munādā). Is it or is it not? It is built on a dhamma in the position of the accusative (mabnī ʿalā al-ḍamm fī maḥall naṣb). It was built on the dhamma even though it is indefinite, because it is intended (maqṣūd), and an intended indefinite noun is like a proper noun (ʿalam), so for this reason it was built on the dhamma. ﴿Al-ṭayr﴾: if it were coordinated with the wording ﴿yā jibālu﴾, it would be in the nominative and built on the dhamma. But it is coordinated with the position of ﴿al-jibāl﴾, which is the accusative. That is, Allah similarly commanded the birds to echo with him. So the birds in the atmosphere of the sky would stop upon hearing David, peace be upon him, recite and would echo with him. If you imagine this matter, a man reciting the Zabur with that recitation and those beautiful melodies, and above him the birds glorifying, and the mountains—there is no doubt that it is a magnificent and awe-inspiring scene. Everything recites with the recitation of this man by the command of whom? By the command of Allah the Mighty and Majestic.

His saying: ﴿And We made iron soft for him﴾ (﴿We made iron soft for him,﴾ so it became in his hand like dough). ﴿Alannā lahu al-ḥadīd﴾ means: We made it soft in his hand, to the extent that it was like dough in the hand of any one of us. Is the meaning that He softened it for him through means that soften iron, which were made subservient and prepared for him? Or did Allah soften the iron for him without a known cause?

Some people hold the first view, and that the meaning of ﴿And We made iron soft for him﴾ is that We facilitated for him the means by which iron becomes soft for him, because the facilitation of means is undoubtedly from the blessing of Allah. Have you seen that if you want to bend a rod of iron and you have a weak fire, you will tire in doing it, or not? But if you have a very strong fire, within a few minutes this iron would soften as you wish. Some scholars hold that the meaning of softening the iron for David is the facilitation of the means by which its softening becomes easy. But some people of knowledge say: Allah softened the iron for him without a cause, but by the power of Allah the Mighty and Majestic, and Allah made that a sign for him, just as Allah made the staff of Moses, when it fell on the ground it became a snake, and when he raised it, it became a staff in one moment, in a single instant. Allah is capable of all things, and He who made iron hard is able to make it soft. In my view, this is closer to the meaning. Firstly: Allah said ﴿And We made [it] soft﴾, attributing the softening to Himself, indicating that the softness of this iron was by mere power. Saying that this was by ordinary means, but that they were made easy for him, goes against the apparent meaning of the verse. Then, if we say this view, would it be a sign for him? No, because everyone for whom the means of softening iron are made easy has had iron softened for him by Allah. Good. Allah softened the iron for him until it was in his hand like dough; he could turn it, make it thin or thick as he wished. That is why He said: ﴿That make full coats of mail﴾. This is the wisdom behind Allah softening the iron for him: so that he could make from it coats of armor for the fighters in the way of Allah.

He said ﴿Make full coats of mail﴾. The author, may Allah have mercy on him, informed us with his saying "and We said ﴿make﴾" that (an) is a verbal (maṣdariyya) particle whose governing element has been deleted, and the estimate is "and We said: that make," i.e., "by making," i.e., "by the act of making." It is possible that (an) is explanatory (tafsīriyya), and that we estimate the deleted element as "we inspired" ("and We inspired to him, that make"), because the explanatory (an) is one preceded by the sense of speech without its letters. This is closer than the author's estimate. And ﴿an iʿmal﴾ means: "And We inspired to him, ﴿that make full coats of mail.﴾"

﴿Iʿmal﴾ means "make." From what? He said: "from it," i.e., from iron. ﴿Sābighāt﴾: what comes after it according to you? Coats of mail in the accusative? I hold that it is not in the accusative; (full, complete, which their wearer trails on the ground).

﴿Sābighāt﴾: the author explained it by his saying: (complete ones which their wearer trails on the ground). And by his saying "coats of mail," he informed us that ﴿sābighāt﴾ is an adjective (ṣifa) for a deleted noun, and this deleted noun is estimated as "coats of mail." Deleting the noun being described is permissible. Ibn Malik said:

*And what is understood from the described and the describing, its deletion is permissible, and in the describing it is rare.*

The sābigh of anything is the complete, perfect, and whole. From this is the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And He has completed His favors upon you, apparent and hidden﴾ [Luqman 20], meaning He completed and perfected them. From it also is ischāgh al-wuḍū' (completing the ablution), meaning completing and perfecting it. So these ﴿sābighāt﴾ coats of mail mean those that are full and complete, which prevent their wearer from being harmed.

As for the author's saying "which their wearer trails on the ground," there is a point to consider in it, because there is no need for it to be trailed on the ground. Also, if they reached this level, they might hinder charging and retreating. It is well known that coats of mail reach only to the knee; this is their extent, because they are iron, and if a person wears iron reaching the ground, he would be shackled with chains. So it is necessary to say: ﴿sābighāt﴾ means complete, having no deficiency, and the completeness of each thing is according to its nature.

﴿Make full coats of mail and measure well in the links﴾ (i.e., the weaving of coats of mail; it was said to its maker "sarrād," meaning: make it such that its rings are proportionate). ﴿Qaddir fī al-sard﴾: (al-sard) means weaving the coat of mail, just as a garment is woven from cotton and wool, a coat of mail is woven from iron. The meaning of "measure in the weaving" is: make this weaving measured and proportionate, from "taqdīr" (measuring). That...

﴿And We had certainly given David bounty from Us﴾ [Saba' 10]. The "wāw" is a conjunctive particle, and it is permissible for it to be for resumption (istiʾnāf). The "lām" is a preparatory lām for an oath (lām al-tawṭiʾa lil-qasam).
* A student: (...).
* The Shaykh: How?
* The student: (...).
* The Shaykh: No, (...). The lām is a preparatory lām for the oath, and "qad" is for confirmation (taḥqīq). This kind of construction occurs frequently in the Qur'an, and it is said of it that the sentence is emphasized with three emphatics: the implied oath, the lām, and "qad." So the estimate of this sentence is "By Allah, indeed We gave David bounty from Us." Is it permissible to delete the lām? Yes, it is permissible. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿By the sun and its brightness, and by the moon when it follows it, and by the day when it displays it, and by the night when it covers it, and by the sky and He who built it﴾ [al-Shams 1–5], up to His saying: ﴿He has certainly succeeded who purifies it﴾. This is the answer to the oath. In ﴿qad afläḥa man zakkāhā﴾, outside the Qur'an it is permissible to say "la-qad afläḥa." All right.

Is it permissible to delete the lām and "qad"? Yes, it is permissible, as in His saying: ﴿By the sky of the constellations, and the promised day, and the witness and the witnessed, "Destroyed were the companions of the trench"﴾ [al-Buruj 1–4]. So ﴿qutila﴾ is the answer to the oath; there is no "qad" or lām in it. So when the answer to the oath is a past-tense verb, three possibilities are permitted: it may be accompanied by the lām and "qad," it may be accompanied by "qad" alone, or the (...) and the lām and "qad" may be deleted. But the lām and "qad" are not generally deleted, except if the oath is long. If it is not long, they are not deleted.

If you say: "Wallāhi la-qad qāma Zayd" (By Allah, Zayd indeed stood), is it correct? "Wallāhi la-qad qāma Zayd" is correct, and this is the original form. "Wallāhi qad qāma Zayd" is also correct, having deleted the lām. "Wallāhi qāma Zayd" is also correct, having deleted from it the lām and "qad." And Allah knows best.

(...) * Among the benefits of the noble verse, ﴿And those who disbelieved said, "Shall we direct you to a man who will inform you when you have been completely disintegrated?"﴾ [Saba' 7], to its end: that the Prophet ﷺ called to belief in the Last Day. From where is this taken? From His saying: ﴿"Shall we inform you when you have been completely disintegrated, that you will be in a new creation?"﴾.

* And among the benefits of the noble verse: the clarification of the arrogance of the disbelievers, their haughtiness and their pride, in that they expressed this with mockery toward what the Prophet ﷺ had reported. The aspects of their haughtiness and pride are:
First: mockery of this news.
Second: belittling the Prophet ﷺ.
Third: describing him as being in one of two states: either a liar or a madman. These are three aspects, all of which indicate the haughtiness of these disbelievers and their obstinacy.

* And among the benefits of the noble verse: the clarification of the harm that the Prophet ﷺ endured, and that he was patient. For a matter that reaches this extent of belittling him and disdaining his report undoubtedly affects his soul profoundly. I believe that when the one calling to the message is harmed in this manner, it is harder on him than being beaten or imprisoned.

* And among the benefits of the noble verse: the clarification of the power of Allah the Mighty and Majestic, in that He will return this creation after it has been torn apart completely, because this is apparent from His saying: ﴿"He will inform you when you have been completely disintegrated."﴾

* And among its benefits: that the disbelievers who disbelieved in the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to acknowledge Allah. From where is this taken? ﴿"Has he invented against Allah a lie?"﴾.

* And among its benefits: the clarification of the ugliness of fabricating against Allah, to the extent that the disbelievers themselves find it ugly, because of His saying: ﴿"Has he invented against Allah a lie?"﴾.

* And among the benefits of the noble verse also: that the enemies of the messengers, indeed the enemies of the messengers' call, pour forth insult, slander, and defamation against what the messengers brought, or against the messengers and what they brought, because of their saying: ﴿"Has he invented against Allah a lie, or is there madness in him?"﴾. It is known that the speech of a liar and the speech of a madman are not accepted. So they use expressions of distortion and disparagement so that the truth will not be accepted. Does this continue to our time? Yes, it continues to our time, because the enemies of the messengers' call will persist until the Day of Resurrection. But the followers of the messengers must be patient and must not be deterred in their resolve by such words, because they are upon the truth, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿"Indeed, you are upon the clear truth"﴾ [al-Naml 79].

* And among the benefits of the noble verse: the clarification that Allah the Mighty and Majestic has taken upon Himself the explanation of the truth and its manifestation, and the nullification of falsehood and its defeat, because of His saying: ﴿"Rather, those who do not believe in the Hereafter are in torment and far error."﴾

* And among its benefits also: that disbelief necessitates the non-acceptance of the truth and not being guided by it, which is taken from His saying: ﴿"in torment and far error"﴾. The "fī" here is for location (ẓarfiyya), and its meaning is that error surrounds them from every side. This is why Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And We turn their hearts and their sights as they did not believe in it the first time, and We leave them in their transgression, wandering blindly﴾ [al-An'am 110]. So when a person does not believe in the truth, he remains in error. The evidence for this is abundant. Listen to a verse such as this and to His saying the Exalted: ﴿"Rather, they denied the truth when it came to them, so they are in a state of confusion"﴾ [Qaf 5], meaning: disturbed and disordered. Everyone who denies the truth increases only in error, even if clear and manifest signs come to him, he does not benefit from them. ﴿"And as for those in whose hearts is a disease, it adds to their filth [another] filth, and they die while they are disbelievers"﴾ [al-Tawbah 125], even though they are clear and evident signs.

* And among the benefits of the noble verse: ﴿"Have they not looked at what is before them and what is behind them"﴾: the obligation of reflection and taking lessons from the signs that exist in the heavens and the earth, because of His saying: ﴿"Have they not looked at what is before them and what is behind them of the heaven and the earth?"﴾. This interrogation is for rebuke, and one is rebuked only for abandoning an obligation.

* And among the benefits of the noble verse: that in the heavens and the earth there are signs, but for whom? For the servant who turns penitently to Allah. As for one who does not want to return to his Lord, he does not benefit from these signs, even if he sees them, considers them, and reflects on them.

* And among the benefits of the noble verse: the affirmation of Allah's will, because of His saying: ﴿"If We will, We cause the earth to swallow them"﴾.

* And among the benefits of the noble verse also: that what occurs of earth-swallowing, earthquakes, and calamities is by the permission of Allah the Mighty and Majestic, as a punishment for the servants and as a lesson. This is contrary to those who say these are natural matters that do not indicate the anger of Allah the Mighty and Majestic nor His warning, as is the view of those who do not believe in Allah. Earth-swallowing is a punishment, and what comes of lightning and horizon-related catastrophes is also a punishment. This is why He said: ﴿"If We will, We cause the earth to swallow them, or We drop upon them fragments [from the sky]."﴾

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: God Most High encompasses His servants, and they cannot escape His decree and His divine measure. God encompasses everything, and there is no escape for the servants from Him, as indicated by His words: ﴿We could cause the earth to swallow them, or drop upon them fragments from the sky﴾.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: God, Mighty and Majestic, bestows favor upon the servant by making the signs manifest to him until the truth becomes clear to him, as indicated by His words: ﴿Indeed in that is a sign for every servant who turns back in repentance﴾. When God bestows upon the servant the ability to reflect on His signs and contemplate them, his faith in God, Mighty and Majestic, increases, as does his faith in what these signs entail of His attributes. Every sign points to a specific attribute of God. The sending down of rain indicates power, knowledge and mercy, and its occurring at an appropriate time indicates wisdom. Everything that occurs in the heavens and the earth indicates an attribute of God Most High that befits it.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: there are great signs in the heavens and the earth for whoever observes and reflects. God, Glorified and Exalted, affirmed this in the Qur'an in many places: ﴿And on the earth are signs for those with certainty﴾ [adh-Dhariyat 20], and ﴿And on the earth are adjacent tracts, and gardens of grapevines, and crops, and palm trees, some with multiple trunks and some with single trunks, watered with one water, yet We make some of them exceed others in fruit. Indeed in that are signs for a people who reason﴾ [ar-Ra'd 4]. The verses with this meaning are numerous. Whoever reflects on what is in the heavens, what is in the earth, and what is between them, the signs of God will become clear to him, strengthening his faith and increasing his hope for God's bounty and his fear of His punishment.

* * *

His words: ﴿And We gave David a bounty from Us. O mountains, echo along with him, and the birds﴾ [Saba' 10].

﴿We gave﴾ (ātaynā) means "We bestowed." It takes two objects, neither of which is originally a subject and predicate. Every verb that takes two objects that are not originally a subject and predicate is called of the category of "give and clothe" (a'ṭā wa kasā). So here, ﴿We gave David﴾ is the first object and ﴿a bounty﴾ is the second object. This cannot be a subject and predicate. If you say "David, bounty," does that work? It does not work. Fine.

It is said "ataynā" (we came) too, but its meaning differs from ﴿ātaynā﴾. Rather, the meaning of "ataynā" is "we came." God Most High said: ﴿And We have certainly brought them a Book which We have detailed with knowledge﴾ [al-A'raf 52], and He Most High said: ﴿The command of God has come﴾ [an-Nahl 1], meaning the command of God has come.

He said: ﴿And We gave David a bounty from Us.﴾ David is one of the prophets of the Children of Israel. Is he after Moses or before him?

* Students: Before him.
* Other students: After him.
* The Shaykh: ﴿Have you not considered the eminent men of the Children of Israel after Moses, when they said to a prophet of theirs, "Appoint for us a king, and we will fight in the way of God"?﴾ [al-Baqarah 246]. In the story, David was among them. So he is after Moses, and he is one of the prophets. The Jews, may God curse them, denied that he was a prophet and described him as a king, and they lied in that. He was indeed one of the prophets of God whom we must believe in, and our faith is not complete except by believing in them, because the pillars of faith, as we know, are belief in God, His angels, His books and His messengers. He was also a messenger, because every prophet mentioned in the Qur'an is a messenger.

He said: ﴿And We gave David a bounty from Us.﴾ ﴿From Us﴾: He began with the source before the bounty in order to make clear the greatness of that bounty, because when a thing is attributed to a great source, it becomes great. As in the words of the Prophet ﷺ in the authentic hadith: "And forgive me with a forgiveness from You and have mercy on me" [agreed upon; al-Bukhari (834) and Muslim (2705/48) from the hadith of Abu Bakr as-Siddiq, may God be pleased with him]. "From You" attributes it to God so that its greatness becomes clear.

(﴿We gave David a bounty from Us﴾: prophethood and a book.) This which the author explained the verse with is by way of illustration, for God gave him prophethood and messengerhood as well, and He gave him the Book. God Most High said: ﴿And We gave David the Psalms﴾ [an-Nisa' 163]. Did He give him anything else besides this? Yes. For this reason the word "bounty" came indefinite, to include every bounty he was given, whether religious or worldly. David, peace be upon him, was among the best of people in voice and in chanting the remembrance, to the extent that God, Mighty and Majestic, commanded the mountains with a command, either a cosmic one or a legislative one. He said to them: ﴿O mountains, echo along with him﴾. (Awwaba) means "to return the sound," and from it comes "al-awwab," meaning one who returns repeatedly to God. From it also comes "āba yauūbu awban," meaning "to return." So ﴿awwibī maʿahu﴾ means "return with him." Echoing (tarjī') means that you repeat the sound that he makes. For example, when he recited, you would hear as if all the mountains around him were reciting with his recitation. This is different from the ordinary echo that happens to every person, because that echo, which happens to everyone when mountains surround them, is a natural matter. But what David was given was beyond that, for the mountains would echo with him, because of the beauty of his voice and his melodies, to the extent that the mountains would echo with him by the command of God, Glorified and Exalted.

﴿And the birds﴾: ﴿the birds﴾ is in the accusative, and he says it is in the accusative as a conjunction with the grammatical position of "the mountains." How? ﴿O mountains﴾ is a vocative. Is it or not? It is indeclinable, built on the ḍamma in the position of the accusative. It is built on the ḍamma although it is indefinite because it is intended, and an intended indefinite noun is like a proper noun, so for this reason it was built on the ḍamma. ﴿The birds﴾: if it were conjoined to the wording ﴿O mountains﴾, it would be nominative built on the ḍamma, but it is conjoined to the grammatical position of "the mountains," which is the accusative. That is, God likewise commanded the birds to echo with him. So the birds in the air of the sky would stop when they heard David, peace be upon him, reciting, and would echo with him. If you imagine this matter, and that a man recites the Psalms with that recitation and those beautiful melodies, and then the birds from above glorify, and the mountains, there is no doubt that it is a magnificent and awe-inspiring sight. Everything recites with the recitation of this man by the command of whom? By the command of God, Mighty and Majestic.

And His words: ﴿And We made iron soft for him﴾ (﴿We made iron soft for him﴾, so it became in his hand like dough). ﴿We made iron soft for him﴾ means: We made it pliable in his hand, so that it was like dough in the hand of any one of us. Is the intended meaning that He made it soft for him through the means that soften iron, which were made subservient and prepared for him, or that God softened the iron for him without a known cause?

Some people hold the first view, that the intended meaning of ﴿And We made iron soft for him﴾ is that We facilitated for him the means by which iron became soft for him, because the facilitating of means is without doubt a blessing of God. Do you see, if you want to bend a piece of iron and you have a weak fire, does it tire you or not? But if you had a very strong fire, within a few minutes this iron would soften as you wish. So some scholars hold that the intended meaning of softening iron for David is the facilitation of the means by which its softening became easy. But some people of knowledge say: God softened the iron for him without a cause, rather by the power of God, Mighty and Majestic, and God made that a sign for him, just as God made the staff of Moses, when it fell to the ground, become a serpent, and when he picked it up it became a staff in an instant, in one moment. God is over all things capable. The One who made iron hard is able to make it soft. And in my view this is closer to the meaning. First: God said ﴿And We made it soft for him﴾, attributing the softening to Himself, indicating that the softening of this iron was by mere power. Saying that this was by ordinary causes that were merely facilitated for him is contrary to the apparent meaning of the verse. Then, if we say this view, would this be a sign for him? No, because everyone for whom the means of softening iron are facilitated, God makes iron soft for him. Fine. God softened iron for him until it was in his hand like dough, able to shape it as thin, or as thick, as he wished. For this reason He said: ﴿That make full coats of mail﴾. This is the wisdom of God's softening iron for him: that he make from it coats of armor for the fighters in the way of God.

He said ﴿That make full coats of mail﴾. The author, may God have mercy on him, informed us by his words: (And We said ﴿That make﴾) that "an" is a verbal particle whose governed verb has been deleted, and the estimate is: (And We said: that make), i.e., "that you make," meaning "by making." It is possible that "an" is explanatory, and we estimate the deleted element as "We revealed" ("And We revealed to him that make"), because the explanatory "an" is one preceded by a meaning of speech but not its letters. This is closer than the author's estimate. And ﴿That make﴾ means: "And We revealed to him: that make full coats of mail."

﴿Make﴾ means "fashion." From what? He said: (from it), i.e., from iron. ﴿Full coats of mail﴾: what follows it in your copies? "Dir'an" in the accusative? For me it is not accusative (...). ("Complete ones that its wearer drags on the ground.")

﴿Full coats of mail﴾: the author explained it by saying: (complete ones that its owner drags on the ground). And by saying "dir'an" (coats of mail), he informed us that ﴿sābighāt﴾ is an adjective of an omitted noun, and the omitted noun is "dir'an." Omitting the modified noun is permissible. Ibn Malik said:

*"What is understood of the modified and the modifier may be omitted, and in the modifier it is rare."*

"Sābigh" of anything is the complete, perfect, full one. From it is God's words: ﴿And He has completed upon you His favors, apparent and hidden﴾ [Luqman 20], meaning He perfected and completed them. From it also comes "isbāgh al-wuḍū'," meaning its perfecting and completing. So these "sābighāt" coats of mail are the full, complete ones that prevent their wearer from being harmed.

As for the author's statement, (that its wearer drags on the ground), this requires consideration, because there is no need for it to be dragged on the ground, and because if it reached that level it might hinder the charge and retreat. What is known is that coats of mail reach only to the knee; that is their limit, because they are iron, and if a person wears iron that reaches the ground, he would be shackled with chains. So the proper thing is to say: ﴿sābighāt﴾ means complete, without deficiency, and the completeness of each thing is according to its kind.

﴿That make full coats of mail and calculate well the links﴾ ("al-sard" means weaving the coat of mail, just as cloth is woven from cotton or wool; the coat of mail is woven from iron. It was said to its maker: "sarrād," meaning make it such that its rings are proportionate.) ﴿Calculate well the links﴾: ("al-sard") means weaving the coat of mail, as cloth is woven from cotton and from wool. The coat of mail is woven from iron. The meaning of "calculating in the weaving" is: make this weaving measured and proportionate. Calculation means that you make the rings proportionate: you do not bring a large ring and a small ring, and among that is that you do not make the rings too tight, because if they are tight the coat of mail becomes stiff and not easy to move in. And do not make them too wide, because if you make them very wide they do not protect; and then they become larger, and if you make them very wide they grow and harm the wearer. Rather, make them measured and proportionate. And I do not know whether you imagine coats of mail or not.

* Student: (...) round.
* The Shaykh: On the hand?
* The student: Yes.
* The Shaykh: No, coats of mail are shirts, a shirt like this garment of ours.
* The student: And what is this called?
* The Shaykh: I do not know about this. Apparently they are the armor of the athletes.
* The student: The shield?
* The Shaykh: The one held in the hand?
* The student: (...).
* The Shaykh: No, coats of mail are shirts made of iron, a shirt you wear as you wear this garment, except that its sleeve does not reach the palm, only to the upper arm. And this coat of mail is woven from iron rings, small rings interlocked with one another, interlaced one with another until the weaving is complete.
* Student: (...).
* The Shaykh: They exist. Perhaps God, Glorified and Exalted, will facilitate that we see someone who has a museum here in town, and we have him bring us something.
* Student: It exists?
* The Shaykh: It exists. As for what you mentioned, the one held in the hand to protect against the spear, this is called a "turs" (shield).
* The student: (...).
* The Shaykh: "Dir"? 
* The student: (...).
* The Shaykh: This shield? I did not know it by this word.
* Student: (...).
* The Shaykh: In any case, now the "dir'" is the iron shirt.

Fine. ﴿And calculate well the links﴾: the meaning of calculating in the weaving now is that the rings should be proportionate, neither tight nor wide, because if they are not proportionate they cause harm: one small and one large. If they are wide they harm and may not protect against arrows; if they are tight they do not move as they should and are heavy on the wearer.

He said: ﴿That make full coats of mail and calculate well the links, and do righteousness﴾ (﴿and do﴾, i.e., the family of David together, ﴿righteousness. Indeed I am Seeing of what you do﴾, so I will reward you for it).

When God, Mighty and Majestic, explained what He bestowed upon David: teaching him the craft of coats of mail, softening iron for him, and directing him how to make these coats, He said: ﴿And do righteousness﴾. Why did the address shift from the singular in ﴿calculate well﴾ to the plural in ﴿and do righteousness﴾? Because calculating the weaving was specific to David, while righteous deeds are general to him and to others, so the address was directed to all the family of David: ﴿and do righteousness﴾.

His words ﴿righteousness﴾ are an adjective of an omitted noun; the estimate is "a righteous deed." Righteous deed is that which combines two qualities: sincerity to God and conformity to His law. So a righteous deed must include these two conditions: sincerity to God and conformity to the Law. If sincerity is absent, it is not righteous, because of the presence of shirk. God Most High said in the sacred hadith: "I am the most self-sufficient of partners in need of partners. Whoever does a deed in which he associates others with Me, I leave him and his association" [Muslim (2985/46) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him]. The second is conformity to God's law. If it does not conform to God's law, it is not righteous and is not accepted. The evidence is the words of the Prophet ﷺ: "Whoever does a deed that is not in accordance with our command, it is rejected" [Muslim (1718/18) from the hadith of 'A'ishah, may God be pleased with her], and God's words: ﴿Or do they have partners who have legislated for them from religion that which God has not permitted?﴾ [ash-Shura 21]. So for a deed to be righteous, these two conditions are necessary.

﴿Indeed I am Seeing of what you do﴾: this verse contains a fronting and a delay. What is the fronting?

* Student: (...).
* The Shaykh: The fronting is "Seeing"?
* Students: No, (...).
* The Shaykh: ﴿Seeing﴾ is the delayed element, and the fronted element is the object. If you say: it is a established rule that fronting an object indicates restriction, is that not so? Fine. Here, if we say it indicates restriction, then God becomes Seeing of what they do exclusively, not of other things, although He, Mighty and Majestic, is Seeing of everything. So what is the reason? The reason for that fronting, since it came in the form of restriction, is to deter from disobedience. As if, were God not Seeing of anything, He would be Seeing of what? Of your deeds. Since a person may say that God does not see my deed, God made the wording by its outward form indicate restriction, so that no claimant may say that God does not know his deed, from one aspect. From another aspect, it suits the rhyme of the verses, and God knows best.

* Student: We said that every prophet in the Qur'an is a messenger. And Adam, what about him?
* The Shaykh: Adam came before the messengers.
* Student: (...)?
* The Shaykh: No, an exception is made from this; Adam is excepted, because He did not mention him as a messenger.
* Student: (...)?
* The Shaykh: This will come, God willing, in the lessons.
* Student: When it is intended for comparison (...), or in everything we recite?
* The Shaykh: No, it is general to everything: everything that recites and everything that glorifies.
* Student: God's words: ﴿Have they not considered what is before them and behind them of the heaven and the earth?﴾ [Saba' 9]. Is it permissible to go to those places (...)?

* Shaykh: No, it is not permissible to enter the place of punishment except on the condition that a person is weeping. The Prophet (ﷺ) said, "If you are not weeping, then do not enter them"[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (433) and Muslim (2980/38) from the hadith of Ibn 'Umar (may Allah be pleased with them both), and its wording: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to the companions at al-Hijr: "Do not enter upon these punished people unless you are weeping; and if you are not weeping, then do not enter upon them, lest there befall you what befell them."]].
* Student: I said: Is the command, whether legislative or universal, valid (...)?
* Shaykh: Yes, indeed, it is valid; because when Allah the Exalted commands them, since they glorify Allah in worship and humility toward Him, it is valid. Its discussion will come, Allah willing, in the benefits.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the demonstration of Allah the Exalted's favour upon Dawud; for His saying: ﴿And We had certainly given Dawud bounty from Us﴾.
* Second: Among its benefits also: Allah's care in clarifying this bounty; for He emphasized it with the oath, the lam, and qad.
* Among its benefits also: that this bounty is a great bounty; because Allah the Exalted attributed it to Himself in His saying: ﴿bounty from Us﴾, and what is attributed to the Great is great. A parallel to this is the supplication that the Prophet (ﷺ) taught Abu Bakr: "So forgive me with a forgiveness from You"[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (834) and Muslim (2705/48) from the hadith of Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (may Allah be pleased with him).]].
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the address of Allah the Exalted directed to inanimate things; for His saying: ﴿O mountains, echo with him [the praises of Allah]﴾.
* Among its benefits also: that inanimate things perceive the address of Allah the Exalted. The reasoning for this: were it not that they perceive, addressing them would be pointless, and Allah the Exalted is free of futility in His words and deeds. What indicates that they perceive this is that they echoed with him and responded.
* Among its benefits also: that among the virtues of Dawud is that Allah commanded the mountains to echo the glorification with him and to recite the Zabur, along with the birds. Is the command in His saying: ﴿O mountains, echo with him﴾ a universal command or a legislative command? It may bear both meanings. If you consider that they are commanded to worship, you would say it is a legislative command; and if you consider that, were it supposed that these mountains disobeyed, would they be punished? Allah knows best: perhaps they would be punished and perhaps not, since they have no intellect by which they comprehend as the children of Adam do, you would say it is a universal command. To escape these two possibilities we say: Allah commanded the mountains to echo with him, and we do not say it is a universal command nor a legislative command.
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the manifestation of the sign of Allah the Mighty in complete power, in that He softened iron for Dawud; for His saying: ﴿And We made iron soft for him﴾. This softening has no known perceptible cause; for had it been by known means, there would be no difference between Dawud and others. This is the correct view, although some scholars say: ﴿We made it soft for him﴾ means: We prepared for him the means by which iron becomes soft, but We prepared for him great, strong means that are not available to others.
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: is iron by its nature hard or not? It is indeed, were it not that Allah softens it by what He has placed of means by which people benefit; but Allah softens it by what He has placed for it of means that soften it so that people may benefit from it. And which is harder, iron or stones? Stones; that is why stones do not soften by fire, whereas iron softens by fire. The scholars said: this indicates that stones are harder. When Allah compared hard hearts, He said: ﴿Then they are like stones or even harder in hardness﴾ [al-Baqarah 74].
Then the Exalted said: ﴿That make full coats of mail and measure well the links﴾ [Saba' 11], to the end.
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: that Allah the Exalted bestowed favour upon Dawud and upon others by teaching him this craft, the craft of making coats of mail, as Allah said: ﴿And We taught him the making of coats of mail for you to protect you from your violence; so are you grateful?﴾ [al-Anbiya' 80]. This teaching which Allah taught Dawud has remained to this day. This is like how Allah taught Nuh the building of the ship, and Allah indicated the materials of its construction in His saying: ﴿And We carried him on a [vessel of] planks and nails﴾ [al-Qamar 13], i.e., nails.
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: that whoever makes something should complete it, for His saying: ﴿make full coats of mail﴾, complete, and not diminish anything from them. Also, whoever makes something should perfect it; and this is a new benefit: that he should perfect it, for His saying: ﴿and measure well the links﴾, completion and perfection.
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: that one should, indeed one must, when Allah bestows a blessing upon him, perform its thanks by righteous action, for His saying: ﴿And work righteousness﴾.
* Among its benefits also: that when Allah bestows a blessing upon a person of a tribe, it is a bestowal upon the whole tribe. How so? By His saying: ﴿And work righteousness﴾, He addressed all the family of Dawud, although the bounty was specific to Dawud. That is why when someone of distinction arises in a tribe, he raises the status of the whole tribe; isn't that so? Just as the reverse holds: when someone of the tribe becomes base, the whole tribe is reproached through him. This is a known matter.
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the warning against opposition, for His saying: ﴿Indeed, I am Seeing of what you do﴾.
* Among its benefits: that Allah the Exalted is Seeing of all that we do, of good and evil, little and much, apparent and hidden, even the deeds of the hearts He knows? Yes; Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And We have certainly created man, and We know what his soul whispers to him﴾ [Qaf 16]. Be mindful: do not harbour in your heart anything that angers Allah; for when you do, Allah the Exalted will certainly know it, and nothing is hidden from Him: ﴿Indeed, I am Seeing of what you do﴾.

Ibn 'Uthaymin said, may Allah have mercy on him, in his commentary on the Qur'an:

Then He, glorified and exalted, said: ﴿And to Solomon [We subjected] the wind; its morning [journey] was a month's [travel] and its evening [journey] was a month's [travel].﴾ The author (al-Mufassir, i.e., Ibn Kathir / the author of the base text) said: "And We subjected to Solomon..." He supplied "And We subjected" because ﴿al-rih﴾ (the wind) is in the accusative case, so it requires a governing verb that completes the accusative. Here we supply what fits, which is "We subjected to him," as occurs in another verse: ﴿So We subjected to him the wind, flowing by his command gently, wherever he directed﴾ [Sad 36].

As for His saying ﴿li-Sulayman﴾ (to Solomon): who is Solomon? He is the son of David. Allah gave him prophethood and kingship, a great kingdom that is not fitting for anyone after him, because Allah subjected to him both mankind and the jinn.

As for His saying ﴿al-rih﴾ (the wind): it is the air, which Allah subjected to him, meaning He made it submissive, such that it moves by his command. He commands it and it turns north if he wishes to go north; he commands it and it turns south if he wishes to go south; he commands it to go east and it goes; he commands it to go west and it goes; he commands it to hasten and it hastens; he commands it to slow down and it slows down. ﴿It flows by his command.﴾

It may be said: this indicates that Solomon shared with Allah in creation, since no one can direct the air. Even if all of creation gathered to direct the air, they could not find a way to do so. Solomon could, so is he not able? He is able. Therefore it is not said that he is a partner of Allah, because the One who subjected the wind to him is Allah. For this reason we do not say that 'Isa (Jesus) was a partner with Allah in creation, when Allah said: ﴿And [mention] when you designed from clay [something] like the form of a bird, by My permission, and then you breathed into it and it became a bird by My permission﴾ [al-Ma'idah 110]. The power of these creatures over what they can do, which no other created being can do, was only by the command of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. They did not act independently in that; rather, Allah granted them a power, just as Allah bestows upon some servants an extraordinary power in memorization, or in understanding, or in the strength of hearing or sight, or of the body, or other than that.

So we say: the wind is the air, which was subjected to Solomon. He said: (﴿al-rih﴾ and the reading of the nominative case, with the supposition of subjection). The author's phrasing here, to indicate the second reading, is strange and is not what is customary from him. It would have been better for him to say: "And in a reading in the nominative case, on the supposition of subjection." This is the better formulation, because his saying "and the reading of the nominative" does not tell us whether this is a canonical (sab'i) reading or an irregular (shadhdh) one, since his customary usage is to say "and in a reading" for the canonical readings and "it was read" for the irregular ones. Here he says "and the reading of," and we do not know. In any case, the reading is canonical. In this reading ﴿And to Solomon the wind [blows], its morning [journey] is a month's [travel]...﴾ How do we parse ﴿al-rih﴾ according to this reading?

He says: it is a delayed subject (mubtada' mu'akhkhar), and the original sentence is "the subjection of the wind," so the modifier was deleted and the modified noun placed in its position. Ibn Malik says:

*And what follows the mudaf (the first term of an idafa) comes as a substitute for it in grammatical case when it is deleted.*

That is: for Solomon is the subjection of the wind. If someone said, "And to Solomon the wind," taking "the wind" as the subject without supposing a deletion, it would not be far-fetched, and the meaning of the wind being his would be what? That it is subjected to him, so he has control over it.

﴿Its morning [journey] is a month's [travel] and its evening [journey] is a month's [travel].﴾ (﴿Its morning﴾: its movement from the morning, meaning the 'ghudwa' (early morning), until midday; ﴿and its evening﴾: its movement from midday until sunset; ﴿a month's [travel]﴾: meaning its distance.) The wind which Allah subjected to him, when it carries him from morning until midday, travels a distance of a month by the pace of camels. On this basis it is swift.

﴿Its evening [journey] is a month's [travel]﴾: so he could go to a place a month's distance away and return to his land on the same day, because its morning journey is a month and its evening journey is a month. Nevertheless, Allah described it as violently blowing but not harmful: ﴿And to Solomon the wind [blowing] violently﴾ [al-Anbiya' 81], ﴿flowing by his command gently wherever he directed﴾ [Sad 36]. So it is swift, but not disturbing. But how does one fly on the wind? The scholars said: he would place an ordinary, customary carpet, and he and his retinue would sit on it, then he would command the wind and it would carry them on this carpet. And Allah, glorified and exalted, is capable of all things. Is it not customary for a person to sit on a carpet and rise up? The custom is that he remains on the ground, but Allah, glorified and exalted, is capable of all things. Can we say that the principle of flight in modern aircraft is based on this, or not?

* Students: It is not possible.
* The Shaykh: Why is it not possible?
* A student: (...) that which opposes the air.
* The Shaykh: Yes, it does not oppose it; but what is it that carries it and propels it?
* A student: (...).
* The Shaykh: No, a tremendous air. For this reason, if you were behind it while it moves, it lifts you; it is carried only by the air.
* The student: Certainly, Shaykh?
* The Shaykh: Yes, indeed, and it is modern and heavy, with people on it and luggage.
* The student: (...).
* The Shaykh: The same fans, and this thrust, there is strong air. But see now how it is controlled when it descends to the ground because of the air. When it descends to the ground, at its rear, near the tail, there is a piece of metal that reflects like this, so that it pushes back the air and the aircraft does not surge forward.
So the point is that the principle of flight is based on this, on the air generated by these engines.

He says: ﴿Its morning [journey] is a month's [travel] and its evening [journey] is a month's [travel]﴾. Is it at the speed of the aircraft or not?
* A student: (...).
* The Shaykh: No, less than the aircraft, because the aircraft travels a month's distance in less than a morning. By car? Faster than a car, without doubt. There remains this swift passage, which normally, if there is no shelter preventing the force of the wind, the wind would blow against the rider until he falls, would it not? Because we now understand that it is less than the aircraft and above the car. The car, as you see, if it is open, the wind blows against the person and disturbs him. But Allah, the Exalted, has made clear in another verse that this wind is gentle, with no disturbance and no unease.

Allah, the Exalted, also said, among what He bestowed upon Solomon: ﴿And We caused to flow for him a fount of copper﴾ (﴿We caused to flow﴾: We melted; ﴿for him a fount of copper﴾: meaning brass). This may be even more remarkable than what was given to David, because Allah said to David: ﴿We made iron pliable for him﴾. But this: He caused a fount of copper to flow for him, meaning He made a spring of brass gush forth that flows as water does, although it is brass. This is evidence of the perfect power of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, because it is well known that brass is a solid metal. Allah made it, for Solomon, a flowing spring as if it were water. For this reason He said: ﴿And We caused to flow for him a fount of copper﴾.

His saying ﴿a fount of copper﴾ refutes what has been said: that Solomon would melt brass so that it flowed. Just as lead, as you see now: when we melt lead it becomes fluid like mercury. We say: No, rather Allah says: ﴿We caused to flow for him a fount of copper﴾, making it a spring that gushes from below and flows. We know that Allah, glorified and exalted, is the Creator of things, solid and fluid, and that He is capable of making the solid fluid and the fluid solid. The flowing, gushing, running water: when Musa struck the sea with his staff it split, and each part was like a great mountain, a great mound. It was flowing water, and he struck it only once; the sea parted and became twelve paths, each path between it and the other like a mountain of water. This is beyond the natural order, because the Creator of things is capable of all things, glorified and exalted.

﴿And We caused to flow for him a fount of copper.﴾ The author, may Allah have mercy on him, said: (It flowed for him for three days and their nights, like the flow of water.) How? "It flowed for him for three days and their nights, like the flow of water." This estimate requires a textual basis (tawqif), meaning that Allah made it flow for him for only three days. We may say that Allah, glorified and exalted, caused a fount of copper to flow for him, which he could manage as he wished. This implies that this favor was continuous, wherever he wanted it, he found it. This is the closer view. We cannot limit it to three days except by an evidence from the Shari'ah, either from the Book or the Sunnah, and there is no specification in the Book nor likewise in the Sunnah. So it is better to keep it on its apparent meaning. The author said: (And the work of people until today from what was given to Solomon.) What is meant by "the work of people until today"? It means that the benefit people derive from this brass, and its melting until it becomes like water, is a trace of the work of Solomon. That is, brass has been melting since the time of Solomon until today. It has been said that brass did not used to melt at all, but in the time of Solomon it melted and then continued to melt permanently.

﴿And of the jinn were those who worked before him by the permission of his Lord.﴾ (﴿by permission﴾: by the command of his Lord.) ﴿Of the jinn those who worked﴾: (min) is partitive, and (al-jinn) is an unseen world hidden from the eyes; for this reason the word (jinn) was used. The root of this word is the letters jim, nun, which indicate concealment. From it is named (junnah), the shield with which a person conceals himself; and (jannah) is named for an orchard with many trees, because it covers whoever is in it, meaning it conceals him. (Jinnah) is also named for this reason, and (janin) (the fetus) is named because it is hidden. So this root, jim and nun, all indicates hiddenness and concealment. The jinn, then, are an unseen world; they are not apparent, though they may be seen. This world includes the righteous and those below that, the believers and the disbelievers, as in Surat al-Jinn. Do they eat and drink? They vomit and urinate, as was reported in a hadith from the Prophet (ﷺ). These jinn may appear before people and be seen, either in their own forms or in other forms, or in the shape of cats or animals, as in the authentic hadith prohibiting the killing of the (jinnan) snakes that are in houses, because some of them may be jinn.

Because some of them may be jinn, they may possess a person, meaning they enter into his body until he is like a garment for them, so they throw him down and harm him. Allah, the Exalted, alluded to this in His saying: ﴿Those who consume interest will not stand [on the Day of Resurrection] except as one stands who is being beaten by Satan into insanity﴾ [al-Baqarah 275], meaning like the one who is afflicted with madness that Satan has struck. This affliction, that is the jinn's affliction of humans, is denied only by the atheists (al-mulahidah), as Ibn al-Qayyim, may Allah have mercy on him, said in Zad al-Ma'ad: they could never reach this type of affliction, so they began to deny it, and they attribute all types of affliction to nerve and brain disorders and the like.

The jinn's affliction of humans is also known by observation, so none denies it except the obstinate. How is that? Because a person afflicted by it has been witnessed, and the jinn who afflicted him has been addressed in clear and explicit speech. This has occurred at the hands of the imams of Islam, such as Imam Ahmad and Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah and others, up to our own day. Once a man afflicted by a jinn was brought to Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah, may Allah have mercy on him, and he admonished the jinn that had afflicted him and advised it, and said: "Leave." It said: "I will not leave, I love him." It was a woman who had afflicted him; a woman afflicted the man, and she said: "I love him." Shaykh al-Islam said: "But he does not love you." She said: "I want to perform Hajj with him." How?! She would take him to Makkah. He said: "He does not want to perform Hajj with you." Then he admonished her, but she did not heed it. Then Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah struck her; he began striking her on the neck of this afflicted man, saying: until my hand grew tired from striking. She said: "I will leave out of honor for the Shaykh." He said: "Do not leave out of honor for me; leave out of obedience to Allah and His Messenger." So she left on condition that she would not return. The man regained consciousness, and when he did, he said: "What brought me to the presence of Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah?" He was told: "You did such and such." He said: "By Allah, I did not sense any of this; neither that I spoke to her nor that he struck me." This story was related by Ibn al-Qayyim in Zad al-Ma'ad from his Shaykh. Ibn al-Qayyim is trustworthy, and Shaykh al-Islam is likewise trustworthy, and similar things have been reported from Imam Ahmad.

So, in defining the jinn we say: they are an unseen world, hidden from humans, who may sometimes appear. Among them are the righteous and those below that, among them the deviators, and among them the Muslims. They eat, drink, urinate, and vomit. All of this is established in the Qur'an and the Sunnah.

He says: ﴿And of the jinn were those who worked before him﴾. ﴿Man﴾ (those who) means "the one who works before him," so it is a relative pronoun. What is its grammatical position? It may be in the nominative case as a delayed subject, with its predicate being ﴿of the jinn﴾. It may also be in the accusative case; that is: "And We subjected to him, of the jinn, those who work before him." Which is preferable? We have mentioned the rule that when there is a choice between supposing a deletion and not supposing one, not supposing one is preferable, because it is the original state: the original state is that nothing has been deleted from the sentence. On this basis we say: ﴿of the jinn﴾ is a prepositional phrase functioning as a delayed... (more precisely) a fronted predicate, and ﴿those who work﴾ is a delayed subject.

﴿Those who work before him﴾: before whose hands? Solomon's hands, meaning in front of him. But (﴿by permission﴾: by the command of ﴿his Lord﴾). Is the permission here cosmic or legislative? The permission is cosmic: by the cosmic permission of Allah, meaning Allah subjected the jinn to work before Solomon by His permission, by His cosmic command. It may also be said that it is a legislative permission, based on His saying: ﴿And whoever of them deviates from Our command, We will make him taste the punishment of the Blaze﴾.

He said: (﴿And whoever deviates﴾: turns away). It was said: swerves, that is, inclines. This is closer. From it comes "the sun deviated," meaning it declined from the middle of the sky.

﴿And whoever of them deviates﴾, meaning inclines (﴿from Our command﴾: to obey him), ﴿to him﴾, meaning to the jinn, to obey him, that is, to obey Solomon (﴿We will make him taste the punishment of the Blaze﴾: the Fire in the Hereafter). ﴿We will make him taste﴾: what caused it to be apocopated (jussive)? ﴿Man﴾ (whoever), because it is the answer to the condition, and the conditional verb is ﴿deviates﴾.

﴿We will make him taste the punishment of the Blaze﴾: meaning We will punish him with fire until he tastes its torment. Is this the fire of this world or the Hereafter? The author said: (In the Hereafter; it was said: in this world, by an angel striking him with a blaze that burns him). And Allah knows best whether his punishment in this world is through an angel, or whether Solomon was permitted to punish them with fire.

In any case, whoever of the jinn deviates from Allah's command to obey Solomon, he is punished with fire, either in this world or in the Hereafter. But if we say it is in this world, it is not necessary that the matter be as the author said: that it is an angel who strikes him with a whip of fire until it burns him. And Allah knows best.

* A student: (...) And in a reading?
* The Shaykh: The well-known one, by the text.
* The student: (...).
* The Shaykh: Both are canonical.
* The student: And the reading of the nominative?
* The Shaykh: Yes. I say: his expression is not customary. The usual phrasing is: "And in a reading in the nominative," then he explains its meaning.
* A student: We said that Allah's command to the jinn to obey Solomon and submit to him is a cosmic command...
* The Shaykh: Permitted.
* The student: (...).
* The Shaykh: Cosmic permission, yes.
* The student: Is not their obedience to Solomon and their subjection to him an act of worship of Allah for them?
