Then they become arrogant and obstinate and say: "What we worship them for are intercessors for us with Allah, to bring us near to Allah in closeness; we do not worship them for their own sakes." And sometimes they refuse to answer and stammer, because the truth is heavy upon them. If they say nothing, then say: "Allah." That is why He said: ﴿Say: Allah﴾, who provides for you from the heavens and the earth. If they refuse and say, "No, it is other than Him," but they cannot say that it is other than Him, then say: "Who?" Repeat the question to them a second time.

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Say: Allah.﴾ The author said: (If they do not say it); that is, if they do not say "Allah" (...).

* * *
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: His saying ﴿Say: Who provides for you from the heavens and the earth? Say: Allah﴾ indicates the obligation of debating and arguing with the polytheists. The obligation is drawn from His saying ﴿Say﴾, because the basic principle of a command is obligation.
* Among its benefits also: it is fitting to argue from what is clearest and most evident. The provision of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is a known matter (...). No one can claim that He sends down the rain or causes plants to grow. So in debate a person should argue from what is most manifest and clear, and this is the method of the Qur'an, as we have passed over in the principles of tafsir.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse also: it is permissible to answer the questioner regarding what is clear, the permissibility of answering the questioner about what he asked when the matter is clear, as shown by His saying ﴿Say: Allah﴾. An example in ordinary matters: I ask you, for instance, "Who brought such-and-such?" You hesitate, you stammer, either out of ignorance or obstinacy, so I say: "Was it not so-and-so who brought it?" and I thereby establish it for you. This, meaning answering the questioner, applies only to clear matters. As for matters that are not clear, the answer may be opposed and not be convincing. But in matters clear to the questioner, he may answer himself: what? If the opponent stammers and does not answer, then the matter stands. But if he answers, the matter is settled. Did the polytheists answer this question correctly elsewhere? Yes, in Surah Yunus: ﴿Say: Who provides for you from the heaven and the earth, or who owns hearing and sight, and who brings forth the living from the dead and brings forth the dead from the living, and who arranges the affair? They will say, "Allah."﴾ [Yunus 31].

* Among its benefits: it is permissible to confront an opponent with what is known in the science of debate as sabr and taqsim. Sabr means tracing out a thing, and taqsim means presenting the matter as a disjunction between this or that. Its example here is ﴿And indeed, we or you are surely upon guidance or in manifest error﴾. We traced the situation and found that the state of each of us does not go beyond two conditions: either guidance or error; and it is either for us or for you, with no third possibility. This is known by sabr and taqsim. Its parallel is His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Have you seen the one who disbelieved in Our verses and said, "I will surely be given wealth and children"?﴾ [Maryam 77]. This is his claim: ﴿I will surely be given wealth and children.﴾ Allah, Exalted, said: ﴿Has he attained knowledge of the unseen, or has he taken a covenant with the Most Merciful?﴾ [Maryam 78], meaning: does he know the unseen, that he will be given wealth and children? Or has Allah informed him of that and made a covenant with him? Is there a third division? The third division is lying; therefore He said: ﴿No!﴾, meaning that he has not attained the unseen and has not taken a covenant with the Most Merciful. Tell me, brother: what did I say, and what example did I give? (...) between this or that, until it becomes clear that it must be one of two matters?

* The student: The example?

* The Shaykh: Bring the verse as an example. We or you: now before us are two paths, guidance and error. Either we are upon guidance and you upon error, or we are upon error and you upon guidance. Likewise the verse in Surah Maryam is also very clear: ﴿Have you seen the one who disbelieved in Our verses and said, "I will surely be given wealth and children" (77)? Has he attained knowledge of the unseen, or has he taken a covenant with the Most Merciful?﴾ [Maryam 77, 78]. The point is that Allah said: has this one attained knowledge of the unseen and known that he will be given wealth and children? Or has he taken a covenant with the Most Merciful, meaning that Allah informed him and made a covenant with him that He would give him wealth and children? Because his claim is either a lie, or he has knowledge of the unseen, or a covenant from Allah. What did Allah say about this? ﴿No!﴾, meaning: neither this nor that. When this and that are negated, what remains? Lying remains: it is a false claim with no reality. Therefore He said: ﴿We will record what he says and extend for him an extension of punishment (79). And We will inherit from him what he says, and he will come to Us alone﴾ [Maryam 79, 80].

Similarly His saying: ﴿And they said, "The Fire will not touch us except for a few numbered days."﴾ [al-Baqarah 80]. What is the answer? ﴿Say: Have you taken a covenant with Allah, so Allah will not break His covenant? Or do you attribute to Allah what you do not know?﴾ If there were a covenant from Allah, then Allah does not break the covenant. ﴿Say: Have you taken a covenant with Allah, so Allah will not break His covenant? Or do you attribute to Allah what you do not know?﴾ The answer is that they attributed to Allah what they did not know.

So here, as I said: it is derived from the verse the argument by what is known among the scholars of debate, or the scholars of debate and disputation, by what? By sabr and taqsim; from His saying: ﴿And indeed, we or you are surely upon guidance﴾.

* Among its benefits: gentleness with the opponent and descending to his level to reach acknowledgment of the truth; from His saying: ﴿And indeed, we or you are surely upon guidance or in manifest error﴾; for this is the utmost descent to the opponent and gentleness with him so that he may acknowledge the truth. Look at something similar in His saying: ﴿Is Allah better, or what they associate?﴾ [al-Naml 59]. It is known that Allah is better; is that not so? But out of descending to their level, it is said to them: ﴿Is Allah better﴾, or your idols and gods?

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the exaggeration in descending to the opponent's level and bearing humiliation to reach the intended goal; from His saying: ﴿Say: You will not be asked about what we committed, and we will not be asked about what you do﴾ [Saba' 25]. A parallel to this descent to the opponent and bearing of humiliation is the conditions that took place between whom? Between the Prophet ﷺ and Quraysh at the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah, and the result and outcome was for whom? For the Messenger ﷺ.

And the result and outcome was for whom? For the Messenger ﷺ.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: a person is not asked about the deeds of others, and others are not asked about his deeds; from His saying: ﴿Say: You will not be asked about what we committed, and we will not be asked about what you do﴾ [Saba' 25].

A parallel to this is His saying: ﴿And no bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another. And if a heavily laden soul calls [another] to its load, nothing of it will be carried, even if he were a close relative﴾ [Fatir 18]: every person and his deeds.

Exception is made from this when the deed of another arises from your deed, such as when you are the one who guides to it or assists in it; then you bear of its burden in proportion to your deed. The Prophet ﷺ said: "Whoever establishes an evil practice in Islam, upon him is its burden and the burden of whoever acts upon it until the Day of Resurrection."[[Reported by Muslim (1017/69) from the hadith of Jarir ibn 'Abd Allah.]] Does this contradict the noble verse before us? * In this verse: the affirmation of resurrection and gathering; from His saying ﴿Say: Our Lord will bring us together; then He will judge between us﴾. This gathering is established by His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿The Day He will gather you for the Day of Gathering; that is the Day of Mutual Loss and Gain﴾ [al-Taghabun 9]. It also includes the gathering in this world in battle; from His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And what We sent down upon Our servant on the Day of Criterion, the day the two hosts met﴾ [al-Anfal 41].

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: a refutation of the Qadariyyah; from His saying ﴿Our Lord will bring us together﴾. It is known that our gathering is by our own doing, yet Allah attributed it to Himself, because He is the one who arranges it and decrees it, Glorified and Exalted is He. Or is it not so?

* The student: (...).

* The Shaykh: According to the second opinion, that it is in this world.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that the ruling of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is entirely truth and justice; from His saying ﴿Then He will judge between us in truth﴾, meaning with justice that contains no injustice or oppression.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the affirmation of what the People of the Sunnah and the Community have established: that when a divine name is transitive, faith in it is not complete except by believing in it as a name, in the attribute it contains, and in the effect and ruling it entails; from His saying ﴿He will judge between us﴾, and then He said after that: ﴿and He is the Judge﴾. This indicates that the transitive names of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, include the rulings and effects that follow from them.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the affirmation of two of Allah's names, ﴿the Judge, the Knowing﴾ [Saba' 26]. As previously explained in the commentary, al-Fattah includes many meanings: opening by victory, by knowledge, by understanding, by good intention, and other things; that is, it is a broad name.

* Among its benefits: the affirmation of knowledge for Allah, Glorified and Exalted; from His saying ﴿al-'Alim﴾, and that it is one of His established and inherent attributes, since He is described by it eternally and forever: ﴿In a Book; my Lord neither errs nor forgets﴾.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the warning to the debater with a certain consequence; from His saying ﴿Say: Our Lord will bring us together; then He will judge between us﴾ [Saba' 26], since this contains a warning, for we know that when Allah judges between them, the truth will be with whom? With the Muslims.

Thus we have understood the disjunction in His saying ﴿And indeed, we or you are surely upon guidance﴾ [Saba' 24]: that those upon guidance are who? They are the Muslims, and that those others are upon error. For if someone said: the verse contains a disjunction, "And indeed, we or you are surely upon guidance"; so we do not know which one is upon guidance. We say: those upon guidance are those whom Allah grants victory and supports against their enemies with truth.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 34, verse 27:

Then Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Say: "Show me those whom you have attached to Him as partners. No! Rather, He is Allah, the Almighty, the All-Wise."﴾ [Saba' 27] In this is what has preceded, that among the etiquettes of debate is adopting a challenge concerning what is known to be impossible for the opponent. For if you challenge him with a matter that is impossible, and his inability becomes apparent, the invalidity of his claim is made clear. Otherwise? Unlike when you challenge him with a matter he is able to do, for this would be harmful to you. Do not challenge the opponent except with a matter that renders him incapable and that he cannot achieve. Here He says: ﴿Show me those whom you have attached to Him as partners﴾, meaning: inform me, what have they created? What have they benefited? They have created nothing, benefited no one, and warded off no harm, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And those whom they invoke besides Allah create nothing, while they themselves are created. [They are] dead, not alive, and they do not perceive when they will be resurrected﴾ [an-Nahl 20-21]. And Ibrahim said to his father: ﴿O my father, why do you worship that which does not hear and does not see and cannot avail you at all?﴾ [Maryam 42].

And His saying: ﴿Show me those whom you have attached to Him as partners﴾.

* It is derived from it that shirk (association of partners with Allah) occurs in worship just as it occurs in creation and management; that is, shirk occurs in divinity (al-uluhiyyah) just as it occurs in lordship (ar-rububiyyah). The reason for this is that these polytheists did not associate partners in lordship, but they associated partners in divinity and worship.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: it is impossible for any person to show that these idols have any share in creation, provision, or management. This is derived from His saying: ﴿No!﴾ [Saba' 27], meaning: you cannot show me any of these idols [possessing such a share].

* Also among the benefits of the verse: the affirmation of two of Allah's names, namely al-'Aziz (the Almighty) and al-Hakim (the All-Wise), and what they include of attributes: might (al-'izzah) and wisdom (al-hikmah). The two names al-'Aziz and al-Hakim, and what they include of attributes: might, wisdom, and judgment (al-hukm). "Might," meaning al-Hakim... we have said: with what? [The answer is:] the possessor of judgment and wisdom.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the actions of Allah, glorified and exalted is He, cannot occur in folly, because of His saying: ﴿the All-Wise﴾ [Saba' 27]. Al-Hakim is the One in whose actions no folly occurs, and this is something known by necessity. Allah, Blessed and Exalted, said: ﴿And We did not create the heavens and the earth and what is between them in play﴾ [ad-Dukhan 38]; and He said: ﴿And We did not create the heaven and the earth and what is between them in vain. That is the assumption of those who disbelieve﴾ [Sad 27]; and Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Did you then think that We created you uselessly and that you would not be returned to Us?﴾ [al-Mu'minun 115].

* Also among its benefits: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, cannot be overcome, because of His saying: ﴿the Almighty﴾ [Saba' 27]. When you believe in this, and seek help in Him, Blessed and Exalted, you will know that you will not be defeated.

Allah the Mighty and Majestic said after this: ﴿And We have not sent you except﴾ [Saba' 28]..

We have mentioned that the author, may Allah have mercy on him, explained in his exegesis "the Mighty" as "the Dominant" (al-Ghalib), and "the Wise" [Saba' 27] as "in His management of His creation," and he also erred in his saying "without a partner in His dominion," because the context is not one of denying a partner in dominion; rather the context is one of denying a partner in worship, since these polytheists acknowledge that Allah has no partner in His dominion.

Allah the Exalted said: (﴿And We have not sent you except as a whole [kaffah]﴾ — a circumstantial phrase (hal) from "mankind," placed first for emphasis) ﴿to mankind﴾ [Saba' 28].

His saying: ﴿And We have not sent you except as a whole [kaffah]﴾ — this exception is what they call an "emptied exception" (istithna' mufrragh) from the most general of circumstances; meaning: We did not send you in any circumstance except this one, namely to mankind as a whole. ﴿Kaffah﴾ means "all together."

And His saying: ﴿We have sent you﴾ — "sending" (al-irsal) means the command to convey something. So when you send a person from among people to another person, it means you have commanded him to convey something to the one it is conveyed to. For this reason the scholars, in explaining the Messenger (rasul), said: he is one to whom a revealed law (shar') is revealed and who is commanded to convey it.

And His saying: ﴿except as a whole for mankind﴾ [Saba' 28] — "mankind" (al-nas) means human beings. They were called "nas" from their saying "anisa" when he moved and acted. On this basis, "nas" is a derived noun, not a fixed noun. They said: its origin is "al-unas," the original being "al-anas," but the hamza was dropped for lightness due to frequent usage. They said: similar to this is their saying "sharr" and "khayr," as when you say "this is khayr than this," meaning "akhyar than this," so the hamza was dropped for lightness due to frequent usage. They said: from this also is "Allah," whose origin is "al-Ilah," the hamza being dropped for lightness due to frequent usage. However, this last point is open to some consideration, because "al-Ilah" comes alongside "Allah," as you say: "He is Allah, the Ilah, the Great," and so on.

He says: (﴿except as a whole for mankind﴾ i.e., the disbelievers of Makkah). This is a deficiency on the part of the author, may Allah have mercy on him; for if we say that you were sent only to the disbelievers of Makkah, then others were not sent to, and this is a very great deficiency. How can the word "mankind" come in a context of messengership and we say its meaning is the disbelievers of Makkah? The correct view is that it means all of mankind: the disbelievers of Makkah, the disbelievers of Washington, the disbelievers of Moscow, the disbelievers of China, and all disbelievers. Is that not so? Until the Day of Resurrection, or only during his lifetime? Until the Day of Resurrection, for mankind in general.

﴿as a bringer of good tidings and a warner﴾ [Saba' 28].

(﴿A bringer of good tidings﴾ to the believers of Paradise, and ﴿a warner﴾ to the disbelievers of punishment.) ﴿Bashiran﴾ is also a circumstantial phrase (hal) from the kaf in His saying: ﴿We have sent you﴾. ﴿Bashir﴾ is on the pattern "fa'il" in the sense of "mufil" (causative), or "bashir" in the sense of "glad tidings" (bushra); and the pattern "fa'il" comes in the sense of "mufil," as we have previously stated many times.

As for his saying: (a bringer of good tidings of Paradise to the believers and a warner of Fire to the disbelievers), it should be said: (a bringer of good tidings of Paradise to the believers), as the author said: and a warner of punishment to the disobedient, so as to include warning against disbelief and warning against sins; meaning that even sins have punishments attached to them so that they deter a person from committing them. And Allah knows best.

﴿And We have not sent you except as a whole for mankind as a bringer of good tidings and a warner﴾ [Saba' 28] (...).

ﷺ; due to His saying: ﴿And We have not sent you﴾ [Saba' 28]. In it is evidence that Muhammad ﷺ is a commanded servant, not a commanding lord; due to His saying: ﴿And We have not sent you﴾ such-and-such. What did I say? (...).

* Also in it: the universality of the Prophet's ﷺ messengership.

According to the author's view: ﴿except as a whole for mankind﴾, it is like his ﷺ saying: "I was sent to mankind in general"[[Narrated by al-Bukhari (335) from the hadith of Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah.]]. Or we say: due to His saying: ﴿for mankind﴾, for "mankind" is one of the forms of generality. There is another opinion which says: ﴿kaffah﴾ means "restraining" (kaff), i.e., that it restrains people from shirk and disobedience; or ﴿except as a whole for mankind﴾ [Saba' 28], i.e., gathering them upon monotheism and sincerity. On this basis it is a circumstantial phrase from the kaf in His saying: ﴿We have sent you﴾, and the ta' in it, on this meaning, is for emphasis (mubalaghah), like His saying: ﴿Indeed, Abraham was a nation [ummah]﴾ [al-Nahl 120], meaning an imam; and as one says: "this is 'allamah," meaning "'allam"; but the ta' is for emphasis.

So we have two opinions regarding ﴿kaffah﴾, and what you mentioned in the explanation is for deficiency, not for negligence. Regarding ﴿kaffah﴾, what? There are two possibilities: that it is a circumstantial phrase from "mankind," placed before it; and that it is a circumstantial phrase from the kaf in ﴿We have sent you﴾. On this latter interpretation, ﴿kaffah﴾ means "restraining" (kaff), i.e., gathering, or "preventing," i.e., restraining the people. This opinion is clear in meaning, and the generality is derived, according to this opinion, from where? From His saying "mankind," for it is a general term.

* Also among the benefits of the verse: that the messengership of the Prophet ﷺ includes two things: good tidings and warning; good tidings to the obedient with reward, and warning to the disobedient with punishment.

* And among its benefits: an indication of the wisdom behind sending messengers, which is giving glad tidings and warning, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, We have revealed to you as We revealed to Noah and the prophets after him﴾ [al-Nisa' 163] up to His saying: ﴿messengers as bringers of good tidings and warners, so that mankind will have no argument against Allah after the messengers﴾ [al-Nisa' 165].

* And among its benefits: that most people do not know the wisdom behind the sending of the Messenger ﷺ, nor do they know that he is a messenger. Is that right? Most people. As for the first, it is clear that most people do not know the wisdom behind sending messengers; as for the second, there is room for consideration, because the message has reached most people and will reach all of mankind until the proof is established against them.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: that majority does not necessarily mean that the truth lies with it, for most people do not know, so they are in ignorance; since those who adhere to religions are few, and those who adhere to religions are people of knowledge and people of certainty.

* And among the benefits of the noble verse: the affirmation of causes. From where is this taken? From His saying: ﴿except as a whole for mankind﴾ according to the last, second meaning, that ﴿kaffah﴾ means "preventing," for the Messenger ﷺ is a cause, not an determinant; he is a cause of guidance, but you do not guide whom you love. And can it be derived from it the affirmation of Allah's voluntary acts?

* Student: (...).

* The Shaykh: From where? From His saying: ﴿And We have not sent you﴾, for this is one of the acts connected with His will, glorified and exalted be He.

* Also among the benefits of the verse: the establishment of proof upon creation, due to His saying: ﴿And We have not sent you except as a whole for mankind as a bringer of good tidings and a warner﴾ [Saba' 28], so that no one has an argument against Allah after the messengers. Can an excuse be derived from it for one to whom the message has not reached?

* Student: (...).

* The Shaykh: From where is it taken? From His saying: ﴿as a bringer of good tidings and a warner﴾ [Saba' 28], for one to whom the message has not reached has received neither good tidings nor warning.

So what is the ruling on one to whom the message has not reached? We say: he is in one of two situations. Either he is negligent in seeking the truth, and then he has no excuse, since he is negligent; or he is not negligent, such that nothing of the messages has reached him and no mention of the messages has occurred to his heart. Of such a person we say: he is judged in this world by the religion he is upon; as for the Hereafter, his matter is with Allah, and we do not testify anything concerning him.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 34, verses 29–36 (part 1 of 2):

﴿They say, "When is this promise, if you are truthful?"﴾ [Saba: 29] ﴿They say﴾ means the ones who denied the Messenger (ﷺ), who had been threatened with punishment and retribution. They say this defiantly, deeming it far-fetched, and denying it: ﴿When is this promise?﴾

﴿When﴾ is an interrogative particle, and what is meant by it is denial and defiance.

﴿The promise﴾ means the punishment you promised us. It is possible that ﴿When is this promise?﴾ refers to victory for you, because the common usage is that "wa'd" (promise) is for good and "wa'eed" (threat) is for evil. But it may be said that the threat against these disbelievers is a promise for the believers.

(﴿When is this promise?﴾ of punishment ﴿if you are truthful?﴾ in it) means: if you are truthful in what you say, that the punishment will befall us and that we will be punished. Truthfulness (sidq) is reporting what agrees with reality, and falsehood (kadhib) is reporting what contradicts reality. So if you say, "Zayd arrived in the town," and he had not arrived, then it is a falsehood because it contradicts reality. And if you say, "Zayd arrived in the town," and he had arrived, then it is truthful because it agrees with reality.

So they say: if you are truthful, when will this happen? This is like His saying regarding the Hour: ﴿And what would make you know? Perhaps the Hour is near. Those who do not believe in it seek to hasten it, while those who believe are apprehensive of it and know that it is the truth﴾ [ash-Shura: 17–18]. So the disbelievers seek to hasten the punishment as a denial of the messengers (peace be upon them).

Allah says: ﴿Then is it for Our punishment that they seek to hasten? Have you considered: if We let them enjoy for years, then there comes to them what they were promised, the enjoyment they had will not avail them﴾ [ash-Shu'ara: 204–207]. That is, what use will it be to them? However long their period lasts, the matter is limited and counted: ﴿If We let them enjoy for years, then there comes to them what they were promised, the enjoyment they had will not avail them﴾ [ash-Shu'ara: 205–207].

They make challenges, and at times they make challenges falsely. When they were informed of the resurrection, they said, defying the messengers (peace be upon them): ﴿Bring our forefathers, if you are truthful﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 25]. Was it said to them that their forefathers would come now, so that they might point to this? No. What was said to them is that their forefathers would be resurrected on the Day of Resurrection, but they were confusing the common people with such claims.

Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: (﴿Say, "For you is an appointed day from which you cannot remain behind an hour, nor can you precede it﴾ [Saba: 30]. It is with Him, and it is the Day of Resurrection.)

﴿For you is an appointed day﴾: the word ﴿mee'ad﴾ may be a noun of place or time (zarf), and it may be a mimi verbal noun (masdar mimi, a noun formed with the prefix mim from a verb). The meaning is that for you there is a promise that will occur on a day from which you cannot delay an hour, nor advance upon it. This is because Allah, the Mighty, in His perfect wisdom, has decreed for everything a specific term. Allah says: ﴿And everything with Him is by measure﴾ [ar-Ra'd: 8]. Everything is by measure with Allah and is determined by its term. So their hastening does not bring the punishment forward, nor does it delay it. When it comes, it does not come early or late. In this there is a clear answer as a threat to them, just as if you say to a person: "I have an appointment for you that will neither come early nor late," meaning: beware of this day.

The author's statement, "It is the Day of Resurrection," is undoubtedly possible, but there is another possibility: that it is the Day of Resurrection and also the day of their death, because on the day of their death they witness the punishment. Allah says: ﴿If you could see when the angels take the disbelievers, striking their faces and their backs, "Taste the punishment of burning. That is for what your hands have sent ahead, and indeed Allah is not ever unjust to the servants"﴾ [al-Anfal: 50–51].

So on this day they experience the punishment before the Day of Resurrection. ﴿If you could see when the wrongdoers are in the overwhelming of death, and the angels are extending their hands: "Release your souls. Today you are recompensed with the punishment of humiliation for what you used to say about Allah other than the truth, and you were arrogant toward His verses"﴾ [al-An'am: 93]. In Surat ad-Dukhan: ﴿So watch for the day when the sky will bring a visible smoke, covering the people. This is a painful punishment. Our Lord, remove from us the punishment; indeed, we are believers. How will there be for them the reminder?﴾ [ad-Dukhan: 10–13], up to His saying: ﴿Indeed, We will remove the punishment a little; indeed, you will return. The Day We will strike with the greatest assault; indeed, We will take retribution﴾ [ad-Dukhan: 15–16]. When did this happen? It happened at Badr, when their nobles and leaders were killed.

Allah says: (﴿And those who disbelieved said﴾ [Saba: 31], from the people of Makkah). The people of Makkah (...) are described as disbelievers before they became believers. But we should not restrict what Allah has stated in general terms. The correct reading is: ﴿And those who disbelieved said﴾, from the people of Makkah and others. What did they say? ﴿We will never believe in this Qur'an or in that which is before it﴾ [Saba: 31]. We seek refuge with Allah. They used ﴿lan﴾, which indicates emphatic negation, and they did not say, "We do not believe," but rather, "We will never believe," emphasizing the absence of their faith in the Qur'an in the future. ﴿We will never believe in this Qur'an﴾: the demonstrative ﴿this﴾ (hadha) is used for what is near, to belittle it, as in His saying: ﴿Is this the one who mentions your gods?﴾ [al-Anbiya': 36] and ﴿Is this the one whom Allah has sent as a messenger?﴾ [al-Furqan: 41].

﴿We will never believe in this Qur'an and not in that which is before it﴾ [Saba: 31]. I said that the demonstrative here is for what is near, to belittle it. As for ﴿al-Qur'an﴾, it is on the pattern (fu'lan). Is it in the sense of "maqru'" (that which is recited), or in the sense of "qari'" (the reciter), or is it a verbal noun meaning "gathering"? There is a difference among the scholars of Arabic on this, and the correct view is that it includes all these meanings. It is in the sense of "qari'," meaning "gathering," because it encompasses the previous books, and all the benefits found in them are present in it. It is also "maqru'," because people recite it and read it. It is also a gathering, because it comprises everything. The pattern fu'lan in the sense of a verbal noun exists in the Arabic language, such as "shukran," "kufran," and "nukran," and similar words. The word "Qur'an" here refers to the Book that Allah revealed to Muhammad (ﷺ), and it is a proper name for it: ﴿this Qur'an, and not that which is before it﴾. ﴿And not that which is before it﴾ means and we do not believe in what is before it, that is, (what preceded it, such as the Torah and the Gospel, which indicate the resurrection, by their denial of it). That is, we also do not believe in what is before it. According to the author's opinion, what is meant is what was before it, what preceded it, and not what comes after it. What preceded it, from (...), from which (...)?

This is what the author held.

It is possible that by His saying ﴿and not in that which is before it﴾ [Saba: 31] is meant what comes after it, that which He informed about, because what is before the thing (bayna yadayhi) means its future. As Allah says: ﴿He knows what is before them and what is behind them﴾ [al-Baqarah: 255]. Both meanings are correct. When a verse can bear two correct meanings that do not contradict each other, it must be understood as including both, because the Qur'an is comprehensive and broad. ﴿And not in that which is before it﴾ [Saba: 31] means: and not in what comes after it of what it informed about, or: ﴿and not in that which is before it﴾, meaning the books that preceded it, such as the Torah and the Gospel.

Allah says: ﴿And if you could see﴾. The author said: (O Muhammad, ﴿when the wrongdoers﴾, the disbelievers, ﴿are made to stand before their Lord﴾ [Saba: 31]).

﴿And if you could see﴾: this ﴿law﴾ (lau) is conditional. Its protasis (fi'l shartiha) is ﴿see﴾ (tara). Is it a jussive (jazima) or not? It is not jussive. Its apodosis is omitted, meaning: you would see a dreadful matter. The apodosis in this kind of construction is greater than its mention, because the mind goes in every direction in imagining it, in terms of horror and ugliness.

And ﴿lau﴾ comes in the Arabic language with several meanings: it may be conditional, as here, and it may be verbal (masdariyyah), as in His saying: ﴿They wish you would compromise, so they would compromise﴾ [al-Qalam: 9].

The author's statement, "O Muhammad": the author restricted the pronoun to the Messenger (ﷺ), although it may be meant for every addressee. That is: and if you, the addressee, could see the state of these people, you would see a dreadful matter.

His saying ﴿when the wrongdoers﴾ [Saba: 31]: ﴿idh﴾ means "time" or "when," so it is an adverb of time (zarf zaman). ﴿The wrongdoers﴾ is the subject (mubtada'), and ﴿are made to stand﴾ is its predicate (khabar).

By "the wrongdoers" the author means "the disbelievers." He restricted it to the disbelievers although wrongdoing is more general, because of the context: Allah says at the end of it: ﴿And We will put shackles on the necks of those who disbelieved﴾ [Saba: 33]. So "the wrongdoers" here means the disbelievers.

Is every disbeliever a wrongdoer?

* Students: (...).
* Shaykh: Is every wrongdoer a disbeliever? No. For this reason, when Allah said: ﴿And the disbelievers are the wrongdoers﴾ [al-Baqarah: 254], the scholars said: we praise Allah that He did not say, "And the wrongdoers are the disbelievers."

﴿And if you could see when the wrongdoers are made to stand before their Lord﴾ [Saba: 31]: that is, they are detained. The meaning of ''waqafa'' is ''habasa'' (to detain), and from this comes the term "waqf" (endowment) for property whose principal is held back and whose benefit is dedicated. So ﴿are made to stand﴾ means they are detained before Allah, the Mighty. His saying ﴿before their Lord﴾, rather than "before Allah," is because such a great act that indicates majesty fits with His lordship (rububiyyah), due to the perfection of His lordship, His perfect dominion, and His sovereignty. You will find these wrongdoers, who in this world had such arrogance, pride, and obstinacy, in the most humble state before the lordship of Allah, the Mighty.

﴿Before their Lord, they will return statements to one another﴾ [Saba: 31]. ﴿Return﴾ means "send back." On this reading it is transitive, because ''raja'a'' can be intransitive and can be transitive. When you say, "I returned from Makkah to Madinah," is this intransitive or transitive?

* Students: Intransitive.
* Shaykh: Intransitive?
* Students: Yes.
* Shaykh: "I returned from Makkah to Madinah" is intransitive. What do you say?
* Students: Yes.
* Shaykh: Intransitive, because it did not take an object. His saying, ﴿So if Allah returns you to a group of them﴾ [at-Tawbah: 83], is transitive.

Here He said: ﴿They return statements to one another﴾. Is it transitive or intransitive? Transitive, meaning: they send them back.

His saying ﴿they return statements to one another﴾: ﴿the statements﴾ here is vague and general, and then He explained it with His saying: ﴿Those who were oppressed will say﴾, and so on [Saba: 31].

The benefit of the vague then detailed is great, because when it is first stated generally and vaguely, the soul yearns to know what that thing is and to have it explained. Is that not so? When I read ﴿they return statements to one another﴾, what is your mind like? Your mind is eager to know what this statement is that they are exchanging. But if it had said: ﴿And if you could see when the wrongdoers are made to stand before their Lord﴾, ﴿Those who were oppressed will say﴾, as it came, it would not have had the same hold on the mind as it did when the statement was made vague and then clarified, or generalized and then detailed.

﴿They return statements to one another﴾: what do they say? (﴿Those who were oppressed﴾, the followers, ﴿will say to those who were arrogant﴾, the leaders: ﴿Were it not for you﴾, you who turned us away from faith, ﴿we would have been believers﴾ in the Prophet.)

Is ﴿Were it not for﴾ (lawla) conditional or not? It is conditional. It is described as a particle of prohibition due to existence, because its apodosis is prevented by the existence of its protasis. ''Lawla'' is used as a conditional, as here, and it is used for exhortation (tahdid), as in His saying: ﴿Why did they not bring four witnesses?﴾ [an-Nur: 13], and it is used for negation, as in His saying: ﴿Why was there not a town that believed so that its faith benefited it, except the people of Yunus?﴾ [Yunus: 98]. The meaning is: no town believed and its faith benefited it, except the people of Yunus when they believed.

Here He says: ﴿Were it not for you﴾. Ibn Malik (may Allah have mercy on him) says:

"After lawla, the omission of the predicate is usually obligatory..."

So here the subject is present, which is ﴿you﴾. Where is the predicate? It is omitted, and the author estimated it with his words: (you turned us away). How did he know it was this wording? From their saying: ﴿Did we turn you away from guidance?﴾ [Saba: 32]. So what we estimate here is not "Were it not for you being present," because "turning away" (sadd) is more specific than mere existence, and if we have a way to estimate the more specific, it is preferable to estimating the more general. This is why we say: when the reader says "In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate," he estimates the object of the sentence as "I recite," not "I begin," because "I begin" is general and "I recite" is specific. Here we could say: "Were it not for your being present," but since we find a more specific verb, namely the turning away indicated by His saying: ﴿Did we turn you away?﴾ [Saba: 32], it is necessary to estimate: "Were it not that you turned us away."

﴿Were it not for you, we would have been believers﴾ [Saba: 31]: this is the apodosis, and this is why it is joined with the lam: ﴿we would have been believers﴾. But believers in whom? He said: (in the Prophet).

The more correct view is that it is more general: that is, we would have been believers in all that the message of the Prophet (ﷺ) includes of faith in Allah, His angels, His books, His messengers, the Last Day, and other matters that must be believed in.

﴿Those who were arrogant said to those who were oppressed﴾ [Saba: 32]. They returned the statement: ﴿They return statements to one another﴾ [Saba: 31]. Did they return the statement? Where is the return? (...).

He says: ﴿Those who were arrogant said to those who were oppressed﴾. This is a reply to their statement. Look at: ﴿Did we turn you away from guidance after it had come to you?﴾ [Saba: 32]. The interrogative here means negation: that is, we will not turn you away from guidance after it has come to you. Rather, you are the ones who chose disbelief. Here the saying of Allah, the Mighty, is confirmed: ﴿When those who were followed disassociate themselves from those who followed﴾ [al-Baqarah: 166]. So here He says: ﴿Did we turn you away?﴾, meaning: we disown you, and we did not compel you to disbelieve; rather, you chose that yourselves.

His saying ﴿we turned you away﴾ means: we diverted you.

His saying ﴿from guidance after it had come to you﴾ [Saba: 32] is for the purpose of affirming the arrival of guidance and its clarity. This is an acknowledgment from these arrogant leaders that guidance had come, became manifest, and was clear: ﴿after it had come to you﴾. The author said in its explanation: (No). This indicates that the interrogative here is for negation. Whenever you find (no) after an interrogative, its meaning is that the author holds the interrogative here to be for negation.

(﴿Rather, you were criminals﴾ [Saba: 32], within yourselves). Look, I seek refuge with Allah. In this world you find the arrogant one approaching this weak one, calling him with complete gentleness, but in the Hereafter they curse one another and disown one another.

Look at the king of Ghassan, when news reached him that the Prophet (ﷺ) had boycotted Ka'b ibn Malik. What did he send to him? He sent him a gentle, tender letter and said: "We have heard that your companion has boycotted you, so come to us and we will console you." Look at the gentleness (...). But Ka'b (may Allah be pleased with him) was not deceived, because of his faith, and he feared he might be deceived in the future. So what did he do? He went to the oven and set this letter alight.

Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (4418), and Muslim (2769/53), from the hadith of Ka'b ibn Malik.

Likewise, everything about which you fear for yourself in the future, you must destroy. Do not say, "I will never be able to do this, and I can never be led astray by it." It is true that at the outset you may not be deceived, but Satan does his work. For this reason, you must destroy everything whose consequence you fear will be dire for you.

The upshot is that these (leaders) in the Hereafter will not show affection, kindness, or mercy to these followers. He says: ﴿Nay, but you were criminals﴾ [Saba' 32], and criminality (ijram) is the sin that is not forgiven.

He says: ﴿Nay, but you were criminals﴾. ﴿And those who were deemed weak will say to those who were arrogant: Nay, but (your) scheming by night and day...﴾ [Saba' 33]. Look: it is a rejection (idrab) of their rejection (idrab), (...) He says: ﴿Nay, but you were criminals﴾ — a rejection of what? Of their saying: ﴿Had it not been for you, we would have been believers﴾ [Saba' 31]. Then these (followers) rejected them; that is, they answered them with another rejection.

They said: (﴿Nay, but scheming of night and day﴾ [Saba' 33], meaning: scheming that you carried out against us during them.) ﴿The scheming of the night and the day﴾: here "scheming" (makr) is attributed to "night" by way of the implied preposition (fi, "in"). This is because the construct (idafah) may be understood as implying (min, "of/from"), or (al-lam, "belonging to"), or (fi, "in"). If the first term is of the same kind as the second, that is, the second is the genus of the first, it is with the implied (min). If the second is a time/place container for the first, it is with the implied (fi). Otherwise it is with the implied (al-lam).

"Ring of iron" is with the implied (min), correct? "Garment of silk" is with the implied (min). "Scheming of the night" is with the implied (fi); that is, scheming in the night.

What is scheming (makr)? They defined makr as: reaching a goal through hidden means in order to bring harm upon the one who opposes you. This is makr; that is, against the one who confronts you, or, if you wish, against the adversary. Define for me what (...)? ﴿The scheming of the night﴾: makr is attributed here to the night because it is a time container.

He says: "We have more wealth and children, and even if we are returned to God, we will not be punished." This is according to one of the two possibilities. The second possibility is that their saying ﴿and we will not be punished﴾ [Saba' 35] means that we will not be resurrected and punished.

Then the Exalted says: ﴿Say: Indeed my Lord extends provision to whom He wills and restricts (it)﴾ [Saba' 36], to the end.

In this is the affirmation of God's will, from His saying ﴿to whom He wills﴾, and the affirmation of voluntary acts, from His saying ﴿extends﴾ and ﴿restricts﴾.

* Also in it: abundance of wealth and children does not indicate divine approval; rather it follows what? The will of God.

* Among its lessons: the great and profound wisdom in people's differing in abundance and scarcity of provision. Were it not so, the interests of creation would not be established. If people were equal in wealth, would some serve others? No, and some would not carry out the interests of others. Consider His saying: ﴿Is it they who apportion the mercy of your Lord? We have apportioned among them their livelihood in the worldly life and raised some of them above others in degrees﴾ [Zukhruf 32]. Why? ﴿So that some of them may take others in service﴾ [Zukhruf 32]. Without this variation in the extension and abundance of provision, this great benefit—the subjugation of people to one another—would not have been achieved.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: most people are ignorant of the wisdom of God, the Mighty and Majestic, in His acts; this is因为 His saying: ﴿but most people do not know﴾.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 34, verses 29–36 (part 1 of 2):

﴿They say, "When is this promise, if you are truthful?"﴾ [Saba: 29] ﴿They say﴾ means the ones who denied the Messenger (ﷺ), who had been threatened with punishment and retribution. They say this defiantly, deeming it far-fetched, and denying it: ﴿When is this promise?﴾

﴿When﴾ is an interrogative particle, and what is meant by it is denial and defiance.

﴿The promise﴾ means the punishment you promised us. It is possible that ﴿When is this promise?﴾ refers to victory for you, because the common usage is that "wa'd" (promise) is for good and "wa'eed" (threat) is for evil. But it may be said that the threat against these disbelievers is a promise for the believers.

(﴿When is this promise?﴾ of punishment ﴿if you are truthful?﴾ in it) means: if you are truthful in what you say, that the punishment will befall us and that we will be punished. Truthfulness (sidq) is reporting what agrees with reality, and falsehood (kadhib) is reporting what contradicts reality. So if you say, "Zayd arrived in the town," and he had not arrived, then it is a falsehood because it contradicts reality. And if you say, "Zayd arrived in the town," and he had arrived, then it is truthful because it agrees with reality.

So they say: if you are truthful, when will this happen? This is like His saying regarding the Hour: ﴿And what would make you know? Perhaps the Hour is near. Those who do not believe in it seek to hasten it, while those who believe are apprehensive of it and know that it is the truth﴾ [ash-Shura: 17–18]. So the disbelievers seek to hasten the punishment as a denial of the messengers (peace be upon them).

Allah says: ﴿Then is it for Our punishment that they seek to hasten? Have you considered: if We let them enjoy for years, then there comes to them what they were promised, the enjoyment they had will not avail them﴾ [ash-Shu'ara: 204–207]. That is, what use will it be to them? However long their period lasts, the matter is limited and counted: ﴿If We let them enjoy for years, then there comes to them what they were promised, the enjoyment they had will not avail them﴾ [ash-Shu'ara: 205–207].

They make challenges, and at times they make challenges falsely. When they were informed of the resurrection, they said, defying the messengers (peace be upon them): ﴿Bring our forefathers, if you are truthful﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 25]. Was it said to them that their forefathers would come now, so that they might point to this? No. What was said to them is that their forefathers would be resurrected on the Day of Resurrection, but they were confusing the common people with such claims.

Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: (﴿Say, "For you is an appointed day from which you cannot remain behind an hour, nor can you precede it﴾ [Saba: 30]. It is with Him, and it is the Day of Resurrection.)

﴿For you is an appointed day﴾: the word ﴿mee'ad﴾ may be a noun of place or time (zarf), and it may be a mimi verbal noun (masdar mimi, a noun formed with the prefix mim from a verb). The meaning is that for you there is a promise that will occur on a day from which you cannot delay an hour, nor advance upon it. This is because Allah, the Mighty, in His perfect wisdom, has decreed for everything a specific term. Allah says: ﴿And everything with Him is by measure﴾ [ar-Ra'd: 8]. Everything is by measure with Allah and is determined by its term. So their hastening does not bring the punishment forward, nor does it delay it. When it comes, it does not come early or late. In this there is a clear answer as a threat to them, just as if you say to a person: "I have an appointment for you that will neither come early nor late," meaning: beware of this day.

The author's statement, "It is the Day of Resurrection," is undoubtedly possible, but there is another possibility: that it is the Day of Resurrection and also the day of their death, because on the day of their death they witness the punishment. Allah says: ﴿If you could see when the angels take the disbelievers, striking their faces and their backs, "Taste the punishment of burning. That is for what your hands have sent ahead, and indeed Allah is not ever unjust to the servants"﴾ [al-Anfal: 50–51].

So on this day they experience the punishment before the Day of Resurrection. ﴿If you could see when the wrongdoers are in the overwhelming of death, and the angels are extending their hands: "Release your souls. Today you are recompensed with the punishment of humiliation for what you used to say about Allah other than the truth, and you were arrogant toward His verses"﴾ [al-An'am: 93]. In Surat ad-Dukhan: ﴿So watch for the day when the sky will bring a visible smoke, covering the people. This is a painful punishment. Our Lord, remove from us the punishment; indeed, we are believers. How will there be for them the reminder?﴾ [ad-Dukhan: 10–13], up to His saying: ﴿Indeed, We will remove the punishment a little; indeed, you will return. The Day We will strike with the greatest assault; indeed, We will take retribution﴾ [ad-Dukhan: 15–16]. When did this happen? It happened at Badr, when their nobles and leaders were killed.

Allah says: (﴿And those who disbelieved said﴾ [Saba: 31], from the people of Makkah). The people of Makkah (...) are described as disbelievers before they became believers. But we should not restrict what Allah has stated in general terms. The correct reading is: ﴿And those who disbelieved said﴾, from the people of Makkah and others. What did they say? ﴿We will never believe in this Qur'an or in that which is before it﴾ [Saba: 31]. We seek refuge with Allah. They used ﴿lan﴾, which indicates emphatic negation, and they did not say, "We do not believe," but rather, "We will never believe," emphasizing the absence of their faith in the Qur'an in the future. ﴿We will never believe in this Qur'an﴾: the demonstrative ﴿this﴾ (hadha) is used for what is near, to belittle it, as in His saying: ﴿Is this the one who mentions your gods?﴾ [al-Anbiya': 36] and ﴿Is this the one whom Allah has sent as a messenger?﴾ [al-Furqan: 41].

﴿We will never believe in this Qur'an and not in that which is before it﴾ [Saba: 31]. I said that the demonstrative here is for what is near, to belittle it. As for ﴿al-Qur'an﴾, it is on the pattern (fu'lan). Is it in the sense of "maqru'" (that which is recited), or in the sense of "qari'" (the reciter), or is it a verbal noun meaning "gathering"? There is a difference among the scholars of Arabic on this, and the correct view is that it includes all these meanings. It is in the sense of "qari'," meaning "gathering," because it encompasses the previous books, and all the benefits found in them are present in it. It is also "maqru'," because people recite it and read it. It is also a gathering, because it comprises everything. The pattern fu'lan in the sense of a verbal noun exists in the Arabic language, such as "shukran," "kufran," and "nukran," and similar words. The word "Qur'an" here refers to the Book that Allah revealed to Muhammad (ﷺ), and it is a proper name for it: ﴿this Qur'an, and not that which is before it﴾. ﴿And not that which is before it﴾ means and we do not believe in what is before it, that is, (what preceded it, such as the Torah and the Gospel, which indicate the resurrection, by their denial of it). That is, we also do not believe in what is before it. According to the author's opinion, what is meant is what was before it, what preceded it, and not what comes after it. What preceded it, from (...), from which (...)?

This is what the author held.

It is possible that by His saying ﴿and not in that which is before it﴾ [Saba: 31] is meant what comes after it, that which He informed about, because what is before the thing (bayna yadayhi) means its future. As Allah says: ﴿He knows what is before them and what is behind them﴾ [al-Baqarah: 255]. Both meanings are correct. When a verse can bear two correct meanings that do not contradict each other, it must be understood as including both, because the Qur'an is comprehensive and broad. ﴿And not in that which is before it﴾ [Saba: 31] means: and not in what comes after it of what it informed about, or: ﴿and not in that which is before it﴾, meaning the books that preceded it, such as the Torah and the Gospel.

Allah says: ﴿And if you could see﴾. The author said: (O Muhammad, ﴿when the wrongdoers﴾, the disbelievers, ﴿are made to stand before their Lord﴾ [Saba: 31]).

﴿And if you could see﴾: this ﴿law﴾ (lau) is conditional. Its protasis (fi'l shartiha) is ﴿see﴾ (tara). Is it a jussive (jazima) or not? It is not jussive. Its apodosis is omitted, meaning: you would see a dreadful matter. The apodosis in this kind of construction is greater than its mention, because the mind goes in every direction in imagining it, in terms of horror and ugliness.

And ﴿lau﴾ comes in the Arabic language with several meanings: it may be conditional, as here, and it may be verbal (masdariyyah), as in His saying: ﴿They wish you would compromise, so they would compromise﴾ [al-Qalam: 9].

The author's statement, "O Muhammad": the author restricted the pronoun to the Messenger (ﷺ), although it may be meant for every addressee. That is: and if you, the addressee, could see the state of these people, you would see a dreadful matter.

His saying ﴿when the wrongdoers﴾ [Saba: 31]: ﴿idh﴾ means "time" or "when," so it is an adverb of time (zarf zaman). ﴿The wrongdoers﴾ is the subject (mubtada'), and ﴿are made to stand﴾ is its predicate (khabar).

By "the wrongdoers" the author means "the disbelievers." He restricted it to the disbelievers although wrongdoing is more general, because of the context: Allah says at the end of it: ﴿And We will put shackles on the necks of those who disbelieved﴾ [Saba: 33]. So "the wrongdoers" here means the disbelievers.

Is every disbeliever a wrongdoer?

* Students: (...).
* Shaykh: Is every wrongdoer a disbeliever? No. For this reason, when Allah said: ﴿And the disbelievers are the wrongdoers﴾ [al-Baqarah: 254], the scholars said: we praise Allah that He did not say, "And the wrongdoers are the disbelievers."

﴿And if you could see when the wrongdoers are made to stand before their Lord﴾ [Saba: 31]: that is, they are detained. The meaning of ''waqafa'' is ''habasa'' (to detain), and from this comes the term "waqf" (endowment) for property whose principal is held back and whose benefit is dedicated. So ﴿are made to stand﴾ means they are detained before Allah, the Mighty. His saying ﴿before their Lord﴾, rather than "before Allah," is because such a great act that indicates majesty fits with His lordship (rububiyyah), due to the perfection of His lordship, His perfect dominion, and His sovereignty. You will find these wrongdoers, who in this world had such arrogance, pride, and obstinacy, in the most humble state before the lordship of Allah, the Mighty.

﴿Before their Lord, they will return statements to one another﴾ [Saba: 31]. ﴿Return﴾ means "send back." On this reading it is transitive, because ''raja'a'' can be intransitive and can be transitive. When you say, "I returned from Makkah to Madinah," is this intransitive or transitive?

* Students: Intransitive.
* Shaykh: Intransitive?
* Students: Yes.
* Shaykh: "I returned from Makkah to Madinah" is intransitive. What do you say?
* Students: Yes.
* Shaykh: Intransitive, because it did not take an object. His saying, ﴿So if Allah returns you to a group of them﴾ [at-Tawbah: 83], is transitive.

Here He said: ﴿They return statements to one another﴾. Is it transitive or intransitive? Transitive, meaning: they send them back.

His saying ﴿they return statements to one another﴾: ﴿the statements﴾ here is vague and general, and then He explained it with His saying: ﴿Those who were oppressed will say﴾, and so on [Saba: 31].

The benefit of the vague then detailed is great, because when it is first stated generally and vaguely, the soul yearns to know what that thing is and to have it explained. Is that not so? When I read ﴿they return statements to one another﴾, what is your mind like? Your mind is eager to know what this statement is that they are exchanging. But if it had said: ﴿And if you could see when the wrongdoers are made to stand before their Lord﴾, ﴿Those who were oppressed will say﴾, as it came, it would not have had the same hold on the mind as it did when the statement was made vague and then clarified, or generalized and then detailed.

﴿They return statements to one another﴾: what do they say? (﴿Those who were oppressed﴾, the followers, ﴿will say to those who were arrogant﴾, the leaders: ﴿Were it not for you﴾, you who turned us away from faith, ﴿we would have been believers﴾ in the Prophet.)
